docs.title: 13.1. Installing Node.js
docs.text:
[Node.js] can be downloaded from nodejs.org: choose version LTS (long-term support) 24, or version 22 starting with 22.22: this is required by [React Router] 8 ([Vite] 8 only requires 20.19). The [Windows] installer also installs [npm]. Verify the installation in a console:

node --version
npm --version

To run multiple versions of [Node.js] on the same machine, you can use [nvm-windows] (under [Windows]) or [nvm] (under [Linux] and [macOS]).

The examples and case study do not require the installation of any tools overall: [Vite], [TypeScript] (and, for the server, the [nest] tool) are part of each project’s dependencies, installed by [npm install]. The scripts in [package.json] ([npm start], [npm run build]) locate them in the [node_modules] folder. To create a new project yourself, you can use [npm create vite@latest mon-projet -- --template react-ts] without installing anything.

docs.title: 13.2. Installing Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
[Visual Studio Code] can be downloaded from code.visualstudio.com. It includes JSX and [TypeScript] by default: code completion, type checking as you type, navigating from a component ([<ChampSaisie>]) to its definition, and renaming a prop throughout the project. No extension is required; you can add ESLint (along with the rules [eslint-plugin-react-hooks], which flag missing dependencies in [useEffect] and conditionally called hooks) from the Extensions panel (Ctrl-Shift-X).

Open a project via the File / Open Folder menu (the [exemples-react] folder, for example), and open a console within it via the Terminal / New Terminal menu.

docs.title: 13.3. The React Developer Tools Extension
docs.text:
The React Developer Tools extension can be installed from the [Chrome], [Edge], or [Firefox] extension store. It adds two tabs to the browser’s developer tools (F12):

  • “Components”: the page’s component tree (not the HTML tag tree), and, for each component, its props, state, and hooks ([useState], [useContext]...) along with their values; the component that rendered it;
  • “Profiler”: a logger that shows which components were re-rendered with each update, why (“props changed,” “hook 2 changed,” etc.), and how long it took.

You can modify a prop or state there and watch the page update: an excellent way to understand when and why a component is re-rendered. The “Highlight updates when components render” option makes each re-rendered component flash on the page.

docs.title: 13.4. Installing MySQL with Laragon
docs.text:
The JSON server requires [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]). [Laragon] (laragon.org) installs one under [Windows], ready to use, along with the [HeidiSQL] administration tool. After installation:

  • the “Start All” button launches the [MySQL] server on port 3306;
  • the user [root] has no password: these are the default values from the server’s [.env.example] file;
  • In [HeidiSQL] (the “Database” button), the File / Run SQL File menu item runs the [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] script.

In [Linux] or [macOS], install [MySQL] or [MariaDB] using the system’s package manager, and run the script using the command-line client: [mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql].

docs.title: 13.5. Installing curl
docs.text:
[curl] is included with [Windows] versions 10 and 11, [macOS], and most distributions of [Linux]. Check its version:

curl --version

The option [--json], used in this document, has been available since version 7.82 (2022). If you are using an older version, replace [--json @fichier] with [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier], or install a recent version starting with curl.se.

For [PowerShell], you should enter [curl.exe], not [curl]: In [PowerShell], [curl] is an alias for another command ([Invoke-WebRequest]), which does not include the options from [curl]. The command prompt ([cmd]) does not have this issue.

docs.title: 5.1. Example 19: Asynchronous Processing
docs.text: Many things happen “later”: timer ticks, keystrokes, server responses. [Angular] relies on the [RxJS] library and its observables for this. [React] does not have its own dedicated asynchronous tools: we combine state, effects, and their cleanup, which we store in hooks; and, starting with [React] 19, [use()] and [<Suspense>] allow us to wait for a promise.

docs.title: 5.1.1. A countdown
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 19-asynchronous/src/hooks/useCompteARebours.ts - a timer in a hook
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Starting at 0, one value per second. The timer stops when the
// count reaches 0... or when the component disappears (cleanup).
// =========================================================================

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

export function useCompteARebours(depart: number): number {
  const [reste, setReste] = useState(depart);

   // [reste > 0]: the effect is restarted when this condition changes—so
   // once, when the count reaches 0 (the timer is then stopped)
  const actif = reste > 0;
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!actif) return;
    const minuterie = setInterval(() => setReste((r) => r - 1), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(minuterie);
  }, [actif]);

  return reste;
}
  • line 11: the counter;
  • line 15: the counter;
  • lines 16–20: the effect depends solely on [actif]: it is executed at startup (the timer starts), then only once more, when the count reaches 0; its cleanup then stops the timer, and the new execution does nothing. [setReste((r) => r - 1)] uses the “function” form of the update: the timer was created once and for all and does not see the new values of [reste]; the function, on the other hand, receives the current value.

docs.title: 5.1.2. Anti-bounce
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 19-asynchronous/src/hooks/useValeurDifferee.ts - "debounce"
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Returns the received value... but only when it has not changed
// for a delay of milliseconds. For a search as you type: we
// wait for the user to pause before querying the server,
// instead of sending a request for every keystroke.
// The principle: each new value restarts the effect, and clearing
// resets the timer for the previous value.
// =========================================================================

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

export function useValeurDifferee<T>(valeur: T, delai: number): T {
  const [differee, setDifferee] = useState(valeur);

  useEffect(() => {
    const minuterie = setTimeout(() => setDifferee(valeur), delai);
    return () => clearTimeout(minuterie); // A keystroke before the end: the timer is canceled
  }, [valeur, delai]);

  return differee;
}

For “search-as-you-type” functionality, we wait for the user to pause before querying the server, rather than sending a request with every keystroke: this is anti-bounce ([debounce]). The hook returns the received value... but only when it hasn’t changed for [delai] milliseconds:

  • lines 17–20: each new value restarts the effect, which sets a timer; and the cleanup from the previous execution (ANNULE) resets the timer for the previous value. Therefore, only the last value, followed by a pause, reaches [setDifferee].

The hook is generic ([<T>]): it works for values of any type.

docs.title: 5.1.3. The page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 19-asynchronous/src/App.tsx - timers, search as you type, use()
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Many things happen “later”: timer ticks,
// keyboard keystrokes, a server’s response. React doesn’t have a tool
// specific to asynchronous operations (Angular uses the RxJS library): we combine
// state, effects, and their cleanup, organized into hooks (hooks/),
// and, since React 19, use() + <Suspense> to wait for a promise.
// =========================================================================

import { Suspense, use, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useCompteARebours } from './hooks/useCompteARebours';
import { useValeurDifferee } from './hooks/useValeurDifferee';

const MEDECINS = ['Marie PELISSIER', 'Paul TATOU', 'Sophie DUPONT', 'Jacques DURAND', 'Martine PELLETIER'];

// a simulated “server”: the response arrives after a random delay
function rechercher(texte: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const trouves = MEDECINS.filter((m) => m.toLowerCase().includes(texte));
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(trouves), 200 + Math.random() * 600));
}

// 3. A promise, created UNE times (outside the component): it resolves at
// the end of one second
const promesseMessage = new Promise<string>((resolve) =>
  setTimeout(() => resolve('trois (une seconde plus tard)'), 1000),
);

// use(promise): the value of the promise. As long as it is not
// resolved, the component “suspends” its display: the nearest <Suspense>
// displays its fallback content instead
function Message({ promesse }: { promesse: Promise<string> }) {
  const valeur = use(promesse);
  return <p className="mb-0">reçu : {valeur}</p>;
}

export default function App() {
  const [journal, setJournal] = useState<string[]>([]);
  const tracer = (message: string) => setJournal((j) => [...j, `${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`]);

   // 1. A countdown: a custom hook
  const rebours = useCompteARebours(20);

   // 2. a search as you type
  const [saisie, setSaisie] = useState('');
  const texte = useValeurDifferee(saisie.trim().toLowerCase(), 400); // after 400 ms of inactivity
  const [resultats, setResultats] = useState<string[]>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (texte.length < 2) {
      return; // no search (and no cleanup)
    }
     // "out of date": a response arrives APRÈS indicating that another one has been launched
     // search should be ignored (otherwise a slow response from an old
     // search would overwrite the one from the new one)
    let perimee = false;
    tracer(`recherche envoyée : « ${texte} »`);
    rechercher(texte).then((trouves) => {
      if (perimee) {
        tracer(`réponse ignorée (périmée) : « ${texte} »`);
        return;
      }
      setResultats(trouves);
    });
     // cleanup: executed when text changes (new search) or upon deletion
    return () => {
      perimee = true;
    };
  }, [texte]);

   // fewer than two letters: no results, regardless of those from the
   // last search (a calculated value, not an additional state)
  const affiches = texte.length < 2 ? [] : resultats;

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 720 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 19 - l'asynchrone</h1>

      <div className="card p-3 mb-3">
        <h2 className="h6">Un compte à rebours (setInterval dans un hook)</h2>
        <p className="display-6 mb-0">{rebours}</p>
      </div>

      <div className="card p-3 mb-3">
        <h2 className="h6">Une recherche au fil de la frappe (anti-rebond, réponses périmées)</h2>
        <input className="form-control mb-2" placeholder="au moins deux lettres : pel, dur..." value={saisie}
               onChange={(e) => setSaisie(e.target.value)} />
        <ul className="mb-0">
          {affiches.map((r) => <li key={r}>{r}</li>)}
          {affiches.length === 0 && <li className="text-muted">aucun résultat</li>}
        </ul>
      </div>

      <div className="card p-3 mb-3">
        <h2 className="h6">Attendre une promesse (use et Suspense)</h2>
        <Suspense fallback={<p className="text-muted mb-0">en attente...</p>}>
          <Message promesse={promesseMessage} />
        </Suspense>
      </div>

      <h2 className="h6">Journal</h2>
      <ol className="small">
        {journal.map((ligne, i) => <li key={i}>{ligne}</li>)}
      </ol>
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 18–21: a simulated “server”: the response arrives after a random delay of 200 to 800 ms;
  • lines 25–27: a promise, created UNE times (outside the component), resolved after one second;
  • lines 32–35: [use(promesse)] returns the value of a promise. As long as it is not resolved, the component “suspends” its display: the nearest [<Suspense>] (line 96) displays its placeholder content ([fallback]). When the promise is resolved, [React] recalls the component, and [use] returns the value. The promise must be created by the component (HORS) or by a library that caches it: a promise created during rendering would be recreated with each call, and the wait would never end;
  • line 42: the custom hook;
  • line 46: the search text, after 400 ms without keystrokes;
  • lines 49–69: the search, restarted when the (cached) text changes:
    • the problem with stale responses: you type “pel,” pause, and the search starts; you type “du,” pause, and a second search starts. If the response to “pel” arrives as APRÈS before the one for “du” (network delays are unpredictable), it would overwrite the correct results;
    • The solution (lines 56–67): a variable specific to the execution of the effect, CHAQUE, which is reset to [true] when the text changes. Any response that arrives afterward is ignored;
  • line 73: fewer than two letters: no results, regardless of the results of the last search. This is a calculated value, not an additional state.

You type “pel,” wait a moment, then type “du”; the response to “pel” arrives too late and is ignored:

Writing your own query handling code (in progress, successful, error, expired, already in cache, etc.) is tedious. To communicate with a server, in practice you use a library that handles this: in Example 24, this will be [TanStack Query].

docs.title: 5.2. Example 20: A Shared State
docs.text: Example 18 shows how to write a store by hand. The [Zustand] library does the same thing in just a few lines, and it is one of the most widely used libraries for managing shared state in a [React] application (along with [Redux Toolkit], which is more comprehensive but also more resource-intensive).

docs.title: 5.2.1. The shopping cart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 20-state-sharing/src/stores/panier.ts - a ÉTAT PARTAGÉ, with state
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A “store” is a state that contains HORS components, in UN a single
// instance, shared by everyone who reads it. Example 18 wrote
// one by hand (useSyncExternalStore); the Zustand library does the
// same thing in just a few lines:
//
//      const usePanier = create<Panier>()((set, get) => ({ ...state and actions... }));
//
// `create` returns a `HOOK`. A component reads what it needs from it using a
// "selector": usePanier((p) => p.articles). It is called only if CE
// part of the state changes. Typical structure:
//    - ÉTAT: data (items);
//    - ACTIONS: functions, which are the only ones that modify the state via set();
//    - calculated values: functions (or selectors).
// The store exists as long as the application exists: it survives the removal of a
// component... but not a page reload (F5), which restarts
// the application. (Context + useReducer can do the same job;
// a store has the advantage of being readable by HORS components as well.)
// =========================================================================

import { create } from 'zustand';

export interface Article {
  libelle: string;
  prix: number;
}

interface Panier {
  articles: Article[];
  ajouter: (article: Article) => void;
  vider: () => void;
}

export const usePanier = create<Panier>()((set) => ({
  articles: [],
   // set(function): receives the current state, returns what changes (the rest is preserved)
  ajouter: (article) => set((p) => ({ articles: [...p.articles, article] })),
  vider: () => set({ articles: [] }),
}));

// reusable selectors: values calculated from the state
export const nombreArticles = (p: Panier) => p.articles.length;
export const totalPanier = (p: Panier) => p.articles.reduce((s, a) => s + a.prix, 0);
  • line 23: the function that creates a store;
  • lines 30–34: the store type: the state ([articles]) and the actions ([ajouter], [vider]), which are the only ones that can modify it;
  • lines 36–41: [create<Panier>()(fabrique)] creates the store and returns a hook. The factory receives [set], which modifies the state: [set(objet)] or [set((etat) => objet)]; only the changes are passed; the rest is preserved. As with [useState], the state itself is never modified: a new one is created;
  • Lines 44–45: selectors—functions that calculate a value based on the state.

The store exists as long as the application runs; in UN, there is only one instance: it survives the removal of a component... but not a page reload (F5), which restarts the application. Context and [useReducer] could do the same job; a store has two advantages: it is readable by components (by a router guard, for example), and a component is only called back if the part of the state it reads has changed.

docs.title: 5.2.2. Preferences
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 20-state-sharing/src/stores/preferences.ts - a state that survives F5
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// For data to survive a page reload or when the
// the browser, it must be stored DANS in the browser: localStorage (a
// small key-to-string dictionary, unique to each site).
// Zustand’s “persist” middleware handles this: it reads localStorage from
// the store is created, and rewrites it whenever a change occurs (key
// "exemple20.preferences", value: the JSON of the state).
// No sensitive data (passwords, tokens) is stored there: any script
// on the page can read localStorage.
// =========================================================================

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware';

interface Preferences {
  sombre: boolean;
  taille: number; // text size, in px
  modifier: (changement: Partial<Pick<Preferences, 'sombre' | 'taille'>>) => void;
}

export const usePreferences = create<Preferences>()(
  persist(
    (set) => ({
      sombre: false,
      taille: 16,
      modifier: (changement) => set(changement),
    }),
    { name: 'exemple20.preferences' },
  ),
);

For data to persist after the page is reloaded or the browser is closed, it must be stored DANS in the browser: [localStorage], a small key/string dictionary specific to each site. The “middleware” [persist] from [Zustand] handles this (lines 24–31): It reads [localStorage] when the store is created and rewrites it whenever a change occurs, under the key [exemple20.preferences] (line 30). Sensitive data (passwords, tokens) is not stored in JAMAIS: any script on the page can read [localStorage].

docs.title: 5.2.3. The components
docs.text:
// 20-etat-partage/src/composants/Boutique.tsx - AJOUTE to the shared cart
import { usePanier, type Article } from '../stores/panier';

const PRODUITS: Article[] = [
  { libelle: 'Consultation', prix: 30 },
  { libelle: 'Vaccin', prix: 12.5 },
];

export default function Boutique() {
   // Only the action is read: The store is not called back when the cart changes
  const ajouter = usePanier((p) => p.ajouter);
  return (
    <div className="card p-3 h-100">
      <h2 className="h6">Boutique</h2>
      {PRODUITS.map((p) => (
        <button key={p.libelle} className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary mb-2" onClick={() => ajouter(p)}>
          + {p.libelle} ({p.prix} €)
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

[usePanier((p) => p.ajouter)]: A component reads the store via a selector and is called only if a part of the state (CE) changes. [Boutique] only reads the action [ajouter], which never changes: it is never called when the shopping cart changes.

// 20-etat-partage/src/composants/ResumePanier.tsx - LIT same shopping cart
import { nombreArticles, totalPanier, usePanier } from '../stores/panier';

export default function ResumePanier() {
  const nombre = usePanier(nombreArticles);
  const total = usePanier(totalPanier);
  const vider = usePanier((p) => p.vider);
  return (
    <div className="card p-3 h-100">
      <h2 className="h6">Panier</h2>
      <p className="mb-2">{nombre} article(s), {total} €</p>
      <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger align-self-start" disabled={nombre === 0} onClick={vider}>Vider</button>
    </div>
  );
}

[ResumePanier] reads the number of items and the total using the store’s selectors.

// 20-etat-partage/src/composants/CompteurLocal.tsx - a state LOCAL, which disappears with the component
import { useState } from 'react';

export default function CompteurLocal({ titre }: { titre: string }) {
  const [clics, setClics] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="card p-3 h-100">
      <h2 className="h6">{titre}</h2>
      <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary align-self-start" onClick={() => setClics(clics + 1)}>
        {clics} clic(s)
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}

A LOCAL report, which disappears along with the component.

docs.title: 5.2.4. The page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 20-state-sharing/src/App.tsx - three client-side data "scopes"
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same question as Example 23 in the course NestJS (application scope,
// request, client), transposed to the browser:
//    - the state LOCAL of a component (CompteurLocal) disappears along with it;
//    - the state of a MAGASIN (the shopping cart) is shared by all components
//      and survives their removal—but not that of F5;
//    - The state stored in localStorage (preferences) persists through F5 and the
//      browser is closed.
// And a new feature in React 19.2, <Activity mode="hidden">: the content is
// CACHÉ, but not removed; its local state is preserved.
// Uncheck and then recheck “Show Area,” then reload the page: compare.
// =========================================================================

import { Activity, useState } from 'react';
import { usePreferences } from './stores/preferences';
import Boutique from './composants/Boutique';
import ResumePanier from './composants/ResumePanier';
import CompteurLocal from './composants/CompteurLocal';

export default function App() {
  const { sombre, taille, modifier } = usePreferences();
  const [zoneVisible, setZoneVisible] = useState(true);

  return (
    <div className={`min-vh-100 ${sombre ? 'bg-dark text-light' : ''}`} style={{ fontSize: taille }}>
      <div className="container py-4">
        <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 20 - un état partagé</h1>
        <div className="d-flex flex-wrap gap-4 mb-3">
          <label className="form-check-label">
            <input type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={sombre}
                   onChange={(e) => modifier({ sombre: e.target.checked })} /> thème sombre
          </label>
          <label>
            taille du texte{' '}
            <input type="range" min={12} max={22} value={taille}
                   onChange={(e) => modifier({ taille: e.target.valueAsNumber })} /> {taille} px
          </label>
          <label className="form-check-label">
            <input type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={zoneVisible}
                   onChange={(e) => setZoneVisible(e.target.checked)} /> afficher la zone
          </label>
        </div>
        <div className="row g-3 text-body">
          {/* removed: these components disappear, along with their local state */}
          {zoneVisible && (
            <>
              <div className="col-md-3"><Boutique /></div>
              <div className="col-md-3"><ResumePanier /></div>
              <div className="col-md-3"><CompteurLocal titre="État local" /></div>
            </>
          )}
          {/* Hidden: the component remains in memory, and its state is preserved */}
          <Activity mode={zoneVisible ? 'visible' : 'hidden'}>
            <div className="col-md-3"><CompteurLocal titre="État local, dans une Activity" /></div>
          </Activity>
        </div>
        <p className="mt-3 mb-2">Hors de la zone, un second résumé du MÊME panier (il reste là quand la zone disparaît) :</p>
        <div className="text-body"><ResumePanier /></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • line 23: without a selector, the entire store is read (and the component is reloaded with each change);
  • lines 47–53: the field is removed when the checkbox is unchecked: its components disappear, along with their local state;
  • lines 55–57: [<Activity mode="hidden">] ([React] 19.2) hides its content without removing it: the component remains in memory, along with its state. This is useful for tabs or a page you leave and return to;
  • line 60: outside the area, a second summary of the MÊME shopping cart.

Add two items to the shopping cart, double-click the first local counter and triple-click the one in the [Activity], uncheck and then recheck “Show Area,” and check “Dark Theme”:

The shopping cart remains intact (it’s in the store); the first counter has reset to 0 (its component was removed and then recreated); the one for [Activity] has retained its value. When you reload the page (F5), the shopping cart is empty, but the theme and text size are preserved ([localStorage]).

This is the same issue as Example 23 from the [NestJS] course (application scope, query, client), transposed to the browser.

docs.title: 10. Case Study: The React Client for the RdvMedecins Application
10.1. The Problem
docs.text:
The [RdvMedecins] application allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor’s office. The [NestJS] course wrote it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages. Here, we are writing the client application [React]: the MÊMES pages, generated in the browser from the JSON data on the server described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box.”

The client must provide everything that the HTML application provided:

  • a login page, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
  • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
  • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
  • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
  • two languages: French and English;
  • unique URLs ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=...]), which can be reloaded, bookmarked, and navigated using the browser’s Back/Forward buttons.

docs.title: 10.2. Installation and Execution
docs.text:
The JSON server must be installed and running (see the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box”). To use the client in a browser, you do not need the CAPTCHA test mode: you can leave the [CAPTCHA_TEST] field blank in the server’s [.env] file.

In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-react] folder:

npm install
npm start

then open http://localhost:5173 in a browser. The demo accounts are listed on the login page (password = login).

The examples also use port 5173: first, stop the currently running example ([Ctrl-C]). You can also start the client on a different port: [npm start -- --port 5174].

// =========================================================================
// main.tsx - the application startup
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - style sheets (Bootstrap, styles.css);
//    - i18next (French and English);
//    - TanStack Query, which reads data from the server: its failed
//      fail, display their error messages in the error area, in UN location
//      (except for those that specify they handle their own errors:
//      meta.erreurGeree);
//    - the router, which displays the page for the current address.
// =========================================================================

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { QueryCache, QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { RouterProvider } from 'react-router/dom';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import './styles.css';
import './i18n/i18n';
import { useMessages } from './stores/messages';
import { routeur } from './routeur';

const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  queryCache: new QueryCache({
    onError: (erreur, requete) => {
      if (!requete.meta?.erreurGeree) {
        useMessages.getState().afficherErreurApi(erreur);
      }
    },
  }),
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retry: false, // an error is displayed immediately, without a retry
      refetchOnWindowFocus: false, // no reload when returning to the tab
    },
  },
});

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <RouterProvider router={routeur} />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  </StrictMode>,
);
  • lines 17–19: the style sheets, followed by the configuration of [i18next], which is executed once when the module is loaded;
  • lines 23–37: the [TanStack Query] client (Example 24), with two settings:
    • lines 24–30: [onError] is called for CHAQUE failed request: its error message is displayed in the error area, in a single location. A query that handles its own error declares it in its metadata: [meta: { erreurGeree: true }];
    • Lines 33–34: By default, [TanStack Query] retries a failed request three times and reloads the data when you return to the tab: here, an error is displayed immediately, and the data changes only when requested;
  • line 42: the router (built in [routeur.ts]) displays the page for the current address.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// routeur.ts - the application router and its dependencies
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The router is built here, independent of any components, so that two
// mechanisms can use it:
//    1. the 401 response to a protected request (expired session): we ignore
//       the user, prepare the message, and redirect to the
//       login page (see api/client.ts);
//    2. “Flash” messages: at the end of CHAQUE navigation, the messages
//       from the previous page disappear, and those displayed for the
//       appear (see stores/messages.ts).
// =========================================================================

import { createBrowserRouter } from 'react-router';
import { routes } from './routes';
import { quandSessionExpiree } from './api/client';
import { useSession } from './stores/session';
import { useMessages } from './stores/messages';

export const routeur = createBrowserRouter(routes);

// 1. Session expired
quandSessionExpiree(() => {
  useSession.getState().oublier();
  useMessages.getState().flash('erreur', 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
  routeur.navigate('/login');
});

// 2. subscribe: the function is called whenever the router’s state changes
// router’s state. A browsing session is TERMINÉE when it is no longer in progress
// (idle) and the address has changed (each visited address has a unique key,
// location.key — including when only the parameters change: /agenda?...)
let cleAdresse = routeur.state.location.key;
routeur.subscribe((etat) => {
  if (etat.navigation.state === 'idle' && etat.location.key !== cleAdresse) {
    cleAdresse = etat.location.key;
    useMessages.getState().nouvellePage();
  }
});
  • line 20: the router, in “data” mode (example 17), is generated as HORS from any component: code that is not a component can thus use it ([routeur.navigate]);
  • lines 23–27: what to do when a protected request receives a 401 response (see [api/client.ts]): forget the user, prepare the message for the next page, go to the login page;
  • lines 33–39: [routeur.subscribe(fonction)]: the function is called whenever the router’s state changes. At the end of each navigation, the messages from the previous page disappear and the “flash” messages appear (see [stores/messages.ts]).

// =========================================================================
// api/types.ts - the JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into TypeScript interfaces, of the API described in Chapter
// "The Server, a Black Box." The compiler thus verifies that the client
// uses only fields that actually exist.
// =========================================================================

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string; // display name: "Marie PELISSIER"
  role: Role;
}

// GET /api/captcha
export interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

// a title, a first name, a last name
export interface Identite {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
export interface Personne extends Identite {
  id: number;
  version: number; // optimistic lock: to be sent back with a modification
  login?: string; // only for ADMIN
}

// what is sent to create/modify a person (ADMIN)
export interface DonneesPersonne extends Identite {
  login: string; // '' = default value (creation) or unchanged (modification)
  password: string; // same as above
  version?: number;
}

export interface Creneau {
  id: number;
  hdebut: number;
  mdebut: number;
  hfin: number;
  mfin: number;
}

// an agenda entry, with the DROITS of the logged-in user
export interface CreneauAgenda extends Creneau {
  libre: boolean;
  patient: Identite | null; // null: available, or occupied by another patient
  moi: boolean; // the logged-in patient’s appointment
  reservable: boolean;
  idRv: number | null; // specified if the user can cancel
}

// GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=...&day=...
export interface Agenda {
  medecin: Personne;
  jour: string; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
  creneaux: CreneauAgenda[];
  info: string | null; // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)
}

// GET /api/my-account
export interface MonEspace {
  patient: Identite;
  rendezVous: { id: number; jour: string; creneau: Creneau; medecin: Personne }[];
}

// GET /api/my-space
export interface MonCompte extends Identite {
  login: string;
  version: number;
}

// PUT /api/my-account
export interface ModificationMonCompte extends Identite {
  login: string;
  password: string; // '' = unchanged
  confirmation: string;
  motDePasseActuel: string;
  version: number;
}

// POST /api/registration
export interface Inscription extends Identite {
  login: string;
  password: string;
  confirmation: string;
}

The JSON objects from API, described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box,” translated into [TypeScript] interfaces:

  • lines 25–29: a title, a first name, a last name—what doctors, clients, and patients have in common when making appointments;
  • lines 32–36: a doctor or a client. [version]: the server’s optimistic lock; a modification returns the read version: if someone has modified the record in the meantime, the server refuses ([ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE]);
  • lines 54–60: a calendar entry. The server specifies the DROITS values for the logged-in user: [reservable], [idRv] (filled in if the user can cancel); the client does not need to recalculate them;
  • Line 67: a translation key, for patients who already have an appointment.

docs.title: 10.4.3.2. src/api/erreur-api.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/erreur-api.ts - UNE class for all errors in API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Reuse of common/erreur-api.ts examples. Any request error
// (4xx/5xx server response, server unreachable, proxy response)
// becomes a ErreurApi, which contains the CLÉ message translation, its
// parameters, and the error for each field in a rejected form.
// =========================================================================

export class ErreurApi extends Error {
  readonly statusCode: number; // 0: the server did not respond
  readonly cle: string; // translation key: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
  readonly params: Record<string, string>;
  readonly champs: Record<string, string>; // Error for each field

  constructor(statusCode: number, cle: string, params: Record<string, string> = {}, champs: Record<string, string> = {}) {
    super(cle);
    this.name = 'ErreurApi';
    this.statusCode = statusCode;
    this.cle = cle;
    this.params = params;
    this.champs = champs;
  }
}

// an error response (4xx, 5xx) -> a ErreurApi
export async function depuisReponse(reponse: Response): Promise<ErreurApi> {
  let corps: { cle?: string; params?: Record<string, string>; champs?: Record<string, string> } = {};
  try {
    const json: unknown = await reponse.json();
    if (typeof json === 'object' && json !== null) {
      corps = json;
    }
  } catch {
     // not JSON: our server did not respond
  }
  return new ErreurApi(
    reponse.status,
     // no key: the response did not come from our server, but from a proxy
     // (Vite: 500 or 502 with no body JSON; nginx: 502, 504...)
    corps.cle ?? (reponse.status >= 500 ? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE' : 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR'),
    corps.params,
    corps.champs,
  );
}

The [ErreurApi] class from Example 24, unchanged: A TOUTE request error becomes a [ErreurApi], which contains the message’s translation key, its parameters, and the error for each field in a rejected form.

// api/client.ts - TOUTES requests to API go through here
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from the examples in common/api.ts, with a new feature: centralized handling
// centralized handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// the account has been deleted, the server has restarted with a different
// secret key... Rather than handling this case in every component, it is
// handles it in ICI, just once. But this file knows neither the router nor the
// messages (it doesn’t depend on anything): it calls a function that was
// assigned to it at startup (quandSessionExpiree, see routeur.ts), which ignores
// the user and redirects to the login page.
//
// Some requests handle their own 401 responses (login, GET
// /api/auth/me...): these are "public" (see rdvmedecins.api.ts).
// =========================================================================

import { depuisReponse, ErreurApi } from './erreur-api';

// What to do when the server returns a 401 response to a protected request
let sessionExpiree: () => void = () => {};

export function quandSessionExpiree(action: () => void): void {
  sessionExpiree = action;
}

export type Methode = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE';

// public: true for routes that handle the 401 themselves
export async function requete<T>(methode: Methode, url: string, corps?: unknown, publique = false): Promise<T> {
  let reponse: Response;
  try {
    reponse = await fetch(`/api${url}`, {
      method: methode,
      headers: corps === undefined ? {} : { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: corps === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(corps),
    });
  } catch {
     // No response: network down, server stopped
    throw new ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
  }
  if (!reponse.ok) {
    const erreur = await depuisReponse(reponse);
    if (erreur.statusCode === 401 && !publique) {
      sessionExpiree();
    }
    throw erreur;
  }
  return (await reponse.json()) as T;
}

The [requete] function from Example 24, with a new feature: the 401 response.

  • Lines 22–26: the function to call when a protected request receives a 401 response. This file has no dependencies (neither on the router nor on the messages): [routeur.ts] assigns this function to it at startup. This avoids a circular dependency (the client imports the router, which imports the routes, which import the pages, which import the client...);
  • line 31: Some requests handle their own 401 errors: the login (incorrect password: 401), [GET /api/auth/moi] (no one is logged in: 401)...;
  • Lines 45–47: A protected request receives a 401: the session has expired. This is reported (PUIS), and the promise is rejected as with any other error: the component waiting for the response has no specific action to take.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/rdvmedecins.api.ts - one function per route in API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The client’s “data access layer”: components call these
// functions, which are typed, without knowing anything about URL, fetch, or JSON. If
// the API changes, only this file changes.
// Each function returns a PROMESSE: the components chain together
// requests using async/await. If a request fails, the promise is rejected
// with a ErreurApi (see client.ts).
// =========================================================================

import { requete } from './client';
import type {
  Agenda,
  Captcha,
  DonneesPersonne,
  Inscription,
  ModificationMonCompte,
  MonCompte,
  MonEspace,
  Personne,
  Utilisateur,
} from './types';

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are handled the same way
export type TypePersonnes = 'medecins' | 'clients';

type Vide = Record<string, never>;

export const api = {
   // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
  captcha: () => requete<Captcha>('GET', '/captcha', undefined, true),
  moi: () => requete<Utilisateur>('GET', '/auth/moi', undefined, true),
  connecter: (login: string, password: string, captchaId: string, captcha: string) =>
    requete<Utilisateur>('POST', '/auth/login', { login, password, captchaId, captcha }, true),
  deconnecter: () => requete<Vide>('POST', '/auth/logout', {}, true),

   // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
  accesInscription: (captchaId: string, captcha: string) =>
    requete<Vide>('POST', '/inscription/acces', { captchaId, captcha }, true),
  etatAccesInscription: () => requete<{ valide: boolean }>('GET', '/inscription/acces', undefined, true),
  inscrire: (donnees: Inscription) => requete<{ login: string }>('POST', '/inscription', donnees, true),

   // ------------------------------------------------ calendar and appointments
   // idMedecin null: for a logged-in doctor, SON calendar
  agenda(idMedecin: number | null, jour: string) {
    const parametres = new URLSearchParams({ jour });
    if (idMedecin !== null) {
      parametres.set('idMedecin', String(idMedecin));
    }
    return requete<Agenda>('GET', `/agenda?${parametres}`);
  },
  reserver: (jour: string, idCreneau: number, idClient: number | null) =>
    requete<{ id: number }>('POST', '/rendez-vous', { jour, idCreneau, idClient: idClient ?? undefined }),
  annulerRv: (idRv: number) => requete<Vide>('DELETE', `/rendez-vous/${idRv}`),

   // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and clients
  lister: (type: TypePersonnes) => requete<Personne[]>('GET', `/${type}`),
  lire: (type: TypePersonnes, id: number) => requete<Personne>('GET', `/${type}/${id}`),
  ajouter: (type: TypePersonnes, donnees: DonneesPersonne) => requete<Personne>('POST', `/${type}`, donnees),
  modifier: (type: TypePersonnes, id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne) => requete<Personne>('PUT', `/${type}/${id}`, donnees),
  supprimer: (type: TypePersonnes, id: number) => requete<Vide>('DELETE', `/${type}/${id}`),

   // ------------------------------------------------ the patient portal
  monEspace: () => requete<MonEspace>('GET', '/mon-espace'),
  monCompte: () => requete<MonCompte>('GET', '/mon-compte'),
  modifierMonCompte: (donnees: ModificationMonCompte) => requete<Utilisateur>('PUT', '/mon-compte', donnees),
  supprimerMonCompte: (motDePasseActuel: string) => requete<Vide>('DELETE', '/mon-compte', { motDePasseActuel }),
};

One function per route in API, typed: the components call [api.agenda(1, '2026-10-05')] without knowing anything about URL or JSON. If API changes, only this file changes.

  • lines 32–36: the connection routes, which are public (last parameter of [requete]: [true]);
  • lines 39–42: account creation, in two steps: solving the CAPTCHA on the login page provides a “pass” (a cookie), which the route [POST /api/inscription] requires;
  • lines 46–52: [URLSearchParams] generates the address parameters (and encodes them). For a logged-in doctor, there is no [idMedecin]: the server returns SON (calendar);
  • line 54: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: no [idClient]. [JSON.stringify] omits the [undefined] properties;
  • lines 58–62: doctors and clients are handled the same way: the type is a parameter;
  • line 28: the type of an empty object [{}], which certain routes return.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// i18n/i18n.ts - French and English (i18next, see example 21)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The dictionaries fr.json and en.json are those from the course NestJS
// (i18n/*.json), supplemented with a few client-specific keys
// (ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE...). The JSON server returns only CLÉS
// ('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'): these are the same as those in the dictionaries.
//
// The selected language is stored in localStorage (a preference, not
// sensitive data); otherwise, the browser’s language is used.
// =========================================================================

import i18n from 'i18next';
import { initReactI18next } from 'react-i18next';
import fr from './fr.json';
import en from './en.json';

export type Langue = 'fr' | 'en';
export const LANGUES: Langue[] = ['fr', 'en'];
const CLE_STOCKAGE = 'rdvmedecins.langue';

function langueDeDepart(): Langue {
  try {
    const memorisee = localStorage.getItem(CLE_STOCKAGE);
    if (memorisee === 'fr' || memorisee === 'en') {
      return memorisee;
    }
  } catch {
     // localStorage unavailable (strict private browsing...): too bad
  }
  return navigator.language.toLowerCase().startsWith('en') ? 'en' : 'fr';
}

// Every time the language changes: save it and update
// the page’s lang attribute (screen readers, spell checkers, hyphenation)
i18n.on('languageChanged', (langue) => {
  document.documentElement.lang = langue;
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(CLE_STOCKAGE, langue);
  } catch {
     // irrelevant
  }
});

i18n.use(initReactI18next).init({
   // Dictionaries are part of the application code: no queries
  resources: { fr: { translation: fr }, en: { translation: en } },
  lng: langueDeDepart(),
  fallbackLng: 'fr',
  interpolation: { escapeValue: false }, // React already escapes everything
});

export default i18n;

The configuration for Example 21:

  • lines 22–32: the stored language, otherwise the browser’s language. Access to [localStorage] may fail (strict private browsing): [try / catch];
  • lines 36–43: each time the language changes, it is saved and the [lang] attribute of the page is updated;
  • line 47: the dictionaries, imported as modules, are part of the compiled code and require no additional requests;
  • line 50: [React] already escapes everything it displays: no need to do it twice.

There is no equivalent to the “title strategy” of [Angular]: each page declares its title with the [<title>] tag, which [React] 19 places in the document header (see [components/TitrePage.tsx]).

docs.title: 10.4.5.1. src/stores/session.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// stores/session.ts - Is QUI connected?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user (or null), stored in a Zustand (see example
// 20): readable by components (useSession) ET via the code that is not
// not a component (router guards: useSession.getState()).
//
// The token JWT itself is not PAS here: it is in a cookie httpOnly that
// is handled only by the browser. The store keeps only the DESCRIPTION from
// the user, returned by the server ({ login, name, role }).
//
// Upon startup (and after a F5), the store is empty: verifier() requests
// the server, just once, to find out who is logged in (GET /api/auth/moi).
// =========================================================================

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { api } from '../api/rdvmedecins.api';
import type { Role, Utilisateur } from '../api/types';

interface Session {
  utilisateur: Utilisateur | null;
  verifier: () => Promise<void>;
  connecter: (login: string, password: string, captchaId: string, captcha: string) => Promise<void>;
  mettreAJour: (u: Utilisateur) => void;
  deconnecter: () => Promise<void>;
  oublier: () => void;
}

// Has the question “Who is logged in?” already been asked of the server?
// (a module variable: it does not need to be displayed)
let verification: Promise<void> | null = null;

export const useSession = create<Session>()((set, get) => ({
  utilisateur: null,

   // called by the router guard before CHAQUE navigation; does not query
   // the server only the first time (the promise is retained and reused)
  verifier() {
    verification ??= api
      .moi()
      .then((u) => set({ utilisateur: u }))
      .catch(() => set({ utilisateur: null })); // 401: unauthorized; or server unreachable
    return verification;
  },

  async connecter(login, password, captchaId, captcha) {
    set({ utilisateur: await api.connecter(login, password, captchaId, captcha) });
  },

   // the user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
  mettreAJour: (u) => set({ utilisateur: u }),

  async deconnecter() {
    try {
      await api.deconnecter();
    } finally {
      get().oublier();
    }
  },

   // without making a request to the server: session expired, account deleted
  oublier: () => set({ utilisateur: null }),
}));

// what is inferred about the user: standard functions
export const role = (u: Utilisateur | null): Role | null => u?.role ?? null;
export const estAdmin = (u: Utilisateur | null) => role(u) === 'ADMIN';
export const estPatient = (u: Utilisateur | null) => role(u) === 'USER';
// ADMIN and DOCTOR: schedule and cancel appointments for any patient
export const estGestionnaire = (u: Utilisateur | null) => role(u) === 'ADMIN' || role(u) === 'DOCTOR';
// the home page for each role, immediately after logging in
export const pageAccueil = (u: Utilisateur | null) => (estPatient(u) ? '/mon-espace' : '/agenda');

The logged-in user, in a store [Zustand] (example 20). A store can be read by the components ([useSession((s) => s.utilisateur)]) ET via the code that is not a component: [useSession.getState()] (the router guards).

  • Line 21: the user’s DESCRIPTION ([{ login, nom, role }]). The token JWT, on the other hand, is in the cookie httpOnly: the client never sees it;
  • Lines 31–44: [verifier()] asks the server who is logged in, UNE times: the promise is kept and reused ([??=]: assignment if the variable is [null]). The guards call it before each navigation: only the first one actually waits;
  • lines 46–48: the connection: the user returned by the server is stored in the store;
  • lines 53–59: logout. [finally]: even if the server does not respond, the client forgets the user;
  • lines 66–72: what is inferred about the user: ordinary functions that take the user as a parameter. A component writes [estAdmin(utilisateur)] after reading [utilisateur] from the store; it is then redisplayed when the user changes.

docs.title: 10.4.5.2. src/stores/messages.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// stores/messages.ts - messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same layout as the HTML application:
//    - a SUCCÈS is displayed as HAUT on the page (green banner);
//    - a ERREUR appears as BAS, on a light pink background (the “sticky” area).
// A message is a translation CLÉ (plus its settings): it is therefore re-translated
// on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// "Flash" messages: an action that ends with a page change
// page (booking, adding a doctor, etc.) places its message using flash();
// it will be displayed on the page SUIVANTE, then disappear upon navigation
// . The router calls nouvellePage() at the end of each
// navigation (see routeur.ts). On the server side, this was the role of the
// short-lived cookie "rdvmedecins_flash".
// =========================================================================

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { ErreurApi } from '../api/erreur-api';

export interface Message {
  cle: string;
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

interface Messages {
  succes: Message | null;
  erreur: Message | null;
   // the messages to be displayed on the next page
  enAttente: { succes: Message | null; erreur: Message | null } | null;
  afficherSucces: (cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>) => void;
  afficherErreur: (cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>) => void;
  afficherErreurApi: (e: unknown) => void;
  effacer: () => void;
  flash: (type: 'succes' | 'erreur', cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>) => void;
  nouvellePage: () => void;
}

export const useMessages = create<Messages>()((set) => ({
  succes: null,
  erreur: null,
  enAttente: null,

  afficherSucces: (cle, params) => set({ succes: { cle, params }, erreur: null }),
  afficherErreur: (cle, params) => set({ erreur: { cle, params }, succes: null }),

   // a ErreurApi -> the page’s message; any other error is a
   // client-side issue, which is logged (browser console)
  afficherErreurApi(e) {
    if (!(e instanceof ErreurApi)) {
      throw e;
    }
    set({ erreur: { cle: e.cle, params: e.params }, succes: null });
  },

  effacer: () => set({ succes: null, erreur: null }),

   // for the page SUIVANTE
  flash: (type, cle, params) =>
    set((m) => ({ enAttente: { succes: null, erreur: null, ...m.enAttente, [type]: { cle, params } } })),

   // a new page: the messages from the previous page disappear, and
   // flash messages appear
  nouvellePage: () =>
    set((m) => ({ succes: m.enAttente?.succes ?? null, erreur: m.enAttente?.erreur ?? null, enAttente: null })),
}));

Messages displayed to the user: a success message at the top of the page, an error message at the bottom.

  • Lines 21–24: A message is a CLÉ translation and its parameters, not plain text: it automatically re-translates itself if the user changes languages;
  • lines 49–54: a [ErreurApi] becomes the page’s error message. Any other error is a client-side issue (a programming error): it is re-triggered so that it appears in the browser console;
  • lines 59–60: [flash] sets a message for the SUIVANTE page. An action that ends with a page change (adding a doctor, followed by a return to the list) uses this: a message displayed immediately would disappear as the user navigates;
  • lines 64–65: called by the router at the end of each navigation: the pending messages become the page’s messages.

docs.title: 10.4.5.3. src/stores/confirmation.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// stores/confirmation.ts - “Are you sure?”
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 16, in the form of a store: confirm(key) opens
// the confirmation window (components/FenetreConfirmation.tsx, placed once
// in the template) and returns a promise resolved to true (Yes) or
// false (No). The message is a translation string: the window translates it
// into the current language.
//
//      if (await confirm('AGENDA.CANCEL_CONFIRM')) { ... }
// =========================================================================

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { useMessages } from './messages';

interface Confirmation {
  cleMessage: string | null; // null: window closed
  reponse: (oui: boolean) => void;
}

// the function that will resolve the current promise (nothing to display: out of scope)
let repondre: ((oui: boolean) => void) | null = null;

export const useConfirmation = create<Confirmation>()((set) => ({
  cleMessage: null,
  reponse(oui) {
    set({ cleMessage: null });
    const r = repondre;
    repondre = null;
    r?.(oui);
  },
}));

// a regular function, usable anywhere
export function confirmer(cle: string): Promise<boolean> {
  repondre?.(false); // a question still open? It evaluates to "no"
   // a new question: the messages from the previous action are out of date
  useMessages.getState().effacer();
  useConfirmation.setState({ cleMessage: cle });
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
    repondre = resolve;
  });
}

The confirmation window from Example 16, implemented as a store and an ordinary function:

  • line 17: the question asked (a translation key), or [null]: the window ([components/FenetreConfirmation.tsx]) is closed;
  • line 22: the function that will resolve the promise for the current question. Nothing to display: this is not a state, but a module variable;
  • lines 35–43: [confirmer] opens the window and returns a promise, resolved to [true] (Yes) or [false] (No) by [reponse]. A page simply writes [if (await confirmer('AGENDA.CANCEL_CONFIRM')) { ... }]. No context is needed, as in Example 16: the store is accessible everywhere.

docs.title: 10.4.6.1. src/hooks/useEnvoiFormulaire.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// hooks/useEnvoiFormulaire.ts - send a form to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All forms in the application follow the same pattern as
// Example 25: No rules are checked in the browser (they
// reside in UN one place only—the server), and in case of rejection:
//    - the error for each field (ErreurApi.champs) is displayed below the
//      field, outlined in red;
//    - the general message (ErreurApi.cle) is displayed at the bottom of the page.
// This hook groups these actions together. A page calls it once per form:
//
//      const submit = useEnvoiFormulaire();
//      if (await envoi.envoyer(() => api.inscrire(input))) { ... }
//      <ChampSaisie ... error={envoi.erreurs.nom} />
// =========================================================================

import { useCallback, useState } from 'react';
import { ErreurApi } from '../api/erreur-api';
import { useMessages } from '../stores/messages';

export function useEnvoiFormulaire() {
  const afficherErreurApi = useMessages((m) => m.afficherErreurApi);
   // the error for each field: a translation CLÉ
  const [erreurs, setErreurs] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
   // error message parameters ({min}...), returned by the server
  const [params, setParams] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
  const [enCours, setEnCours] = useState(false);

   // executes the send; returns true if successful. In case of ErreurApi, the
   // errors are displayed and false is returned.
  const envoyer = useCallback(
    async (action: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<boolean> => {
      setErreurs({});
      setParams({});
      setEnCours(true);
      try {
        await action();
        return true;
      } catch (e) {
        afficherErreurApi(e); // (rethrows any error that is not a ErreurApi)
        const erreur = e as ErreurApi;
        setErreurs(erreur.champs);
        setParams(erreur.params);
        return false;
      } finally {
        setEnCours(false);
      }
    },
    [afficherErreurApi],
  );

   // the user modifies a field: the error disappears
  const effacerErreur = useCallback((champ: string) => {
    setErreurs((e) => {
      if (!(champ in e)) return e; // nothing to clear: the MÊME object (no new display)
      const { [champ]: _efface, ...reste } = e;
      return reste;
    });
  }, []);

  return { erreurs, params, enCours, envoyer, effacerErreur };
}

All forms in the application follow the pattern shown in Example 25: no validation rules are checked in the browser, and if the server rejects the submission, the error for each field is displayed below the field, with a general error message at the bottom of the page. This custom hook (Example 15) handles the following actions:

  • lines 24–27: its state: the error for each field (a translation key), their parameters, and “submitting” (to disable the button);
  • lines 31–50: [envoyer(action)] executes the submission and returns [true] if it succeeds. If [ErreurApi] is returned, the errors are displayed and the function returns [false]. [useCallback]: the function remains MÊME from one display to the next;
  • Lines 53–59: The user modifies a field: the error disappears. If the field did not have an error, the MÊME object is returned; [React] does not redisplay anything. [const { [champ]: _efface, ...reste } = e]: [reste] is a copy of [e], without the [champ] property.

docs.title: 10.4.6.2. src/hooks/useCaptcha.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// hooks/useCaptcha.ts - a CAPTCHA image, and the option to change it
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Loads a CAPTCHA (GET /api/captcha) when the component is displayed, which
// uses it. reload() requests another one: this is necessary after CHAQUE
// attempt, because an image is only used UNE once (the server forgets it as soon as
// it has verified it). The login page uses it with the component
// ChampCaptcha, which displays the image and the input field.
// =========================================================================

import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { api } from '../api/rdvmedecins.api';
import type { Captcha } from '../api/types';

export function useCaptcha() {
  const [captcha, setCaptcha] = useState<Captcha | null>(null);

  const recharger = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      setCaptcha(await api.captcha());
    } catch {
      setCaptcha(null); // server unreachable: the login will fail with a plaintext message
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    recharger();
  }, [recharger]);

   // captchaId: the ID of the displayed image, to be sent with the response
  return { svg: captcha?.svg ?? '', captchaId: captcha?.id ?? '', recharger };
}

A CAPTCHA image, loaded when the component is displayed, and [recharger()] to request another one: this is necessary after the CHAQUE attempt, because the server discards an image as soon as it has verified it.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// formatage.ts - the display of people, hours, and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends data BRUTES (start_hour: 8, start_minute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the responsibility
// the client (see example 09).
// =========================================================================

import type { Creneau, Identite } from './api/types';

// "Ms. Alice DURAND"
export function libelle(p: Identite): string {
  return `${p.titre} ${p.prenom} ${p.nom}`;
}

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
export function heure(h: number, m: number): string {
  return `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

// "8:00 - 8:20"
export function horaire(c: Creneau): string {
  return `${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}`;
}

// today’s date, in the “yyyy-MM-dd” format (the same as <input type="date"> and API)
export function aujourdhui(): string {
  const d = new Date();
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

// true if [jour] is a valid date in the yyyy-MM-dd format
export function estUneDateValide(jour: unknown): jour is string {
  if (typeof jour !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(jour)) {
    return false;
  }
  const date = new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`);
  return !isNaN(date.getTime()) && date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) === jour;
}

// "Monday, October 5, 2026" / "Monday 5 October 2026"
export function jourLong(jour: string, langue: string): string {
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(langue === 'en' ? 'en-GB' : 'fr-FR', {
    dateStyle: 'full',
    timeZone: 'UTC', // "2026-10-05T00:00:00Z" must remain 5, regardless of the time zone
  }).format(new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`));
}

The server sends raw data ([hdebut: 8, mdebut: 0]; [jour: "2026-10-05"]); formatting is the client’s responsibility (example 09). These are ordinary functions: [React] does not require “pipes,” and an expression such as JSX can call any function ([{horaire(c)}]).

  • Lines 33–39: [jour is string]: a type predicate: if the function returns [true], [TypeScript] then knows that [jour] is a string. A date “that exists”: [2026-02-30] has the correct format, but [new Date] converts it to March 2; the resulting date is then compared to the original string;
  • lines 42–47: the day spelled out in full, in the user’s language, using [Intl.DateTimeFormat]. [timeZone: 'UTC']: The date is constructed at midnight (UTC); formatted in the Martinique time zone (UTC-4), it would still be the previous day.

docs.title: 10.4.8.1. src/routes.tsx
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// routes.tsx - the application's pages and their access rights
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The MÊMES URLs that the application HTML (/login, /agenda, /doctors,
// /my-space...), but these are now routes in the CLIENT. The
// browser only sends a request to the server for the very first
// page; afterward, the router changes the address and the displayed component.
//
// The flip side of the coin: if the user reloads /agenda (F5), the
// browser does indeed request /agenda from the server, which must then
// return index.html (This is easily done in development; in production,
// see web/client-spa.ts on the JSON server).
//
// All pages are ENFANTS from the root route, whose component,
// Template, displays them in its <Outlet />. The page() function describes a
// page: its address, its component (loaded on demand for pages
// that are not always visited), and the guard that verifies its permissions.
// =========================================================================

import type { ComponentType } from 'react';
import { redirect, type MiddlewareFunction, type RouteObject } from 'react-router';
import type { TypePersonnes } from './api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { garde, gardeInscription, type Droits } from './gardes';
import Gabarit from './components/Gabarit';
import Connexion from './pages/Connexion';
import Agenda from './pages/Agenda';
import PageErreur from './pages/PageErreur';

// a page: component loaded immediately (Component) or on demand
// (load); autresGardes: page-specific guards, after the common guard
interface Page {
  path: string;
  droits: Droits;
  Component?: ComponentType;
  charger?: () => Promise<ComponentType>;
  autresGardes?: MiddlewareFunction[];
}

function page({ path, droits, Component, charger, autresGardes = [] }: Page): RouteObject {
  return {
    path,
     // The guards execute AVANT when the page loads
    middleware: [garde(droits), ...autresGardes],
    ...(charger ? { lazy: async () => ({ Component: await charger() }) } : { Component }),
  };
}

// the doctor management pages ET for clients (ADMIN), on the same
// template; the component receives the type as a property
function pagesPersonnes(type: TypePersonnes): RouteObject[] {
  const droits: Droits = { roles: ['ADMIN'] };
  const liste = async () => {
    const { default: Personnes } = await import('./pages/Personnes');
    return () => <Personnes type={type} />;
  };
  const formulaire = async () => {
    const { default: PersonneFormulaire } = await import('./pages/PersonneFormulaire');
    return () => <PersonneFormulaire type={type} />;
  };
  return [
    page({ path: type, droits, charger: liste }),
    page({ path: `${type}/ajouter`, droits, charger: formulaire }),
    page({ path: `${type}/:id/modifier`, droits, charger: formulaire }),
  ];
}

export const routes: RouteObject[] = [
  {
    path: '/',
    Component: Gabarit,
     // displayed during the very first visit (the time it takes to query the
     // server which is connected)
    HydrateFallback: () => null,
    children: [
       // "/": to /login, which in turn redirects to the role’s home page if the user is logged in
       // (a component that displays nothing: the redirection occurs beforehand)
      { index: true, loader: () => redirect('/login'), Component: () => null },
      page({ path: 'login', droits: { public: true }, Component: Connexion }),
      page({ path: 'agenda', droits: {}, Component: Agenda }),
      ...pagesPersonnes('medecins'),
      ...pagesPersonnes('clients'),
      page({
        path: 'inscription',
        droits: { public: true },
        charger: async () => (await import('./pages/Inscription')).default,
        autresGardes: [gardeInscription],
      }),
      page({ path: 'mon-espace', droits: { roles: ['USER'] }, charger: async () => (await import('./pages/EspacePatient')).default }),
      page({ path: 'mon-compte', droits: { roles: ['USER'] }, charger: async () => (await import('./pages/MonCompte')).default }),
      page({ path: 'interdit', droits: {}, Component: () => <PageErreur code={403} /> }),
      page({ path: '*', droits: { public: true }, Component: () => <PageErreur code={404} /> }),
    ],
  },
];

The MÊMES addresses that the HTML application uses, but these are now routes from the CLIENT:

  • lines 31–37: the description of a page: its address, access permissions, and component, either provided immediately ([Component]) or loaded on demand ([charger]);
  • lines 39–46: [page()] generates the corresponding route:
    • line 43: the common guard, generated based on the page’s permissions, followed by the page-specific guards. They execute AVANT when the page loads (Example 18);
    • line 44: [lazy]: the page code is loaded on the first visit (Example 17). The login page and the calendar, which everyone can see, are loaded immediately; the ADMIN and patient pages are loaded on demand;
  • lines 50–65: the three pages for managing doctors, followed by clients, using the same template. The component is wrapped in a parameterless component, [() => <Personnes type={type} />]: this is how it receives the type as a prop;
  • lines 69–70: the root route. Its component, [Gabarit], displays the current page in its [<Outlet />];
  • line 73: what is displayed during the very first navigation, while the guard asks the server which one is connected: nothing;
  • line 77: the address [/] redirects to [/login], whose guard itself redirects to the role’s home page if the user is logged in;
  • lines 78–79: [droits: { public: true }]: the page is accessible without being logged in; [droits: {}]: you must be logged in, regardless of your role;
  • lines 83–87: creating a public account has a second guard, [gardeInscription];
  • lines 88–89: [roles: ['USER']]: the patient’s pages;
  • line 90: the 403 page;
  • line 91: the 404 page: [*] refers to any address that no other route recognizes.

Reminder: If the user reloads [/agenda] (F5), the browser does indeed request [/agenda] from the server, which must then return [index.html]: this is what the development server for [Vite] does, and, in production, the server for JSON (see the “Deployment” chapter).

docs.title: 10.4.8.2. src/gardes.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// gardes.ts - the router guards (middleware, see Example 18)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// guard (permissions) FABRIQUE the guard for a page, based on its access permissions:
//    - public: accessible without being logged in;
//    - role s: authorized roles (none = all logged-in roles).
// Each page declares its own (see routes.tsx). Before each navigation
// to this page, the guard:
//    1. the first time (startup, F5), asks the server who is
//       connected (useSession.getState().verify()) ;
//    2. checks the page’s permissions and redirects if necessary.
//
// RAPPEL: These checks are merely a CONFORT (do not display a page
// unnecessary). Data protection is handled by the server, which
// verifies the token and role in the CHAQUE request.
// =========================================================================

import { redirect, type MiddlewareFunction } from 'react-router';
import type { Role } from './api/types';
import { api } from './api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { pageAccueil, useSession } from './stores/session';
import { useMessages } from './stores/messages';

export interface Droits {
  public?: boolean;
  roles?: Role[];
}

export function garde(droits: Droits): MiddlewareFunction {
  return async ({ request }) => {
    await useSession.getState().verifier();
     // getState(): the state of the store, read HORS from a component
    const utilisateur = useSession.getState().utilisateur;
    const url = new URL(request.url);

    if (droits.public) {
       // Already logged in: the login page is no longer relevant
      if (url.pathname === '/login' && utilisateur !== null) {
        throw redirect(pageAccueil(utilisateur));
      }
      return;
    }
    if (utilisateur === null) {
       // The requested page is cached to return to it after login
      throw redirect(`/login?redirect=${encodeURIComponent(url.pathname + url.search)}`);
    }
    if (droits.roles && !droits.roles.includes(utilisateur.role)) {
      throw redirect('/interdit');
    }
  };
}

// a guard PROPRE on the /registration route: no passcode (captcha
// resolved on the login page), return to the login page
export const gardeInscription: MiddlewareFunction = async () => {
  const { valide } = await api.etatAccesInscription().catch(() => ({ valide: false }));
  if (!valide) {
    useMessages.getState().flash('erreur', 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
    throw redirect('/login');
  }
};
  • lines 24–27: a page’s access rights;
  • lines 29–51: [garde(droits)] FABRIQUE a guard, i.e., router middleware (example 18):
    • line 31: the first time (startup, F5), the server is asked who is logged in; on subsequent occasions, the response is already available;
    • lines 36–42: a public page. A logged-in user no longer needs to do anything on the login page: they are redirected to their home page;
    • lines 43–46: no one is logged in: redirect to the login page, while retaining the requested page ([?redirect=...]), to return to it after login;
    • lines 47–49: the role is not authorized: the 403 page;
    • [throw redirect(...)]: a guard “triggers” a redirect: the current navigation is abandoned in favor of the new address;
  • lines 55–61: the guard specific to page [/inscription]: without a pass (the CAPTCHA solved on the login page), return to the login page with a message. The server would refuse to create the account in any case.

These checks are simply a CONFORT: do not display a useless page. Data protection is ensured by the server, which re-verifies the token and role at CHAQUE request.

// =========================================================================
// components/BarreNavigation.tsx - the navigation bar
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same content as in the HTML application (views/partials/navbar.hbs):
// Title, role-based menus, FR / EN, role, name, logout.
// "Doctors" and "Clients" appear only for ADMIN: a simple
// display convenience; true protection is provided by the server.
// =========================================================================

import { NavLink, useNavigate } from 'react-router';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { LANGUES } from '../i18n/i18n';
import { estAdmin, estPatient, useSession } from '../stores/session';

export default function BarreNavigation() {
  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation();
  const utilisateur = useSession((s) => s.utilisateur);
  const deconnecter = useSession((s) => s.deconnecter);
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  async function seDeconnecter() {
    await deconnecter().catch(() => {}); // even if the server does not respond
    navigate('/login');
  }

  return (
    <nav className="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
      <span className="navbar-brand mb-0">{t('APP.TITLE')}</span>

      {utilisateur ? (
        <ul className="navbar-nav me-auto">
          {estPatient(utilisateur) && (
            <li className="nav-item">
              {/* NavLink sets the "active" class (Bootstrap) on the menu of the displayed page */}
              <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/mon-espace">{t('APP.MENU_MY_SPACE')}</NavLink>
            </li>
          )}
          <li className="nav-item">
            <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/agenda">{t('APP.MENU_AGENDA')}</NavLink>
          </li>
          {estAdmin(utilisateur) && (
            <>
              <li className="nav-item">
                <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/medecins">{t('APP.MENU_DOCTORS')}</NavLink>
              </li>
              <li className="nav-item">
                <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/clients">{t('APP.MENU_PATIENTS')}</NavLink>
              </li>
            </>
          )}
        </ul>
      ) : (
        <div className="me-auto"></div>
      )}

      <div className="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
        {/* FR / EN: no request to the server; the page is re-rendered locally */}
        <div className="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label={t('APP.LANGUAGE')}>
          {LANGUES.map((l) => (
            <button key={l} type="button" className={`btn ${i18n.language === l ? 'btn-light' : 'btn-outline-light'}`}
                    aria-pressed={i18n.language === l} onClick={() => i18n.changeLanguage(l)}>
              {l.toUpperCase()}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>

        {utilisateur && (
          <>
            <span className="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{utilisateur.role}</span>
            <span className="text-white">{utilisateur.nom}</span>
            <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light" onClick={seDeconnecter}>{t('APP.LOGOUT')}</button>
          </>
        )}
      </div>
    </nav>
  );
}
  • lines 17–18: the component reads the user and the logout function from the session store; it is re-displayed when the user changes (login, logout, session expired);
  • lines 21–24: logout, then the login page. Even if the server does not respond, the client forgets the user (see [stores/session.ts]): the error is ignored ([catch(() => {})]);
  • lines 32–37: the menus depend on the role;
  • line 35: [NavLink] (example 17) sets the [active] class from [Bootstrap] on the menu of the displayed page;
  • lines 59–64: the FR / EN buttons. [i18n.changeLanguage(l)]: no request is sent to the server; the entire page is re-rendered locally. [aria-pressed]: a screen reader announces the current language button as “pressed”;
  • lines 67–73: the role, the name, and the logout button.
