docs.title: 8. Communicating with the server
docs.text: The examples in this chapter query the server JSON [RdvMedecins]: It must be running ([npm run start:dev] in the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder) on port 8080, at the same time as the [Vite] development server on port 5173.

docs.title: 8.1. Example 22: An initial request for HTTP
8.1.1. The development server’s proxy
docs.text:
The page in this example comes from http://localhost:5173 (the [Vite] development server); API is located at http://localhost:8080. To a browser, these are two different origins (the port is part of the origin). However, for security reasons, a browser does not allow a page to read responses from another origin unless the server explicitly permits it (the mechanism known as CORS). And a request to another origin does not carry cookies (and therefore not the token), unless the code requests it ([credentials: 'include']) ET and the server accepts it, again via CORS.

Rather than opening the server to other origins, we route requests from API through the development server at [Vite]. This is the proxy declared in the [vite.config.ts] file in the examples (see Example 01):

    proxy: {
       '/api': 'http://localhost:8080',
    },

The browser sends a request to [GET http://localhost:5173/api/captcha]; the development server forwards the request to [http://localhost:8080/api/captcha], then sends the response back to the browser. From the browser’s perspective, the page and API have the same origin:

In production, there will no longer be a development server: the JSON server itself will serve the compiled client files (see the “Deployment” chapter). The page and API will still have the same origin.

docs.title: 8.1.2. The request
docs.text:
[React] does not have its own HTTP client: the browser’s [fetch] function is used, or a library ([axios]...). [fetch] is more than sufficient.

// =========================================================================
// 22-fetch/src/App.tsx - a first request HTTP to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server JSON RdvMedecins must be running (port 8080). It is asked to
// a CAPTCHA: GET /api/captcha -> { "id": "...", "svg": "<svg ...>" }.
//
//    - fetch(url): the browser function that sends a request HTTP.
//      It returns a PROMESSE from the response; reponse.json() a promise
//      for the body, converted from JSON. React does not have its own HTTP client;
//    - the address is RELATIVE (/api/captcha): the request is sent to the
//      page’s server, Vite’s server (port 5173), which forwards it to the
//      JSON server (port 8080) via its proxy (see vite.config.ts);
//    - three statuses to display: in progress, successful, error.
// =========================================================================

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

// what GET returns for /api/captcha
interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

const styleCaptcha = { display: 'inline-block', border: '1px solid #dee2e6', borderRadius: '0.375rem' };

export default function App() {
  const [captcha, setCaptcha] = useState<Captcha | null>(null);
  const [enCours, setEnCours] = useState(true);
  const [erreur, setErreur] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [nbRequetes, setNbRequetes] = useState(0);
   // Every click on "Another image" changes this number, which restarts the effect
  const [demande, setDemande] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
     // AbortController: the way to ANNULER a pending request
    const annulation = new AbortController();
    setEnCours(true);
    setErreur(null);
    fetch('/api/captcha', { signal: annulation.signal })
      .then(async (reponse) => {
         // fetch does not return an error response (4xx, 5xx): test passes
        if (!reponse.ok) {
          throw new Error(`le serveur a répondu ${reponse.status} ${reponse.statusText}`);
        }
        const c = (await reponse.json()) as Captcha;
        setCaptcha(c);
        setNbRequetes((n) => n + 1);
        setEnCours(false);
      })
      .catch((e: Error) => {
        if (e.name === 'AbortError') return; // request canceled: nothing to display
        setErreur(e.message);
        setCaptcha(null);
        setEnCours(false);
      });
     // cleans up the ANNULE request if the effect is restarted or if the
     // component disappears before the response. In development, StrictMode
     // executes the effect twice at startup: the first request is
     // canceled (Network tab: “canceled”); only the second one counts.
    return () => annulation.abort();
  }, [demande]);

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 22 - une première requête HTTP</h1>
      <div className="card p-3">
        {enCours && <p className="text-muted">Chargement...</p>}
        {erreur && (
          <div className="alert alert-danger mb-3">
            Impossible d'obtenir un captcha : {erreur}.<br />
            Le serveur JSON RdvMedecins est-il lancé (port 8080) ?
          </div>
        )}
        {captcha && !enCours && (
          <>
            {/* dangerouslySetInnerHTML: insert a string like HTML */}
            <div className="mb-2"><div style={styleCaptcha} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: captcha.svg }} /></div>
            <p className="small text-muted">id : <code>{captcha.id}</code></p>
          </>
        )}
        <button className="btn btn-primary align-self-start" disabled={enCours} onClick={() => setDemande((d) => d + 1)}>
          Autre image
        </button>
        <p className="small text-muted mt-2 mb-0">
          {nbRequetes} requête(s) réussie(s) - ouvrez l'onglet Réseau des outils de développement (F12).
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 19–22: what [GET /api/captcha] returns;
  • lines 27–30: three states to display: in progress, successful (the CAPTCHA), error;
  • line 32: a request number: each click on “Another image” increments it, which triggers the effect again;
  • lines 34–61: the request is an effect: it synchronizes the component with the server, upon initial display and then with each new request:
    • line 36: a [AbortController] allows you to cancel a pending request: it changes its [signal] to [fetch];
    • line 39: [fetch(url)] sends a request (GET) and returns a promise for the response. The address is RELATIVE: the request is sent to the page’s server, [Vite], which forwards it to the server JSON;
    • lines 42–44: ATTENTION: [fetch] does not reject PAS if it receives an error response (4xx, 5xx); its promise is rejected only if the AUCUNE response does not arrive (network outage). Therefore, [reponse.ok] is checked (true for a 2xx code);
    • Line 45: [reponse.json()] reads the body and converts it from JSON (another promise). [as Captcha]: We tell [TypeScript] the format of the received data; it cannot verify this;
    • lines 50–55: an error; [AbortError]: the request was canceled; there is nothing to display;
    • Line 60: The ANNULE cleanup checks whether the effect is re-triggered or if the component disappears before a response is received. In development, [<StrictMode>] runs the effect twice at startup: the first request is canceled (the Network tab shows it as “canceled”); only the second one counts;
  • line 77: the image is a snippet of SVG, a string to be inserted like HTML. [{captcha.svg}] would display the text [<svg ...>], escaped. [dangerouslySetInnerHTML] inserts the string as-is: its name warns of the danger. Use QUE only for safe content: this SVG is generated by the NOTRE server. With user input, this would open the door to script injection;
  • Line 81: a new request; the effect is triggered again.

If the JSON server is down, the [Vite] proxy returns a 500 error: “Unable to obtain a CAPTCHA: the server responded with a 500 Internal Server Error.”

docs.title: 8.2. Example 23: Login, Cookie, and Session
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 23-connection/src/App.tsx - connect to the server RdvMedecins
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    1. On startup: GET /api/auth/moi - are we already logged in?
//       (after a F5, the client has forgotten everything; the server, however, reads the cookie);
//    2. Login: POST /api/auth/login, body JSON { login, password,
//       captchaId, captcha }. If successful, the server sets the cookie
//       httpOnly from the token JWT: our code doesn't recognize it JAMAIS (try
//       document.cookie in the console: it’s not there);
//    3. Protected request: GET /api/medecins. The browser includes the cookie
//       on its own (same origin);
//    4. Logout: POST /api/auth/logout—the server deletes the cookie.
//
// The form uses React 19’s ACTIONS: <form action={function}>.
// Instead of handling onSubmit and each field, we receive all the values
// from the form (FormData), and useActionState stores the result of the
// last action (in this case, an error message) and indicates whether it is in progress.
//
// A cookie belongs to a machine (localhost) and a path (/api): it
// is therefore common to TOUS all the examples. Once logged in here, examples
// 24 and 25 are as well.
// =========================================================================

import { useActionState, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom';

interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';
}
interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}
interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}
// the format of TOUTES the error messages in API
interface ErreurApi {
  statusCode: number;
  cle: string;
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

// the few messages this example requires (example 25 will use i18next)
const MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  'LOGIN.ERROR': 'Login ou mot de passe incorrect.',
  'ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA': "Les caractères recopiés ne correspondent pas à l'image.",
  'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS': 'Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez plus tard.',
};

// a request GET, whose response JSON is typed; an error if it is not a 2xx
async function lire<T>(url: string): Promise<T> {
  const reponse = await fetch(url);
  if (!reponse.ok) {
    throw reponse; // we "trigger" the response itself: its status will indicate what to do
  }
  return (await reponse.json()) as T;
}

// the submit button: useFormStatus() determines whether the form QUI LE CONTIENT
// is being submitted (so it must be a separate component placed inside)
function BoutonConnexion() {
  const { pending } = useFormStatus();
  return <button className="btn btn-primary" disabled={pending}>{pending ? 'Connexion...' : 'Se connecter'}</button>;
}

// the result of the last login attempt
interface EtatConnexion {
  erreur: string | null;
  login: string; // the login entered, to display it again
}

export default function App() {
  const [utilisateur, setUtilisateur] = useState<Utilisateur | null>(null);
  const [medecins, setMedecins] = useState<Medecin[]>([]);
  const [captcha, setCaptcha] = useState<Captcha | null>(null);
  const [pret, setPret] = useState(false); // Has the initial verification been completed?
  const [erreurServeur, setErreurServeur] = useState<string | null>(null);

  async function chargerCaptcha() {
    setCaptcha(await lire<Captcha>('/api/captcha'));
  }

  async function chargerMedecins() {
    setMedecins(await lire<Medecin[]>('/api/medecins'));
  }

   // 1. Who is logged in? 200 -> the user; 401 -> no one
  useEffect(() => {
    async function verifierSession() {
      try {
        setUtilisateur(await lire<Utilisateur>('/api/auth/moi'));
        await chargerMedecins();
      } catch (e) {
        if (!(e instanceof Response) || e.status !== 401) {
          setErreurServeur('Le serveur JSON RdvMedecins est-il lancé (port 8080) ?');
        } else {
          await chargerCaptcha();
        }
      }
      setPret(true);
    }
    verifierSession();
  }, []);

   // 2. The connection: a ACTION, which receives the previous status and the
   // form data, and returns the new status
  async function seConnecter(_precedent: EtatConnexion, donnees: FormData): Promise<EtatConnexion> {
    const login = String(donnees.get('login'));
    const reponse = await fetch('/api/auth/login', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, // the body is JSON
      body: JSON.stringify({ login, password: donnees.get('password'), captchaId: captcha?.id, captcha: donnees.get('captcha') }),
    });
    if (!reponse.ok) {
       // the body JSON of the error response
      const erreur = (await reponse.json().catch(() => null)) as ErreurApi | null;
      const cle = erreur?.cle ?? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE';
      await chargerCaptcha(); // Each image is used only once
      return { erreur: `${reponse.status} - ${MESSAGES[cle] ?? cle}`, login };
    }
    setUtilisateur((await reponse.json()) as Utilisateur);
    await chargerMedecins();
    return { erreur: null, login };
  }
  const [etat, actionConnexion] = useActionState(seConnecter, { erreur: null, login: 'admin' });

   // 4. Disconnection
  async function seDeconnecter() {
    await fetch('/api/auth/logout', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: '{}' });
    setUtilisateur(null);
    setMedecins([]);
    await chargerCaptcha();
  }

  let contenu;
  if (!pret) {
    contenu = <p className="text-muted">Vérification de la session...</p>;
  } else if (utilisateur) {
     // logged in
    contenu = (
      <div className="card p-3">
        <p>
          Connecté : <strong>{utilisateur.nom}</strong> ({utilisateur.login}), rôle{' '}
          <span className="badge text-bg-primary">{utilisateur.role}</span>
        </p>
        <h2 className="h6">GET /api/medecins</h2>
        <ul>
          {medecins.map((m) => <li key={m.id}>{m.titre} {m.prenom} {m.nom}</li>)}
        </ul>
        <p className="small text-muted">Rechargez la page (F5) : vous restez connecté.</p>
        <button className="btn btn-outline-secondary align-self-start" onClick={seDeconnecter}>Se déconnecter</button>
      </div>
    );
  } else if (!erreurServeur) {
     // not logged in: the form. The fields are not PAS validated: name
     // identifies them in FormData; after each action, React resets them to
     // their initial value (defaultValue)
    contenu = (
      <form className="card p-3" action={actionConnexion}>
        <div className="mb-2">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="login">Login</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" className="form-control" autoComplete="username" defaultValue={etat.login} />
        </div>
        <div className="mb-2">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="password">Mot de passe</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" className="form-control" autoComplete="current-password" />
        </div>
        <div className="mb-3">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="captcha">Recopiez les caractères de l'image</label>
          <div className="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
            <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: captcha?.svg ?? '' }} />
            <button type="button" className="btn btn-link btn-sm" onClick={chargerCaptcha}>Autre image</button>
          </div>
          <input id="captcha" name="captcha" className="form-control" autoComplete="off" />
        </div>
        <BoutonConnexion />
        <p className="small text-muted mt-2 mb-0">Comptes : admin, pelissier, martin... (mot de passe = login).</p>
        {etat.erreur && <div className="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">{etat.erreur}</div>}
      </form>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 23 - connexion au serveur</h1>
      {contenu}
      {erreurServeur && <div className="alert alert-danger mt-3">{erreurServeur}</div>}
    </div>
  );
}

The flow (lines 4–12): Upon startup, the server is queried to determine which one is connected; then comes the connection, a secure request, and logout.

  • Lines 27–47: several instances of API, including the error messages generated by TOUTES;
  • lines 50–54: the few messages this example needs to translate the server’s keys (Example 25 will use [i18next]);
  • lines 57–63: a small generic function for requests GET: the response JSON, with a type; and, if it is not a 2xx, we “trigger” the response itself: its status will indicate what to do;
  • lines 67–70: the form submission button. [useFormStatus()] (from [react-dom]) indicates whether the form QUI LE CONTIENT is currently being submitted: so this must be a separate component placed within the form;
  • Lines 94–109: On startup, [GET /api/auth/moi]: Are we already logged in? After a F5, the client has forgotten everything; the server, however, reads the cookie. 200: the user; 401: no one (a CAPTCHA is then loaded); anything else: the server does not respond. A [async] function cannot be the effect itself (an effect returns its cleanup, not a promise): we declare it within the effect, then call it;
  • lines 113–130: the connection, written as an action of [React] 19 (see below). It receives the previous state and the form data ([FormData]), and returns the new state:
    • line 114: [donnees.get(nom)] reads a field from the form, identified by its attribute [name];
    • lines 115–119: [POST /api/auth/login], with a body JSON: [method], the header [Content-Type], and the body, generated by [JSON.stringify]. If successful, the server sets the [httpOnly] cookie from the JWT token: our code does not see JAMAIS (try [document.cookie] in the console: it’s not there);
    • lines 120–126: a failure: the body of the error response, JSON, provides the message key; each CAPTCHA image is used only once: another one is loaded;
    • lines 127–129: a success: the user, followed by a protected request, [GET /api/medecins]: the browser automatically includes the cookie (same origin);
  • line 131: [useActionState(action, étatInitial)] ([React] 19) returns the status generated by the last execution of the action, and a version of the action to be passed to the form;
  • lines 134–139: logout; [POST /api/auth/logout]: the server deletes the cookie. Every POST must have a JSON body (the server rejects others; see the previous chapter): ['{}'];
  • line 165: [<form action={fonction}>]: starting with [React] 19, a form’s [action] attribute can accept a function. Upon submission, [React] prevents the browser from submitting the form, consolidates the fields into a [FormData], and calls the function, during which [useFormStatus] displays “in progress.” [onSubmit], [preventDefault], and a per-field status are no longer needed;
  • Lines 168–180: The fields are not checked: PAS refers to them in [name]. After each action, [React] resets the form: each field reverts to its initial value ([defaultValue]). The password and CAPTCHA fields are therefore cleared; the login field reverts to the value stored in the state by the action ([etat.login]), that is, the one that was just entered;
  • line 184: the error message generated by the last action.

A cookie belongs to a machine (localhost) and a path ([/api]): it is therefore shared with TOUS in the examples. Once logged in here, examples 24 and 25 are also logged in.

An incorrect password: the login is retained, and a new image is displayed:

Logged in as [admin]; you can reload the page (F5): you remain logged in:

// =========================================================================
// common/types.ts - the JSON objects exchanged with the API RdvMedecins
// (see the chapter on the black box, which describes each route)
// =========================================================================

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/moi
export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: Role;
}

// GET /api/captcha
export interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

// a doctor or a client (GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients...)
export interface Personne {
  id: number;
  version: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  login?: string; // only for ADMIN
}

export interface Identite {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}

// a row from GET /api/agenda
export interface CreneauAgenda {
  id: number;
  hdebut: number;
  mdebut: number;
  hfin: number;
  mfin: number;
  libre: boolean;
  patient: Identite | null;
  moi: boolean;
  reservable: boolean;
  idRv: number | null;
}

// GET /api/calendar?idMedecin=...&day=...
export interface Agenda {
  medecin: Personne;
  jour: string;
  creneaux: CreneauAgenda[];
  info: string | null;
}

The translation, in [TypeScript] interfaces, of the API described in the previous chapter. A line in the calendar ([CreneauAgenda]) describes a time slot (ET) and what the logged-in user is authorized to do with it.

docs.title: 8.3.2. Errors
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// common/erreur-api.ts - UNE class for all errors from API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All error responses from the RdvMedecins server have the same format:
//    { "statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN", "params": {...}, "fields": {...} }
// But a request can also fail (AUTREMENT): no response at all
// (network down: fetch sends a TypeError), or a response that doesn’t come
// from our server (a Vite proxy error page when the
// JSON server is down). We convert all of this to the UNE class,
// ErreurApi, which contains the translation key sent by the server (and,
// if any, its parameters, and the error for each field).
// =========================================================================

export class ErreurApi extends Error {
  readonly statusCode: number; // 0: the server did not respond
  readonly cle: string; // e.g., 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
  readonly params: Record<string, string>;
  readonly champs: Record<string, string>;

  constructor(statusCode: number, cle: string, params: Record<string, string> = {}, champs: Record<string, string> = {}) {
    super(cle);
    this.name = 'ErreurApi';
    this.statusCode = statusCode;
    this.cle = cle;
    this.params = params;
    this.champs = champs;
  }
}

// an error response (4xx, 5xx) -> a ErreurApi
export async function depuisReponse(reponse: Response): Promise<ErreurApi> {
   // the body of the error (JSON), if it exists and is in the correct format
  let corps: { cle?: string; params?: Record<string, string>; champs?: Record<string, string> } = {};
  try {
    const json: unknown = await reponse.json();
    if (typeof json === 'object' && json !== null) {
      corps = json;
    }
  } catch {
     // not JSON: our server did not respond
  }
   // no key: the proxy or network responded instead
  const cle = corps.cle ?? (reponse.status >= 500 ? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE' : 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR');
  return new ErreurApi(reponse.status, cle, corps.params, corps.champs);
}
  • Lines 14–28: UNE class for all errors in API: the status HTTP (0: no response), the translation key sent by the server, its parameters, and the error for each field in a rejected form. It inherits from [Error]: it can be launched ([throw]) and recognized ([instanceof ErreurApi]). The “property parameters” of [TypeScript] ([constructor(public readonly cle: string)]) are not used: the [erasableSyntaxOnly] option of [tsconfig.json] disables them, because they generate code;
  • Lines 31–45: An error response becomes a [ErreurApi]. The body is not always from our server’s JSON: when the JSON server is down, the [Vite] proxy responds without a JSON body. No key: a status code of 500 or higher means “server unreachable.”

docs.title: 8.3.3. Requests
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// common/api.ts - requests to API, on a single line
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// In Example 23, each request repeated the same steps: prefix
// /api, header JSON, test of response.ok, reading the error body... We
// group them here:
//
//    const doctors = await api.get<Person[]>('/doctors');
//    await api.post('/appointments', { day, idCreneau, idClient });
//
//    - if successful, the promise returns the body JSON, TYPÉ;
//    - if it fails, it is REJETÉE with a ErreurApi.
// All requests pass through the `requete` function: this is where
// where a problem such as COMMUN would be handled for all of them (see the case study and the
// 401 response). Used in Examples 24 and 25.
// =========================================================================

import { depuisReponse, ErreurApi } from './erreur-api';

export async function requete<T>(methode: string, url: string, corps?: unknown): Promise<T> {
  let reponse: Response;
  try {
    reponse = await fetch(`/api${url}`, {
      method: methode,
       // a body JSON (the server rejects a POST that is not a body)
      headers: corps === undefined ? {} : { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: corps === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(corps),
    });
  } catch {
     // fetch did not receive a AUCUNE response (network, server down)
    throw new ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
  }
  if (!reponse.ok) {
    throw await depuisReponse(reponse);
  }
  return (await reponse.json()) as T;
}

export const api = {
  get: <T>(url: string) => requete<T>('GET', url),
   // A POST always has a JSON body: {} by default
  post: <T>(url: string, corps: unknown = {}) => requete<T>('POST', url, corps),
  put: <T>(url: string, corps: unknown) => requete<T>('PUT', url, corps),
  delete: <T>(url: string, corps?: unknown) => requete<T>('DELETE', url, corps),
};
  • lines 20–37: TOUTES—requests pass through this generic function:
    • lines 23–28: the prefix [/api], and, if there is a body, the header and JSON;
    • lines 29–32: no response: a [ErreurApi] with status 0;
    • lines 33–35: an error response: a [ErreurApi];
    • line 36: a success: the body, typed;
  • lines 39–45: shortcuts, a function per method HTTP. A POST always has a body JSON: [{}] by default.

This is where a COMMUN issue would be handled for all requests: the case study will address the 401 response (session expired) here.

docs.title: 8.3.4. A login bar
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// common/BarreConnexion.tsx - log in/log out, in a single bar
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The form from Example 23, reduced to a single bar and rewritten using api.ts.
// The component calls onUtilisateurChange with the logged-in user (or
// null) every time the user changes—including at startup, after
// querying GET /api/auth/me.
// =========================================================================

import { useEffect, useEffectEvent, useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import { api } from './api';
import { ErreurApi } from './erreur-api';
import type { Captcha, Utilisateur } from './types';
import './BarreConnexion.css';

interface Props {
  onUtilisateurChange: (utilisateur: Utilisateur | null) => void;
}

export default function BarreConnexion({ onUtilisateurChange }: Props) {
  const [utilisateur, setUtilisateur] = useState<Utilisateur | null>(null);
  const [captcha, setCaptcha] = useState<Captcha | null>(null);
  const [login, setLogin] = useState('admin');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const [reponseCaptcha, setReponseCaptcha] = useState('');
  const [erreur, setErreur] = useState<string | null>(null);

  function changer(u: Utilisateur | null) {
    setUtilisateur(u);
    onUtilisateurChange(u);
  }

  async function nouveauCaptcha() {
    setCaptcha(await api.get<Captcha>('/captcha'));
    setReponseCaptcha('');
  }

   // at startup: are we already logged in?
  const demarrer = useEffectEvent(async () => {
    try {
      changer(await api.get<Utilisateur>('/auth/moi'));
    } catch {
      changer(null); // 401: No one is logged in
      await nouveauCaptcha().catch(() => setErreur('Le serveur JSON est-il lancé (port 8080) ?'));
    }
  });
  useEffect(() => {
    demarrer();
  }, []);

  async function seConnecter(e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setErreur(null);
    try {
      const u = await api.post<Utilisateur>('/auth/login', { login, password, captchaId: captcha?.id, captcha: reponseCaptcha });
      setPassword('');
      changer(u);
    } catch (err) {
      setErreur(err instanceof ErreurApi ? `${err.statusCode} ${err.cle}` : String(err));
      await nouveauCaptcha();
    }
  }

  async function seDeconnecter() {
    await api.post('/auth/logout');
    changer(null);
    await nouveauCaptcha();
  }

  return (
    <div className="alert alert-secondary d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 py-2">
      {utilisateur ? (
        <>
          <span>
            Connecté : <strong>{utilisateur.nom}</strong> <span className="badge text-bg-primary ms-1">{utilisateur.role}</span>
          </span>
          <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary ms-auto" onClick={seDeconnecter}>Se déconnecter</button>
        </>
      ) : (
        <form className="d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 w-100" onSubmit={seConnecter}>
          <input className="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="login" autoComplete="username" value={login}
                 onChange={(e) => setLogin(e.target.value)} />
          <input type="password" className="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="mot de passe"
                 autoComplete="current-password" value={password} onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)} />
          {/* the captcha image SVG, generated by the NOTRE server (see example 22) */}
          <div className="barre-captcha" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: captcha?.svg ?? '' }} />
          <input className="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="captcha" autoComplete="off" size={8}
                 value={reponseCaptcha} onChange={(e) => setReponseCaptcha(e.target.value)} />
          <button className="btn btn-sm btn-primary">Se connecter</button>
          {erreur && <span className="text-danger small">{erreur}</span>}
        </form>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

The form from Example 23, reduced to a bar and rewritten using [api.ts] (and with validated fields, for comparison):

  • line 17: the component notifies its parent whenever the logged-in user changes;
  • lines 39–46 and 47–49: on startup, [GET /api/auth/moi]. The function called by the effect notifies the parent: [useEffectEvent] avoids making this a dependency (see Example 13);
  • line 55: a one-line request; if it fails, a [ErreurApi];
  • line 86: the CAPTCHA image, scaled to the height of the bar using a small stylesheet:
/* The CAPTCHA image SVG, inserted as-is into the page: we resize it
   à la hauteur de la barre. Une feuille de style importée s'applique à
   TOUTE la page : la classe .barre-captcha la limite à notre élément. */
.barre-captcha svg {
  display: block;
  height: 32px;
  width: auto;
}

docs.title: 8.3.5. The access layer to the API
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 24-layer-api/src/rdvmedecins.ts - the access layer to API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A typed function per route of the API. The components are not aware of
// the URL, fetch, or the JSON format: they call functions.
// This is the client-side equivalent of the server-side DAO layer: if the API
// changes (a URL, a field name), only this file is modified.
// =========================================================================

import { api } from '../../commun/api';
import type { Agenda, Personne } from '../../commun/types';

export const rdvmedecins = {
  getMedecins: () => api.get<Personne[]>('/medecins'),
  getClients: () => api.get<Personne[]>('/clients'),
   // URLSearchParams generates "idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15" by encoding the necessary data
  getAgenda: (idMedecin: number, jour: string) =>
    api.get<Agenda>(`/agenda?${new URLSearchParams({ idMedecin: String(idMedecin), jour })}`),
  reserver: (jour: string, idCreneau: number, idClient?: number) =>
    api.post<{ id: number }>('/rendez-vous', { jour, idCreneau, idClient }),
  annuler: (idRv: number) => api.delete<Record<string, never>>(`/rendez-vous/${idRv}`),
};

A function per route of the API, typed. The components do not recognize URL, [fetch], or the JSON format: they call functions. This is the client-side equivalent of the DAO layer on the server side: if the API changes (a URL, a field name), only this file is modified. [URLSearchParams] (line 18) generates the [idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15] portion of an address by encoding the necessary data.

docs.title: 8.3.6. TanStack Query
docs.text:
Reading data from a server into an effect, as in Example 22, requires handling everything: the “in progress” status, errors, stale responses, cancellations, duplicate requests sent twice, and data already received that could be reused... [TanStack Query] (formerly [React Query]), the most widely used library for this purpose, handles all of this.

// =========================================================================
// 24-couche-api/src/main.tsx
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// TanStack Query (formerly React Query): the most
// used to LIRE retrieve data from a server in a React application.
// It caches responses that have already been received;
// <QueryClientProvider> makes it available to the entire application (a context,
// see Example 14).
// =========================================================================

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App';

const queryClient = new QueryClient({
   // in case of failure, no retry: we want to see the error
  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } },
});

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <App />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  </StrictMode>,
);
  • line 17: the [TanStack Query] client, which stores previously received responses in memory (in the “cache”); [retry: false]: in case of failure, no retry (by default, it attempts three);
  • line 24: it is provided to the entire application via a context (see Example 14).

docs.title: 8.3.7. The page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 24-couche-api/src/App.tsx - a calendar, with the API access layer
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Log in (top bar), choose a doctor and a date: the calendar
// is displayed. ADMIN and DOCTOR can make appointments for a patient and cancel them;
// a patient (Martin...) makes an appointment for themselves. Each action ends with
// a refresh of the calendar: SERVEUR is the definitive version.
//
// useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn }): a LECTURE of data, described by
//    - queryFn: the function that retrieves it (a promise);
//    - queryKey: what IDENTIFIE this data: ['agenda', idMedecin, jour].
// TanStack The query first calls queryFn, then every time the key
// CHANGE (another doctor, another day). It returns an object: data (the
// response), isPending, isFetching, error... and refetch() to retrieve the data again.
// It also handles what needs to be written manually with useEffect: cancel
// an expired response, avoid sending the same request twice, and keep
// responses in the cache.
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import BarreConnexion from '../../commun/BarreConnexion';
import { ErreurApi } from '../../commun/erreur-api';
import type { CreneauAgenda, Utilisateur } from '../../commun/types';
import { rdvmedecins } from './rdvmedecins';

function demain(): string {
  const d = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 3600 * 1000);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function horaire(c: CreneauAgenda): string {
  const hm = (h: number, m: number) => `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
  return `${hm(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${hm(c.hfin, c.mfin)}`;
}

// an error -> a text (its key, since there’s no dictionary here)
function texteErreur(e: unknown): string {
  return e instanceof ErreurApi ? `${e.statusCode} ${e.cle}` : String(e);
}

export default function App() {
  const [utilisateur, setUtilisateur] = useState<Utilisateur | null>(null);
  const [idMedecin, setIdMedecin] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [jour, setJour] = useState(demain);
  const [idClient, setIdClient] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [message, setMessage] = useState<{ type: 'success' | 'danger'; texte: string } | null>(null);

  const connecte = utilisateur !== null;
  const gestionnaire = connecte && utilisateur.role !== 'USER';

   // doctors, then (ADMIN, DOCTOR) clients: re-read when
   // the user changes (it is part of the key)
  const medecins = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['medecins', utilisateur?.login],
    queryFn: rdvmedecins.getMedecins,
    enabled: connecte, // false: no request (no one logged in)
  });
  const clients = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['clients', utilisateur?.login],
    queryFn: rdvmedecins.getClients,
    enabled: gestionnaire, // a USER would receive a 403
  });

   // the schedule: the key contains the doctor and the day
  const agenda = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['agenda', idMedecin, jour, utilisateur?.login],
    queryFn: () => rdvmedecins.getAgenda(idMedecin!, jour),
    enabled: connecte && idMedecin !== null,
  });

   // Selecting a new doctor or day clears the previous message
  function choisirMedecin(id: number) {
    setIdMedecin(id);
    setMessage(null);
  }
  function choisirJour(j: string) {
    setJour(j);
    setMessage(null);
  }

  async function reserver(c: CreneauAgenda) {
    try {
      await rdvmedecins.reserver(jour, c.id, gestionnaire ? (idClient ?? undefined) : undefined);
      setMessage({ type: 'success', texte: `Créneau ${horaire(c)} réservé.` });
    } catch (e) {
      setMessage({ type: 'danger', texte: texteErreur(e) });
    }
    agenda.refetch();
  }

  async function annuler(c: CreneauAgenda) {
    try {
      await rdvmedecins.annuler(c.idRv!);
      setMessage({ type: 'success', texte: `Rendez-vous de ${horaire(c)} annulé.` });
    } catch (e) {
      setMessage({ type: 'danger', texte: texteErreur(e) });
    }
    agenda.refetch();
  }

  const a = agenda.data;
  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 24 - une couche d'accès à l'API</h1>
      <BarreConnexion onUtilisateurChange={setUtilisateur} />

      {connecte && (
        <>
          <div className="row g-2 mb-3">
            <div className="col-sm-5">
              <select className="form-select" value={idMedecin ?? ''} onChange={(e) => choisirMedecin(Number(e.target.value))}>
                <option value="" disabled>-- choisir un médecin --</option>
                {medecins.data?.map((m) => <option key={m.id} value={m.id}>{m.titre} {m.prenom} {m.nom}</option>)}
              </select>
            </div>
            <div className="col-sm-3">
              <input type="date" className="form-control" value={jour} onChange={(e) => choisirJour(e.target.value)} />
            </div>
            {gestionnaire && (
              <div className="col-sm-4">
                <select className="form-select" value={idClient ?? ''}
                        onChange={(e) => setIdClient(e.target.value === '' ? null : Number(e.target.value))}>
                  <option value="">-- patient à inscrire --</option>
                  {clients.data?.map((c) => <option key={c.id} value={c.id}>{c.titre} {c.prenom} {c.nom}</option>)}
                </select>
              </div>
            )}
          </div>

          {message && <div className={`alert alert-${message.type}`}>{message.texte}</div>}
          {agenda.error && <div className="alert alert-danger">{texteErreur(agenda.error)}</div>}
          {agenda.isFetching && <p className="small text-muted">chargement de l'agenda...</p>}

          {a && (
            <>
              {/* info: the key sent by the server when a patient already has an upcoming appointment */}
              {a.info && <div className="alert alert-info">{a.info}</div>}
              <table className="table table-sm align-middle">
                <caption className="caption-top">
                  Agenda du {a.jour} - {a.medecin.titre} {a.medecin.prenom} {a.medecin.nom}
                </caption>
                <tbody>
                  {a.creneaux.map((c) => (
                    <tr key={c.id}>
                      <td>{horaire(c)}</td>
                      <td>
                        {c.libre ? (
                          <span className="badge text-bg-success">Libre</span>
                        ) : c.patient ? (
                          <span className={`badge ${c.moi ? 'text-bg-primary' : 'text-bg-secondary'}`}>
                            {c.patient.titre} {c.patient.prenom} {c.patient.nom}
                          </span>
                        ) : (
                          <span className="badge text-bg-secondary">Réservé</span>
                        )}
                      </td>
                      <td className="text-end">
                        {/* The buttons follow the permissions calculated by the server */}
                        {c.reservable && <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" onClick={() => reserver(c)}>Réserver</button>}
                        {c.idRv !== null && <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" onClick={() => annuler(c)}>Annuler</button>}
                      </td>
                    </tr>
                  ))}
                </tbody>
              </table>
            </>
          )}
        </>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 54–58: [useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn, enabled })] describes a LECTURE of data:
    • [queryFn]: the function that retrieves it, a promise;
    • [queryKey]: what IDENTIFIE returns—an array. [TanStack Query] first calls [queryFn], then calls CHANGE each time; two components that request the same key share the same request and the same response. The user is added to it: the list is reloaded when the user changes;
    • [enabled: false]: no request (no one is logged in);
    • The result is an object: [data] (the response, [undefined] until it arrives), [isPending], [isFetching] (a request is in progress), [error], and [refetch()] to be re-read;
  • lines 59–63: the patient list, only for ADMIN and DOCTOR (a USER would receive a 403);
  • lines 66–70: the schedule: the key contains the doctor and the day; changing either one sends a new request. An expired response is automatically ignored;
  • lines 82–90: a reservation: [POST /api/rendez-vous], then [agenda.refetch()]: the calendar is re-read. The SERVEUR is the authoritative one;
  • line 106: the connection bar notifies the page;
  • line 114: the doctors, if they have arrived ([?.]: nothing if [data] is [undefined]);
  • line 133: a calendar request is in progress;
  • lines 160–161: the buttons follow the permissions calculated by the server;
  • line 138: [info]: the key sent by the server when a patient already has an upcoming appointment (displayed raw: no dictionary here).

Logged in as [admin], we select Ms. PELISSIER, then a patient, and book the first time slot:

Logged in as [martin], we book a time slot: the patient sees their own name, but the name of another patient is never sent to them; the “Book” button is no longer available (only one upcoming appointment):

For transaction processing (booking, canceling), [TanStack Query] also provides [useMutation], which handles the “in progress” status and errors from modifications. We won’t use those here: a [async] function and a [try / catch] are sufficient.

docs.title: 8.4. Example 25: Errors Returned by the Server
docs.text:
Customer management ([admin] form). This form performs no validation in the browser: everything is sent to the server, which responds—in the event of a rejection—with a JSON error:

400 { cle: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM', champs: { nom: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED' } }
409 { cle: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS', champs: { prenom: ..., nom: ... } }
409 { cle: 'ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE' }         (verrou optimiste)

docs.title: 8.4.2. The page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 25-server-errors/src/App.tsx - display errors from SERVEUR
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Customer management (admin account). This form does not
// VOLONTAIREMENT perform any validation in the browser: everything is sent
// to the server, which responds, in case of rejection, with an error JSON (converted
// to ErreurApi by commun/api.ts):
//
//    400 { key: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM', fields: { name: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED' } }
//    409 { key: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS', fields: { first_name: ..., last_name: ... } }
//    409 { key: 'ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE'         } (optimistic lock)
//
// The error in the CHAQUE field (ErreurApi.champs) is logged in the status and
// displayed below the field; its message is the CLÉ sent by the server,
// which the component translates (i18next). Editing a field clears its error.
// Try: an empty name, a title "Dr.", a namesake (Alice DURAND), a
// username already taken (martin), the same record edited in two tabs...
// =========================================================================

import { useState, useTransition, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { api } from '../../commun/api';
import BarreConnexion from '../../commun/BarreConnexion';
import { ErreurApi } from '../../commun/erreur-api';
import type { Personne, Utilisateur } from '../../commun/types';
import { useConfirmation } from '../../16-confirmation/src/confirmation/confirmation';

interface SaisieClient {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  login: string;
  password: string;
  version: number;
}
type Champ = keyof SaisieClient;

const VIDE: SaisieClient = { titre: 'Mr', prenom: '', nom: '', login: '', password: '', version: 0 };

interface Message {
  cle: string;
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

export default function App() {
  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation();
  const confirmer = useConfirmation();

  const [utilisateur, setUtilisateur] = useState<Utilisateur | null>(null);
  const [clients, setClients] = useState<Personne[]>([]);
  const estAdmin = utilisateur?.role === 'ADMIN';

   // the form: idEdite === null -> creation, otherwise modification
  const [idEdite, setIdEdite] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [saisie, setSaisie] = useState<SaisieClient>(VIDE);
   // the error for each field (a translation error: CLÉ), returned by the server
  const [erreurs, setErreurs] = useState<Partial<Record<Champ, string>>>({});
   // the general message for the last error, and the success message
  const [erreurPage, setErreurPage] = useState<ErreurApi | null>(null);
  const [succes, setSucces] = useState<Message | null>(null);
   // useTransition: isPending is true during the execution of the action
   // is passed to startTransition—here, the data is sent to the server
  const [envoiEnCours, startTransition] = useTransition();

  async function recharger() {
    setClients(await api.get<Personne[]>('/clients'));
  }

  async function surConnexion(u: Utilisateur | null) {
    setUtilisateur(u);
    setClients([]);
    if (u?.role === 'ADMIN') {
      await recharger();
    }
  }

  function effacerMessages() {
    setErreurs({});
    setErreurPage(null);
    setSucces(null);
  }

  function nouveau() {
    setIdEdite(null);
    setSaisie(VIDE);
    effacerMessages();
  }

  function editer(c: Personne) {
    setIdEdite(c.id);
     // the VERSION read from the record is sent back with the modification: if someone
     // has modified the record in the meantime, the server will respond with a 409 error CONCURRENT_UPDATE
    setSaisie({ titre: c.titre, prenom: c.prenom, nom: c.nom, login: c.login ?? '', password: '', version: c.version });
    effacerMessages();
  }

   // a modified field: its value changes, its error disappears
  function modifier(champ: Champ, valeur: string) {
    setSaisie((s) => ({ ...s, [champ]: valeur }));
    setErreurs((e) => ({ ...e, [champ]: undefined }));
  }

  function enregistrer(evenement: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    evenement.preventDefault();
    effacerMessages();
     // a transition ASYNCHRONE (React 19): envoiEnCours remains true until
     // the end of the function
    startTransition(async () => {
      try {
        const client =
          idEdite === null
            ? await api.post<Personne>('/clients', saisie)
            : await api.put<Personne>(`/clients/${idEdite}`, saisie);
        nouveau(); // form cleared, messages deleted...
         // ... except for this one
        setSucces({
          cle: idEdite === null ? 'FORM.AJOUTE' : 'FORM.MODIFIE',
          params: { nom: `${client.prenom} ${client.nom}`, login: client.login ?? '' },
        });
        await recharger();
      } catch (e) {
        if (!(e instanceof ErreurApi)) {
          throw e;
        }
        setErreurPage(e); // the general message
        setErreurs(e.champs); // the error for each field
      }
    });
  }

  async function supprimer(c: Personne) {
    const nom = `${c.prenom} ${c.nom}`;
    if (!(await confirmer(t('FORM.CONFIRMER_SUPPRESSION', { nom })))) {
      return;
    }
    effacerMessages();
    try {
      await api.delete(`/clients/${c.id}`);
      setSucces({ cle: 'FORM.SUPPRIME', params: { nom } });
    } catch (e) {
      setErreurPage(e instanceof ErreurApi ? e : null);
    }
    await recharger();
  }

   // an input field, with its error message translated
  function champ(nom: 'prenom' | 'nom' | 'login' | 'password', type = 'text') {
    const erreur = erreurs[nom];
    return (
      <>
        <label className="form-label" htmlFor={nom}>{t(`FORM.${nom.toUpperCase()}`)}</label>
        <input id={nom} type={type} className={`form-control ${erreur ? 'is-invalid' : ''}`} value={saisie[nom]}
               autoComplete={type === 'password' ? 'new-password' : 'off'} onChange={(e) => modifier(nom, e.target.value)} />
        {/* a server error message is a CLÉ: let’s translate it */}
        {erreur && <div className="invalid-feedback">{t(erreur)}</div>}
      </>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <div className="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
        <h1 className="h3 mb-0">Exemple 25 - les erreurs renvoyées par le serveur</h1>
        <select className="form-select form-select-sm w-auto" value={i18n.language} onChange={(e) => i18n.changeLanguage(e.target.value)}>
          <option value="fr">FR</option>
          <option value="en">EN</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <BarreConnexion onUtilisateurChange={surConnexion} />
      {utilisateur && !estAdmin && <p className="alert alert-warning">{t('FORM.ADMIN_SEULEMENT')}</p>}

      {estAdmin && (
        <div className="row g-4">
          <div className="col-lg-6">
            <table className="table table-sm align-middle">
              <tbody>
                {clients.map((c) => (
                  <tr key={c.id}>
                    <td>{c.titre} {c.prenom} {c.nom}</td>
                    <td><code>{c.login}</code></td>
                    <td className="text-end text-nowrap">
                      <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary me-1" onClick={() => editer(c)}>{t('FORM.MODIFIER')}</button>
                      <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" onClick={() => supprimer(c)}>{t('FORM.SUPPRIMER')}</button>
                    </td>
                  </tr>
                ))}
              </tbody>
            </table>
          </div>

          <div className="col-lg-6">
            <form className="card p-3" noValidate onSubmit={enregistrer}>
              <h2 className="h5">{t(idEdite === null ? 'FORM.TITRE_AJOUT' : 'FORM.TITRE_MODIF')}</h2>
              <div className="mb-2">
                <label className="form-label" htmlFor="titre">{t('FORM.TITRE')}</label>
                {/* a "Dr" option that the server will reject: see ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE */}
                <select id="titre" className={`form-select ${erreurs.titre ? 'is-invalid' : ''}`} value={saisie.titre}
                        onChange={(e) => modifier('titre', e.target.value)}>
                  <option>Mr</option><option>Mme</option><option>Melle</option><option>Dr</option>
                </select>
                {erreurs.titre && <div className="invalid-feedback">{t(erreurs.titre)}</div>}
              </div>
              <div className="row g-2 mb-2">
                <div className="col-sm-6">{champ('prenom')}</div>
                <div className="col-sm-6">{champ('nom')}</div>
              </div>
              <div className="row g-2 mb-3">
                <div className="col-sm-6">{champ('login')}</div>
                <div className="col-sm-6">{champ('password', 'password')}</div>
              </div>
              <div className="d-flex gap-2">
                <button className="btn btn-primary" disabled={envoiEnCours}>{t('FORM.ENREGISTRER')}</button>
                <button type="button" className="btn btn-secondary" onClick={nouveau}>{t('FORM.ANNULER')}</button>
              </div>
              {succes && <div className="alert alert-success mt-3 mb-0">{t(succes.cle, succes.params)}</div>}
              {/* The general message and the status HTTP—to understand */}
              {erreurPage && (
                <div className="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">
                  {t(erreurPage.cle, erreurPage.params)}{' '}
                  <span className="small text-muted">({erreurPage.statusCode} {erreurPage.cle})</span>
                </div>
              )}
            </form>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 54–55: the form: [idEdite === null] for creating a customer, or [idEdite] for modifying a customer;
  • line 57: the error for each field, a translation form CLÉ, returned by the server;
  • line 63: [useTransition] returns a “in progress” flag and a function [startTransition(action)]. Starting with [React] 19, the action can be [async]: the indicator remains true until the end of the function, without requiring any manual handling;
  • lines 89–95: modifying a customer. The VERSION read from the master record reflects the modification: if someone has modified the master record in the meantime, the server will respond with a 409 [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE] (optimistic lock);
  • lines 98–101: a modified field: its value changes, and its error disappears;
  • lines 103–129: sending:
    • [POST /api/clients] (creation) or [PUT /api/clients/:id] (update);
    • if successful: the form is cleared, and a message is translated, along with its parameters;
    • in the case of [ErreurApi] (lines 125–126): the general message and the error for the CHAQUE field; the row as it appears in the report: [e.champs] has exactly the desired format;
  • lines 131–144: deletion, after confirmation. The confirmation message is translated by [t], with a parameter;
  • lines 147–158: a function that creates an input field with its label and error message: [t(erreur)] translates the CLÉ sent by the server;
  • line 164: language selection: the errors already displayed are retranslated, since they are keys;
  • line 199: a “Dr” option that the server will reject, resulting in [ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE];
  • line 212: the button is disabled during transmission;
  • line 219: the general message and the status HTTP, for context.

Logged in as [admin], with the title “Dr,” an empty name, and an invalid login:

A namesake (Alice Durand, who already exists) and a username already in use ([martin]): 409, and the two affected fields are flagged:

The same page in English: the server messages are translated back:

A successful addition:

Then its deletion:

To see the optimistic lock, open the same record in two tabs, save it in the first tab, then in the second: the server responds with a 409 error ([ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE]).

docs.title: 3.1. Example 10: Components and Their Props
docs.text: A component is a reusable piece of the user interface. This example creates one, [CarteMedecin], and uses it multiple times.

docs.title: 3.1.1. Data Type
docs.text:
// the data type shared by the parent (App) and the child (CarteMedecin)
export interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  specialite: string;
  disponible: boolean;
}

The type [Medecin] is shared by the parent and child: it is stored in a separate module.

docs.title: 3.1.2. The child
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 10-components/src/CarteMedecin.tsx - a component ENFANT
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It receives its data from its parent via PROPS (properties): the
// attributes written by the parent to <CarteMedecin ... />, grouped by
// React into a UN object, the first parameter of the function. Their type is
// checked at compile time: <CarteMedecin doctor={42} /> would be rejected.
//
// Golden rule: a component does not MODIFIE JAMAIS its props. The data
// flows from the parent to the child; to request a change,
// the child calls a function passed to it by the parent (see Example 11).
// =========================================================================

import type { Medecin } from './medecin';
// styles: an object { initials: '_initiales_x7f3a_1' } - the actual name of each class
import styles from './CarteMedecin.module.css';

// the type of props: what the parent PEUT (?) or DOIT provides
interface Props {
  medecin: Medecin;
  rang: number;
  compact?: boolean; // optional
}

// the object is "unpacked" from the props; compact = false: its default value
export default function CarteMedecin({ medecin, rang, compact = false }: Props) {
   // a value calculated from the props: recalculated if the parent changes them
  const initiales = `${medecin.prenom[0]}${medecin.nom[0]}`;

  return (
    <div className={`card h-100 ${medecin.disponible ? 'border-success' : ''}`}>
      <div className="card-body d-flex gap-3 align-items-center">
        <div className={styles.initiales}>{initiales}</div>
        <div>
          <h2 className="h6 mb-1">{rang}. {medecin.titre} {medecin.prenom} {medecin.nom}</h2>
          {!compact && <p className="mb-0 text-muted small">{medecin.specialite}</p>}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • line 14: a type import only;
  • line 16: an import of the CSS module (see below);
  • lines 19–23: the component’s prop types—the attributes that the parent writes to [<CarteMedecin ... />]. [compact?] is optional;
  • line 26: [React] combines the props into a UN object, which it passes as the first parameter to the function. It is immediately “unpacked”: [{ medecin, rang, compact = false }] yields three variables, with [compact] being equal to [false] if the parent does not provide it. The type of the props is checked at compile time: [<CarteMedecin medecin={42} />] would be rejected, as would the omission of [rang];
  • line 28: a value calculated from the props: if the parent changes the props, the component is re-invoked and the value is recalculated;
  • line 33: the class CSS, read from the module CSS;
  • line 36: the specialty is displayed only in normal mode.

Golden rule: a component never modifies its own props. Data flows from the parent to the child; to request a change, the child calls a function passed to it by the parent (see Example 11).

docs.title: 3.1.3. A CSS module
docs.text:
/* a "CSS module" (*.module.css file): Quickly renames each class
   (.initiales -> ._initiales_x7f3a_1) ; elle ne peut donc s'appliquer qu'aux
   éléments du composant qui l'importe */
.initiales {
  width: 2.5rem;
  height: 2.5rem;
  border-radius: 50%;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background: #087ea4;
  color: white;
  font-weight: bold;
}

A file whose name ends with [.module.css] is a CSS module: [Vite] renames each of its classes ([.initiales] becomes, for example, [._initiales_x7f3a_1]) and, upon import, provides an object that associates the original name with the actual name: [styles.initiales]. The class can therefore only be applied to elements of the component that imports it: this is equivalent to the style encapsulation in [Angular]. The classes in [Bootstrap], which are global, remain usable everywhere.

// =========================================================================
// 10-components/src/App.tsx - the PARENT component
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It imports the CarteMedecin component and uses it as a new
// tag, <CarteMedecin />, as many times as necessary: a component is
// a piece of the RÉUTILISABLE interface, with its own data, its JSX, and
// style. A tag that begins with a MAJUSCULE is a component;
// in lowercase (<div>, <p>), it is an element HTML.
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';
import CarteMedecin from './CarteMedecin';
import type { Medecin } from './medecin';

export default function App() {
  const [medecins, setMedecins] = useState<Medecin[]>([
    { id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
    { id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre', disponible: false },
    { id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
  ]);
  const [compact, setCompact] = useState(false);

   // the parent modifies SES data: React notifies the parent, then the
   // children, along with their new props
  function inverserDisponibilite() {
    setMedecins((liste) => liste.map((m) => ({ ...m, disponible: !m.disponible })));
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 10 - les composants et leurs props</h1>
      <div className="d-flex gap-3 mb-3">
        <label className="form-check-label">
          <input type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={compact}
                 onChange={(e) => setCompact(e.target.checked)} /> affichage compact
        </label>
        <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" onClick={inverserDisponibilite}>Inverser les disponibilités</button>
      </div>
      <div className="row g-3">
        {medecins.map((m, i) => (
          <div key={m.id} className="col-md-4">
            {/* doctor={m} passes the OBJET m (an expression);
                medecin="m", sans accolades, transmettrait la CHAÎNE "m" */}
            <CarteMedecin medecin={m} rang={i + 1} compact={compact} />
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className="mt-3 mb-1 small text-muted">La même carte, en version compacte, par un attribut sans valeur :</p>
      <div className="w-50">
        {/* compact, which has no value, is true */}
        <CarteMedecin medecin={medecins[0]} rang={1} compact />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • line 12: the child component is imported like any other module;
  • lines 25–27: the parent modifies SES data. [React] re-renders it, then re-renders the children with their new props: the maps update;
  • line 44: the component is used as a new tag. [medecin={m}] passes OBJET to [m] (an expression); [medecin="m"], without curly braces, would pass the CHAÎNE “m”;
  • line 51: an attribute without a value ([compact]) is equal to [true].

docs.text: Data flows down through the props. To send information back up, the parent passes functions to the child, which the child then calls.

docs.title: 3.2.1. "Events" from the child
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 11-retrieve-the-information/src/Compteur.tsx
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A child that PRÉVIENT its parent: the parent passes it FONCTIONS
// in their props (by convention, their names begin with "on"), and the child
// calls them when something happens:
//      <Counter label="Coffees" max={3} onIncremente={...} onLimite={...} />
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';

interface Props {
  libelle: string;
  max: number;
  onIncremente: (valeur: number) => void; // with the new value
  onLimite: () => void; // with no data
}

export default function Compteur({ libelle, max, onIncremente, onLimite }: Props) {
   // the status PROPRE for this counter: each <Counter> has its own
  const [valeur, setValeur] = useState(0);

  function plus() {
    if (valeur >= max) {
      onLimite();
      return;
    }
    setValeur(valeur + 1);
     // value has not yet been updated (it will be on the next call to the
     // component): the value is sent as +1
    onIncremente(valeur + 1);
  }

  return (
    <div className="d-flex align-items-center gap-2 mb-2">
      <span className="w-25">{libelle}</span>
      <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" onClick={plus}>+1</button>
      <span className="badge text-bg-secondary">{valeur} / {max}</span>
    </div>
  );
}
  • Lines 12–17: Two props are functions: [onIncremente] receives the new value, while [onLimite] receives nothing. By convention, their names begin with “on,” such as [onClick];
  • Line 21: The state PROPRE for this counter: each [<Compteur>] on the page has its own. The state is attached to the component’s position in the page tree;
  • lines 23–32: the parent is notified. Note: [setValeur(valeur + 1)] does not change the variable [valeur] (a constant set to CET when the component is called): it will be [valeur + 1] at the time of the PROCHAIN call. Therefore, [valeur + 1] is passed to the parent.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 11-report-the-information/src/ChampTexte.tsx - a CONTRÔLÉ component
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "custom" form field (label + field + tooltip + character counter
// ) that is used as a controlled <input> (see example 05):
//      <ChampTexte value={name} onChange={setNom} label="Name" max={20} />
// The component has no status: the value belongs to the parent, which passes it to the component
// (value) and notifies it of every keystroke (onChange). It is the
// parent that decides on the new value.
// =========================================================================

import { useId } from 'react';

interface Props {
  valeur: string;
  onChange: (valeur: string) => void;
  libelle: string;
  max: number;
  aide?: string;
}

export default function ChampTexte({ valeur, onChange, libelle, max, aide = '' }: Props) {
   // useId: an identifier UNIQUE, which is different for each <ChampTexte> on the
   // page, to link <label htmlFor> and <input id>
  const id = useId();

  return (
    <div className="mb-3">
      <label className="form-label" htmlFor={id}>{libelle}</label>
      <input id={id} className={`form-control ${valeur.length === max ? 'is-invalid' : ''}`} value={valeur}
             maxLength={max} onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)} />
      <div className="form-text">{aide} ({valeur.length} / {max})</div>
    </div>
  );
}

A “custom” form field (label, field, tooltip, character counter) that is used as a controlled [<input>] (see Example 05): the parent passes it the value ([valeur]) and a function called with each keystroke ([onChange]).

  • lines 14–20: the props; [aide] is optional;
  • line 25: [useId()] provides a unique identifier, different for each [<ChampTexte>] on the page, to link [<label htmlFor>] and [<input id>];
  • line 31: Each keystroke calls the parent’s function with the new text.

The component has no state: the value belongs to the parent, which determines the new value. This is called “propagating state”: data shared by multiple components is stored in their closest common ancestor.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 11-send-information-back/src/App.tsx - the parent listens to its children
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Data flows down (props); information flows back up via
// functions passed in the props:
//    1. "events" from the child: onIncremente, onLimite;
//    2. a controlled component: value + onChange, such as a <input>. The state
//       remains the property of the parent, which can modify it itself (Clear).
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';
import Compteur from './Compteur';
import ChampTexte from './ChampTexte';

export default function App() {
  const [total, setTotal] = useState(0);
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('');
  const [prenom, setPrenom] = useState('Marie');
  const [nom, setNom] = useState('PELISSIER');

   // the function called by a counter: it receives the value that the counter passes
  function surIncremente(libelle: string, valeur: number) {
    setTotal((t) => t + 1);
    setMessage(`${libelle} vaut maintenant ${valeur}`);
  }

  function vider() {
    setPrenom('');
    setNom('');
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 11 - l'enfant prévient son parent</h1>

      <div className="card p-3 mb-4">
        <h2 className="h6">1. Des fonctions appelées par les enfants</h2>
        <Compteur libelle="Cafés" max={3} onIncremente={(v) => surIncremente('Cafés', v)}
                  onLimite={() => setMessage('Pas plus de 3 cafés !')} />
        <Compteur libelle="Verres d'eau" max={8} onIncremente={(v) => surIncremente("Verres d'eau", v)}
                  onLimite={() => setMessage('Assez bu.')} />
        <p className="mb-0">Total des clics : {total} - <em>{message}</em></p>
      </div>

      <div className="card p-3">
        <h2 className="h6">2. Des composants contrôlés</h2>
        {/* onChange={setPrenom}: the state’s function, passed as-is */}
        <ChampTexte valeur={prenom} onChange={setPrenom} libelle="Prénom" max={20} aide="Obligatoire" />
        <ChampTexte valeur={nom} onChange={setNom} libelle="Nom" max={20} aide="Mis en majuscules à l'affichage" />
        <p className="mb-0">Données du parent : <strong>{prenom} {nom.toUpperCase()}</strong></p>
        <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary mt-2 align-self-start" onClick={vider}>Vider (depuis le parent)</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 22–25: the function called by a counter; it receives the value the counter passes to it;
  • lines 38–39: the parent passes arrow functions, which add the counter’s label;
  • line 48: [onChange={setPrenom}]: the report function is passed as-is; the child calls it with the new text;
  • line 51: the parent modifies the values itself; the fields follow.

docs.text: Props pass data... but also content: "JSX" is a value just like any other (such as "[ReactNode]"), which can be passed to a component, and the component can place it wherever it wants.

docs.title: 3.3.1. A card
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 12-composition/src/Carte.tsx - a reusable GABARIT
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Props pass DONNÉES... but also CONTENU: JSX is
// a value like any other (of type ReactNode), which can be passed to a
// component, which places it wherever it wants:
//    - children: the special property that receives whatever the parent writes ENTRE
//                 <Map> and </Map>—the “main” content;
//    - header, footer: other sections, provided by the parent as
//                 the form of props; the header has default content.
// The card defines the frame (border, header, footer); the parent provides
// content inside it. This is the client-side equivalent of the template layout.hbs
// and its {{{body}}} in the NestJS course.
// =========================================================================

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

interface Props {
  couleur?: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger';
  entete?: ReactNode;
  pied?: ReactNode;
  children: ReactNode;
}

export default function Carte({ couleur, entete = 'Sans titre', pied, children }: Props) {
  return (
    <div className={`card mb-3 ${couleur ? `border-${couleur}` : ''}`}>
      <div className={`card-header ${couleur ? `text-bg-${couleur}` : ''}`}>{entete}</div>
      <div className="card-body">{children}</div>
      {/* no footer provided: no footer at all */}
      {pied && <div className="card-footer text-muted small">{pied}</div>}
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 18–23: [entete], [pied], and [children] are [ReactNode]: JSX, text, a number, or nothing;
  • line 25: default content;
  • line 29: [children] is a special property: it receives whatever the parent writes in ENTRE, [<Carte>], and [</Carte>]—the “main” content;
  • line 31: no footer provided—no footer at all.

The template defines the framework (border, header, footer); the parent provides the content inside it: this is equivalent to the content projection of [Angular] ([<ng-content>]) and the “slots” of [Vue.js], and, on the server side, the template [layout.hbs] and its [{{{body}}}] within the course [NestJS].

docs.title: 3.3.2. A generic table
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 12-composition/src/Tableau.tsx - a table GÉNÉRIQUE
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Array<T> is a generic component: it displays rows of
// of any type T. It knows how to iterate through the rows, but not how
// display UNE a row: the parent tells it how by passing it a
// FONCTION, renderLigne(row, index), which returns the JSX of the cells.
// This is what’s called a “render prop”: the content provided by the
// parent uses data belonging to the child (the row, its
// rank).
// =========================================================================

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

interface Props<T> {
  lignes: T[];
  colonnes: string[];
  renderLigne: (ligne: T, index: number) => ReactNode;
  vide?: ReactNode; // displayed when there are no rows
}

// <T extends { id: number }>: each row must have an id (the key)
export default function Tableau<T extends { id: number }>({ lignes, colonnes, renderLigne, vide = 'Aucune donnée.' }: Props<T>) {
  return (
    <table className="table table-sm align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          {colonnes.map((c) => <th key={c}>{c}</th>)}
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {lignes.length === 0 ? (
          <tr>
            <td className="text-muted" colSpan={colonnes.length}>{vide}</td>
          </tr>
        ) : (
          lignes.map((l, i) => <tr key={l.id}>{renderLigne(l, i)}</tr>)
        )}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
  • lines 15–20: a generic type: the props of an array of lines of type [T], whatever they may be;
  • line 18: a prop that is a function returning JSX: the array knows how to iterate over the rows, but not how to display UNE per row; the parent tells it how. This process is called a “render prop”;
  • line 23: a generic component: [T] is inferred at runtime from the type of the rows. Each row must have a [id], which serves as a key;
  • line 37: For each line, the array calls the parent’s function, passing it data that belongs to it (the line, its index).
