docs.text:
In the console open to the [exemples-react] folder:

npm start 01-premiere-application

The console displays:

> exemples-react@1.0.0 start
> vite --config vite.config.ts 01-premiere-application

  VITE v8.3.1  ready in 400 ms

  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
  ➜  Network: use --host to expose

Open the URL http://localhost:5173/ and click the button three times:

Two experiments to try:

  • Change the title text in [App.tsx] and save the file: the page updates immediately, without having to reload it, and the counter retains its value. The development server monitors the files, recompiles the changes, and notifies the browser;
  • view the page’s source code (Ctrl-U): you’ll only find the [index.html] page, which is almost empty. The HTML page displayed was generated by [React] within the browser. To view it, use the developer tools inspector (F12, Elements tab) or the [React Developer Tools] extension, which also displays the components and their status.

docs.title: 2.2. Example 02: State and Calculated Values
docs.text:
The state is at the heart of [React]. This example calculates the price TTC of an item:

// =========================================================================
// 02-status/src/App.tsx - status, calculated values, useEffect
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A small price calculator TTC:
//    - useStat   e : a value from ÉTAT; changing it (setXxx) triggers
//                    the component, which renders the page with the new value;
//    - a value of CALCULÉE from the state is not PAS a state: it is a
//      simple variable, recalculated each time the component is called;
//    - useMem    o : the same thing, but the calculation is only redone if its
//                    dependencies have changed (useful for a computationally expensive calculation);
//    - useEffec  t : code executed when the display is updated, when certain
//                    values have changed: a "side effect" (affecting something other
//                    thing other than the page: in this case, the tab title).
// =========================================================================

import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';

// a formatter for euro amounts, in the French style (1,234.50 €)
const euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

export default function App() {
  const [libelle, setLibelle] = useState('Stylo');
  const [prixHT, setPrixHT] = useState(2.5);
  const [quantite, setQuantite] = useState(1);
  const [tauxTVA, setTauxTVA] = useState(20); // as a percentage

   // values from CALCULÉES: simple constants, recalculated with each
   // call to the component. They are always up to date, with nothing to synchronize
  const totalHT = quantite * prixHT;
  const montantTVA = (totalHT * tauxTVA) / 100;
   // useMemo (calculation, [dépendances]): same result, but React only recalculates
   // recalculation unless one of the dependencies has changed since the previous call
  const totalTTC = useMemo(() => totalHT + montantTVA, [totalHT, montantTVA]);

   // the history of the totals TTC: it depends on the values SUCCESSIVES of the
   // total. The old total is stored in the report; if it differs from the
   // new one, the report is adjusted PENDANT when the component is called (React
   // then immediately repeats the call before displaying anything)
  const [historique, setHistorique] = useState<{ id: number; texte: string }[]>([]);
  const [ancienTTC, setAncienTTC] = useState(totalTTC);
  if (totalTTC !== ancienTTC) {
    setAncienTTC(totalTTC);
    const texte = `${euros.format(ancienTTC)} -> ${euros.format(totalTTC)}`;
     // Each row has a unique number (id) that identifies it (see key, example 03)
    setHistorique((h) => [{ id: (h[0]?.id ?? 0) + 1, texte }, ...h].slice(0, 5));
  }

   // useEffect (effect, [dépendances]): the effect is executed first
   // display, then after each display where totalTTC has changed
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = `TTC : ${euros.format(totalTTC)}`;
  }, [totalTTC]);

   // changing the item resets the quantity to 1: this is done in the
   // event handler, where we know POURQUOI the status changes
  function changerLibelle(nouveau: string) {
    setLibelle(nouveau);
    setQuantite(1);
  }

  function reinitialiser() {
    setLibelle('Stylo');
    setPrixHT(2.5);
    setQuantite(1);
    setTauxTVA(20);
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 02 - l'état et les valeurs calculées</h1>
      <div className="row g-4">
        <div className="col-md-6">
          <div className="card p-3">
            {/* value + onChange: the field displays the status, and each keystroke changes it (see example 05) */}
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="libelle">Article</label>
            <input id="libelle" className="form-control mb-2" value={libelle}
                   onChange={(e) => changerLibelle(e.target.value)} />
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="prix">Prix unitaire HT</label>
            {/* valueAsNumber: the field’s value, as a number (NaN if empty) */}
            <input id="prix" type="number" step="0.1" min="0" className="form-control mb-2" value={prixHT}
                   onChange={(e) => setPrixHT(e.target.valueAsNumber || 0)} />
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="quantite">Quantité (revient à 1 si l'article change)</label>
            <input id="quantite" type="number" min="0" className="form-control mb-2" value={quantite}
                   onChange={(e) => setQuantite(e.target.valueAsNumber || 0)} />
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="tva">Taux de TVA</label>
            {/* the value of a <select> is a CHAÎNE: Number(...) converts it */}
            <select id="tva" className="form-select mb-3" value={tauxTVA}
                    onChange={(e) => setTauxTVA(Number(e.target.value))}>
              <option value={5.5}>5,5 %</option>
              <option value={10}>10 %</option>
              <option value={20}>20 %</option>
            </select>
            <button className="btn btn-outline-secondary" onClick={reinitialiser}>Réinitialiser</button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div className="col-md-6">
          <div className="card p-3">
            <h2 className="h5">{quantite} x {libelle}</h2>
            <table className="table mb-0">
              <tbody>
                <tr><td>Total HT</td><td className="text-end">{euros.format(totalHT)}</td></tr>
                <tr><td>TVA ({tauxTVA} %)</td><td className="text-end">{euros.format(montantTVA)}</td></tr>
                <tr className="fw-bold"><td>Total TTC</td><td className="text-end">{euros.format(totalTTC)}</td></tr>
              </tbody>
            </table>
          </div>
          <div className="card p-3 mt-3">
            <h2 className="h6">Historique du total TTC</h2>
            <ul className="mb-0">
              {historique.map((ligne) => (
                <li key={ligne.id}>{ligne.texte}</li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

The [main.tsx] file in this example—and in most of the following examples—is the same as the one in Example 01, without its comments. Only the [main.tsx] files that differ will be shown.

  • Line 16: the hooks used, all provided by [React];
  • Line 19: a French-style amount formatter (1,234.50 €), created once and for all outside the component. Example 09 will present the API and [Intl] files;
  • Lines 22–25: four report data entries. Their type is derived from the initial value: [useState('Stylo')] is a report of type [string], and [useState(2.5)] is a report of type [number];
  • Lines 29–30: two values calculated from the state. These are not states (PAS): they are simple constants, recalculated each time the component is called. They are therefore always up to date. This is an important rule in [React]: only store in the report what cannot be calculated; everything else is calculated during display;
  • Line 33: [useMemo(calcul, [dépendances])] gives the same result, but [React] stores the value and only recalculates it if one of the dependencies has changed since the previous call. For an addition, this is unnecessary; it’s used for a computationally expensive operation (sorting a long list...). We included it here to demonstrate its syntax;
  • lines 39–45: the history of the totals in TTC depends on successive values of the total, which a calculated value cannot express. We store the old total in the report ([ancienTTC]); if, during display, it differs from the new one, we update the report while the component is being called. [React] allows this: it then discards the current result and immediately calls the component again with the new state, before displaying anything. Each line in the history is assigned a unique number, [id], the use of which will be explained in Example 03;
  • Lines 50–52: [useEffect(effet, [dépendances])]: The function [effet] is executed after the display: once initially, then every time one of the dependencies (here, [totalTTC]) changes. This is used for side effects: to affect something other than what the component displays (here, the browser tab title; elsewhere, a timer, a HTTP request);
  • Lines 56–58: Changing the item resets the quantity to 1. This is done in the function that handles the field change, where we know why the state is changing. This is the method recommended by [React]: rather than an effect that “monitors” the label, the action is performed in the event handler;
  • lines 61–65: several state changes in a row. [React] groups them together: the component is called only once, at the end of the handler.

JSX:

  • lines 76–77: a controlled field (see Example 05): [value] displays the state; [onChange] is called with each keystroke, via the [e] event; [e.target.value] is the field text. In JSX, the attribute [for] of a label is written as [htmlFor];
  • lines 80–81: for a numeric field, [e.target.valueAsNumber] returns the value as a number ([NaN] if the field is empty, hence [|| 0]);
  • lines 87–92: the value of a [<select>] is always a string: [Number(...)] converts it;
  • line 110: [map] generates one [<li>] element per line in the history (see example 03).

With the development server running ([npm start 02-etat]), we modify the item, price, quantity, and rate:

Each time the total for TTC changes, a row is added to the history, and the tab title changes. Changing the item resets the quantity to 1.

The difference between [Angular] and [Vue.js] is profound. In these frameworks, the data is reactive (signals, [ref]): the framework knows which data a section of the page uses, and updates only that section. [React] takes a simpler approach: every time the state changes, it re-runs the entire component function (and those of its children), then compares the result to the previous one. The code then reads like an ordinary function: the calculated values are variables, and the conditions are the [if]. The trade-off: you must follow a few rules (never modify the state directly, always call the hooks in the same order), and consider the effects and their dependencies.

docs.title: 2.3. Example 03: The JSX Syntax
docs.text:
JSX is HTML written in the [TypeScript] code, where everything enclosed in curly braces is an expression. This example displays a list of doctors, which can be filtered:

// =========================================================================
// 03-jsx/src/App.tsx - the syntax JSX
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The JSX is HTML written as DANS, the code TypeScript. Each tag becomes
// a function call, and everything between curly braces is a
// ordinary expression:
//    - attribute={expressio    n} : the value of an attribute (src, disabled, etc.);
//    - className={...          } : CSS classes, a string that is calculated;
//    - style={{ prop: value }}  : a OBJET consisting of CSS properties (camelCase);
//    - {condition && <p/>      } : an element that exists only if the
//                                  condition is true;
//    - {c ? <A/> : <B/>        } : one or the other;
//    - {liste.map((x) => <li key={x.id}/>)} : one element per element in the
//                                  list; key provides the IDENTITÉ for each one.
// No special syntax for conditions and loops: it’s just
// TypeScript. Everything before the `return` is ordinary code.
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';

// An interface TypeScript describes the structure of the objects in the list
interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  specialite: 'généraliste' | 'pédiatre' | 'cardiologue';
  disponible: boolean;
}

const MEDECINS: Medecin[] = [
  { id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
  { id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre', disponible: false },
  { id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'cardiologue', disponible: true },
];

// "one block among several, depending on a value": a switch statement within a function
function icone(specialite: Medecin['specialite']) {
  switch (specialite) {
    case 'pédiatre':
      return <span title="enfants">🧸</span>;
    case 'cardiologue':
      return <span title="cœur">❤️</span>;
    default:
      return <span title="tous publics">🩺</span>;
  }
}

export default function App() {
  const [medecins] = useState(MEDECINS);
  const [filtre, setFiltre] = useState(''); // search text
  const [seulementDisponibles, setSeulementDisponibles] = useState(false);
  const [afficherAide, setAfficherAide] = useState(true);

   // the displayed list: a regular variable, recalculated on each call
  const texte = filtre.trim().toLowerCase();
  const affiches = medecins.filter(
    (m) => (!seulementDisponibles || m.disponible) && `${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${m.specialite}`.toLowerCase().includes(texte),
  );

   // "one of the three blocks": it is calculated in AVANT and returned, using if statements
  let contenu;
  if (medecins.length === 0) {
    contenu = <p className="text-muted">Aucun médecin.</p>;
  } else if (affiches.length === 0) {
    contenu = <p className="text-warning">Aucun médecin ne correspond à « {filtre} ».</p>;
  } else {
    contenu = (
      <table className="table">
        <thead>
          <tr><th>#</th><th>Doctor</th><th>Specialty</th><th>Status</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {/* one row per doctor; key: the ID of each row, so that
              React sache quelle ligne ajouter, déplacer ou supprimer */}
          {affiches.map((m, i) => (
            <tr key={m.id} className={m.disponible ? '' : 'opacity-50'}>
              <td>{i + 1}</td>
              <td>{m.titre} {m.prenom} {m.nom}</td>
              <td>{icone(m.specialite)} {m.specialite}</td>
              <td>
                {/* a string of classes calculated by a string template */}
                <span className={`badge ${m.disponible ? 'text-bg-success' : 'text-bg-secondary'}`}>
                  {m.disponible ? 'disponible' : 'indisponible'}
                </span>
              </td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    );
  }

  return (
     // <> ... </>: a "fragment," to return multiple elements without
     // wrapping them in an additional HTML element
    <>
      <div className="container py-4">
        <h1 className="h3 mb-3">
          {/* The image is in the example's public/ folder: served as-is */}
          <img src="/medecin.svg" alt="logo" width={32} height={32} /> Exemple 03 - la syntaxe JSX
        </h1>

        <div className="d-flex flex-wrap gap-3 align-items-center mb-3">
          <input className="form-control w-auto" placeholder="rechercher..." value={filtre}
                 onChange={(e) => setFiltre(e.target.value)} />
          <label className="form-check-label">
            <input type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={seulementDisponibles}
                   onChange={(e) => setSeulementDisponibles(e.target.checked)} /> disponibles seulement
          </label>
          <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" onClick={() => setAfficherAide((a) => !a)}>
            {afficherAide ? "Cacher l'aide" : "Montrer l'aide"}
          </button>
        </div>

        {/* &&: the paragraph appears only if EXISTE is true */}
        {afficherAide && (
          <p className="alert alert-info">Tapez un nom ou une spécialité. Les médecins indisponibles sont grisés.</p>
        )}

        {contenu}

        {/* style: an object; a single number is interpreted as pixels */}
        <p style={{ fontSize: 12 + affiches.length * 2 }}>
          {affiches.length} médecin(s) affiché(s) - la taille de ce texte en dépend.
        </p>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
  • lines 22–27: a [TypeScript] interface describes the format of the objects in the list; [specialite] can only take three values;
  • lines 38–47: “one block among several, depending on a value.” JSX does not have a syntax for this: it is an ordinary function, with a [switch], which returns JSX. [Medecin['specialite']] is the type of the property [specialite]. [🧸] is a HTML entity (an emoji), allowed in JSX;
  • lines 50–53: the page state. Only the value of [useState(MEDECINS)] is retained; it is never modified here;
  • lines 56–59: the displayed list: a variable, recalculated each time the component is called;
  • lines 62–68: one of three possible contents, selected using [if] before [return]. A segment of JSX is a value like any other: it can be stored in a variable;
  • lines 76–88: the list: [map] converts each doctor into a line of [<tr>]. [i] is the doctor’s rank in the list;
  • line 77: the attribute [key] identifies each line. When the list changes, [React] uses this to determine which line to add, move, or delete, rather than rebuilding the entire list. The key must be unique among the list’s elements and stable (the same from one display to the next): an identifier, not the rank. [React] indicates in the console that the list has no keys;
  • line 77: the CSS classes are a string that is calculated, in this case using the [? :] operator;
  • line 80: the JSX returned by the [icone] function;
  • line 83: a string template (***[ ]***[...][ ] [) fabrique la liste des classes : ]badge) and a calculated class.

The [return]:

  • line 97: a fragment, [<>...</>], allows you to return multiple elements without wrapping them in an additional HTML element (here, there is only one—this is just for the example);
  • line 101: the image is in the [public/] folder in the example: [Vite] serves it as-is, at the root of the site. [width={32}]: a numeric value, enclosed in curly braces;
  • lines 105–106: the search field, which is a control; for a checkbox, [checked] is read and written;
  • line 111: an “arrow” function written directly in the attribute: it toggles the state;
  • Lines 117–119: [condition && <p>...</p>]: The paragraph exists only if the condition is true (if it is false, [React] displays nothing for [false], [null], or [undefined]). Watch out for this pitfall: [{liste.length && <p/>}] would display “0” for an empty list; instead, write [liste.length > 0 && ...];
  • line 121: the content selected above;
  • line 124: the attribute [style] receives an object (hence the double curly braces: the expression, then the object), whose properties CSS are written as “camelCase” ([fontSize] for [font-size]). A number on its own is interpreted as pixels.

Type “géné” and check “available only,” then type “zzz”:

docs.title: 2.4. Example 04: Events
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 04-events/src/App.tsx - respond to user actions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// onEvenement={function}: the function is called when the element emits
// this event:
//    - onClick={f                   } calls f(event);
//    - onClick={() => delete(t)}    an arrow function, to pass its
//                                     own arguments;
//    - the received event is a React “synthetic event,” which has the
//      same interface as the browser event (preventDefault(),
//      target, key...); evenement.nativeEvent returns the original event;
//    - useRef: a RÉFÉRENCE on a HTML element (ref={field}), to read or
//      interact with the element itself (champ.current.value, .focus()...).
// Here, there is no state for the input field: we read it ourselves.
// =========================================================================

import { useRef, useState, type FormEvent, type KeyboardEvent, type MouseEvent } from 'react';

interface Tache {
  id: number;
  libelle: string;
  faite: boolean;
}

// The style of the clickable area: an object, just like the style attribute
const styleZone = { background: '#e7f5ff', height: 80, cursor: 'crosshair' };

export default function App() {
  const [taches, setTaches] = useState<Tache[]>([
    { id: 1, libelle: 'Installer Node.js', faite: true },
    { id: 2, libelle: 'Lire le chapitre sur les événements', faite: false },
  ]);
  const [journal, setJournal] = useState<string[]>([]);
   // a reference to the <input> of the new task (null until it is displayed)
  const champ = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
   // A reference can also hold a value that is not displayed: the
   // editing does not trigger the component
  const prochainId = useRef(3);

  function tracer(message: string) {
    setJournal((j) => [`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`, ...j]);
  }

   // onSubmit: Enter text in the field OU, then click the button. preventDefault()
   // prevents the browser from submitting the form (and reloading the page)
  function ajouter(evenement: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    evenement.preventDefault();
    const input = champ.current!;
    const libelle = input.value.trim();
    if (libelle === '') {
      return;
    }
     // a state containing an array: replace it with a new array using REMPLACE
     // (never modify the old one: React wouldn't detect the change)
    setTaches((t) => [...t, { id: prochainId.current++, libelle, faite: false }]);
    tracer(`ajout de « ${libelle} »`);
    input.value = '';
    input.focus();
  }

   // a key: evenement.key provides its name
  function clavier(evenement: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) {
    if (evenement.key === 'Escape') {
      evenement.currentTarget.value = '';
    }
  }

  function basculer(tache: Tache, faite: boolean) {
    setTaches((t) => t.map((x) => (x.id === tache.id ? { ...x, faite } : x)));
    tracer(`« ${tache.libelle} » : ${faite ? 'faite' : 'à faire'}`);
  }

  function supprimer(tache: Tache) {
    setTaches((t) => t.filter((x) => x.id !== tache.id));
    tracer(`suppression de « ${tache.libelle} »`);
  }

   // the original event (nativeEvent) contains the coordinates for the area
  function position(evenement: MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
    tracer(`clic en (${evenement.nativeEvent.offsetX}, ${evenement.nativeEvent.offsetY})`);
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 04 - les événements</h1>

      <form className="d-flex gap-2 mb-3" onSubmit={ajouter}>
        <input ref={champ} className="form-control" placeholder="nouvelle tâche (Échap pour vider)" onKeyDown={clavier} />
        <button type="submit" className="btn btn-primary">Ajouter</button>
      </form>

      <ul className="list-group mb-3">
        {taches.map((t) => (
          <li key={t.id} className="list-group-item d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
            {/* e.target: the checkbox for row CETTE; checked: its state */}
            <input type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={t.faite}
                   onChange={(e) => basculer(t, e.target.checked)} />
            <span className={`flex-grow-1 ${t.faite ? 'text-decoration-line-through text-muted' : ''}`}>{t.libelle}</span>
            {/* an arrow function: the task of the CETTE line as an argument */}
            <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" onClick={() => supprimer(t)}>Supprimer</button>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <div className="p-3 mb-3 rounded" style={styleZone} onClick={position}>Cliquez dans cette zone</div>

      <h2 className="h6">Journal</h2>
      <ul className="small">
        {journal.map((ligne, i) => (
           // key: the row’s position counted from the added PREMIÈRE (which has
           // always has key 1): each row retains the same key when other
           // lines are added to the top of the list
          <li key={journal.length - i}>{ligne}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
  • Line 17: [FormEvent], [KeyboardEvent], [MouseEvent] are event types of [React] (hence the term [type]);
  • Line 26: the style of the clickable area, an object;
  • line 35: [useRef] creates a reference: an object [{ current: ... }] that [React] retains from one display to the next. Assigned to the [ref] attribute of an element (line 88), it refers to the HTML element itself, once displayed: [champ.current.value], [champ.current.focus()]...;
  • line 38: A reference can also retain any value, which is not displayed. Modifying it ([prochainId.current++]) does not reload the component, unlike a state;
  • lines 46–59: called by the form’s [onSubmit] event, triggered when you press Enter in the OU field or click the [submit] button:
    • line 47: prevents the browser from submitting the form to the server, which would reload the page;
    • line 48: the [<input>] element; the [!] element confirms that it exists (it is displayed);
    • line 55: a state containing an array: it is replaced with a new array ([[...t, nouvelle]]: the elements of [t], followed by the new task). We do not modify JAMAIS or the state itself ([t.push(...)]): [React] compares the old and new values; if they are the same array, it concludes that nothing has changed and displays nothing;
    • lines 57–58: the field is cleared and focus is returned to it, directly on the HTML element;
  • lines 62–66: [evenement.key] returns the name of the key. [currentTarget] is the element that holds the handler (in this case, the field);
  • line 69: modify an array element: a new array, where the element in question is replaced by a modified copy ([{ ...x, faite }]);
  • line 74: delete an element: a new array, without that element;
  • lines 79–81: the event for [React] is a “synthetic” event, which has the same interface as the browser’s event; [nativeEvent] provides the original event, here with the click coordinates relative to the area ([offsetX]).

JSX:

  • line 87: the form handler;
  • line 88: the reference, and a key handler. This field is not validated (no [value]): the browser manages its value, which is read when needed;
  • Lines 96–97: A manager writes on the spot: an arrowed function that calls [basculer] with the task from CETTE;
  • Line 100: Same principle: [onClick={supprimer(t)}] would call [supprimer] immediately, during display;
  • Line 113: the key for the log lines.

Add a task, check the second one, delete the first one, then click in the field:

docs.title: 2.5. Example 05: Validated Fields
docs.text:
A form with all types of fields, linked to the report:

// =========================================================================
// 05-control-fields/src/App.tsx - all field types, "controlled"
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A CONTRÔLÉ field displays a value from the report (value={...}) and notifies
// the component of each change (onChange={...}), which sets the status to
// up to date. The state is the single source of truth: typing in the field updates
// the state, and modifying the state (via code) modifies the field.
// This is the hand-coded “two-way” binding. What is read
// in the event depends on the field:
//    - text input, textarea          -> e.target.value (string)
//    - input type="number           " -> e.target.valueAsNumber (NaN if empty)
//    - checkbox                   -> e.target.checked (boolean)
//    - radio button                 s -> e.target.value of the selected button
//    - dropd                        own -> e.target.value
//    - select multipl               e -> e.target.selectedOptions (multiple)
//    - input type="date             " -> e.target.value, "yyyy-MM-dd"
// Same form as Example 18 in the course NestJS; but here, no
// server: everything happens in the browser.
// =========================================================================

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';

const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const LOISIRS = ['sport', 'musique', 'lecture', 'cinéma'];
const PAYS = [
  { code: 'fr', libelle: 'France' },
  { code: 'be', libelle: 'Belgique' },
  { code: 'ch', libelle: 'Suisse' },
];

export default function App() {
   // A record for each form field
  const [titre, setTitre] = useState('Mme');
  const [nom, setNom] = useState('');
  const [age, setAge] = useState<number | null>(30);
  const [presentation, setPresentation] = useState('');
  const [newsletter, setNewsletter] = useState(false);
  const [loisirs, setLoisirs] = useState<string[]>(['lecture']);
  const [pays, setPays] = useState('fr');
  const [langues, setLangues] = useState<string[]>([]);
  const [naissance, setNaissance] = useState('');
  const [envoye, setEnvoye] = useState<string | null>(null);

   // All values combined into a single object (what would be sent to a server)
  const modele = { titre, nom: nom.trim(), age, presentation, newsletter, loisirs, pays, langues, naissance };

   // multiple checkboxes for UN table: add or remove the value
  function basculerLoisir(loisir: string, coche: boolean) {
    setLoisirs((l) => (coche ? [...l, loisir] : l.filter((x) => x !== loisir)));
  }

  function envoyer(evenement: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    evenement.preventDefault(); // no submission to the server, no page reload
    setEnvoye(JSON.stringify(modele));
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 05 - les champs contrôlés</h1>
      <div className="row g-4">
        <form className="col-md-7" onSubmit={envoyer}>
          <div className="mb-3">
            <span className="form-label d-block">Titre</span>
            {/* radio buttons: a single state; “checked” indicates which one is selected */}
            {TITRES.map((t) => (
              <div key={t} className="form-check form-check-inline">
                <input type="radio" className="form-check-input" name="titre" id={`titre-${t}`} value={t}
                       checked={titre === t} onChange={(e) => setTitre(e.target.value)} />
                <label className="form-check-label" htmlFor={`titre-${t}`}>{t}</label>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
          <div className="row g-3 mb-3">
            <div className="col-8">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="nom">Nom</label>
              <input id="nom" className="form-control" value={nom} onChange={(e) => setNom(e.target.value)} />
            </div>
            <div className="col-4">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="age">Âge</label>
              {/* An empty field results in NaN: store `null` in the state and `''` in the field */}
              <input id="age" type="number" className="form-control" value={age ?? ''}
                     onChange={(e) => setAge(Number.isNaN(e.target.valueAsNumber) ? null : e.target.valueAsNumber)} />
            </div>
          </div>
          <div className="mb-3">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="presentation">Présentation (mise à jour à la sortie du champ)</label>
            {/* a validated NON field: defaultValue is its initial value, then
                le navigateur le gère seul ; onBlur ne prévient qu'à la sortie */}
            <textarea id="presentation" rows={2} className="form-control" defaultValue={presentation}
                      onBlur={(e) => setPresentation(e.target.value)} />
          </div>
          <div className="mb-3 form-check">
            {/* a single checkbox: true / false */}
            <input id="newsletter" type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={newsletter}
                   onChange={(e) => setNewsletter(e.target.checked)} />
            <label htmlFor="newsletter" className="form-check-label">Recevoir la lettre d'information</label>
          </div>
          <div className="mb-3">
            <span className="form-label d-block">Loisirs</span>
            {LOISIRS.map((l) => (
              <div key={l} className="form-check form-check-inline">
                <input type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" id={`loisir-${l}`} checked={loisirs.includes(l)}
                       onChange={(e) => basculerLoisir(l, e.target.checked)} />
                <label className="form-check-label" htmlFor={`loisir-${l}`}>{l}</label>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
          <div className="row g-3 mb-3">
            <div className="col-6">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="pays">Pays</label>
              {/* value on the <select> (and not “selected” on the <option>) */}
              <select id="pays" className="form-select" value={pays} onChange={(e) => setPays(e.target.value)}>
                {PAYS.map((p) => (
                  <option key={p.code} value={p.code}>{p.libelle}</option>
                ))}
              </select>
            </div>
            <div className="col-6">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="langues">Langues parlées</label>
              {/* multiple: value is a TABLEAU; selectedOptions, the selected options */}
              <select id="langues" multiple size={3} className="form-select" value={langues}
                      onChange={(e) => setLangues([...e.target.selectedOptions].map((o) => o.value))}>
                <option value="fr">français</option>
                <option value="en">anglais</option>
                <option value="es">espagnol</option>
              </select>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div className="mb-3">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
            <input id="naissance" type="date" className="form-control w-auto" value={naissance}
                   onChange={(e) => setNaissance(e.target.value)} />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="btn btn-primary">Envoyer</button>
        </form>

        <div className="col-md-5">
          <h2 className="h6">Le modèle, en direct</h2>
          {/* JSON.stringify (object, null, 2): the JSON, indented by 2 spaces */}
          <pre className="bg-light p-2 rounded small">{JSON.stringify(modele, null, 2)}</pre>
          {envoye !== null && (
            <>
              <h2 className="h6">Dernier envoi</h2>
              <pre className="bg-success-subtle p-2 rounded small text-wrap">{envoye}</pre>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

The principle (lines 4–6): a controlled field displays a value from the report ([value={...}]) and notifies the component of any changes ([onChange={...}]), which then updates the report. The report is the single source of truth: the field simply displays what the report says. If the [onChange] manager did not update the report, the field would not accept user input.

  • Lines 33–41: one report per field;
  • line 45: all values combined into a single object—what would be sent to a server. This is a calculated value; [nom.trim()] removes leading and trailing spaces;
  • Lines 48–50: multiple checkboxes for UN array: the value is added or removed;
  • lines 52–55: Submit the form without reloading the page.

JSX, field by field:

  • lines 65–68: radio buttons: they share the same state; [checked] specifies which one is selected. [key={t}]: the key for each button;
  • line 76: a text field;
  • lines 81–82: a numeric field: an empty field yields [NaN]; we then store [null] in the state and display [''] ([age ?? '']: [''] if [age] is equal to [null] or [undefined]);
  • lines 89–90: an unvalidated field: [defaultValue] is its initial value, after which the browser handles it on its own; [onBlur] notifies the component when the field is exited. The state is therefore updated only upon exiting the field;
  • line 94: a single checkbox: [checked] and [e.target.checked];
  • lines 100–103: the leisure fields;
  • line 112: a list: [value] on [<select>], not [selected] on [<option>];
  • lines 121–122: a multiple-choice list: [value] is an array; [e.target.selectedOptions] provides the selected options, which are converted into an array of values ([[...liste]] converts a collection into an array);
  • line 131: a date, in the form of a string [yyyy-MM-dd];
  • line 140: the template, in the format JSON, indented by 2 spaces.

Writing [value] and [onChange] in each field is repetitive: this is the trade-off for the simplicity of [React], which has no equivalent to [v-model] for [Vue.js] or to [[(ngModel)]] for [Angular]. The following examples show how to reduce this repetition: a single state object (Example 06), a function that generates a field’s attributes (Examples 06 and 07), and a library (Example 08).

docs.title: 2.6. Example 06: A form, an object, a reducer
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 06-use-reducer/src/App.tsx - a form, an object, a reducer
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Example 05 had one useState per field. For a real form, we
// prefer a UN object that contains all the values, the MODÈLE, and we
// describe these changes in a single function, RÉDUCTEUR:
//
//      reducer(etatActuel, action) -> nouvelEtat
//
// useReducer(reducer, etatInitial) returns the state and a function
// dispatch(action): the component no longer modifies the state; it DÉCRIT what
// what happened ({ type: 'update', field: 'name', value: 'Dupont' }), and the
// reducer derives the new state from this. All the logic is in one place,
// and it’s a PURE function (same input, same output, no side
// edge effects), which is easy to test.
//
// The state also tracks, for each field, whether it has been “touched” (exited at
// at least once); from this, we can determine whether it has been “modified” (its value differs from
// the initial value) and whether it is disabled.
// =========================================================================

import { useReducer, type ChangeEvent } from 'react';

// the format of the form data
interface Profil {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  age: number;
  newsletter: boolean;
  email: string;
  pays: string;
  naissance: string;
  presentation: string;
}

const DEPART: Profil = {
  titre: 'Mme',
  prenom: 'Marie',
  nom: 'PELISSIER',
  age: 30,
  newsletter: false,
  email: '',
  pays: 'fr',
  naissance: '',
  presentation: '',
};

type Champ = keyof Profil; // 'title' | 'first_name' | ...: the name of a field

interface Etat {
  valeurs: Profil;
  touches: Partial<Record<Champ, boolean>>; // fields already exited
}

// possible actions: a "discriminated union" based on the type property
type Action =
  | { type: 'modifier'; champ: Champ; valeur: Profil[Champ] }
  | { type: 'quitter'; champ: Champ }
  | { type: 'majuscules' }
  | { type: 'reinitialiser' };

// the reducer: it never returns the received report; it returns a new one
function reducteur(etat: Etat, action: Action): Etat {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'modifier':
      return { ...etat, valeurs: { ...etat.valeurs, [action.champ]: action.valeur } };
    case 'quitter':
      return { ...etat, touches: { ...etat.touches, [action.champ]: true } };
    case 'majuscules': {
      const { prenom, nom } = etat.valeurs;
      return { ...etat, valeurs: { ...etat.valeurs, prenom: prenom.toUpperCase(), nom: nom.toUpperCase() } };
    }
    case 'reinitialiser':
      return { valeurs: { ...DEPART }, touches: {} };
  }
}

const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const CHAMPS_SUIVIS: Champ[] = ['prenom', 'nom', 'age', 'email'];

export default function App() {
  const [etat, dispatch] = useReducer(reducteur, { valeurs: { ...DEPART }, touches: {} });
  const v = etat.valeurs;

   // values DÉDUITES from the report
  const modifie = (c: Champ) => v[c] !== DEPART[c];
  const desactive = (c: Champ) => c === 'email' && !v.newsletter; // The email requires the newsletter
  const formulaireModifie = (Object.keys(DEPART) as Champ[]).some(modifie);

   // Common attributes of a text field: a function that generates them
   // (id, value, onChange, onBlur, disabled), to be "applied" to the element: {...link('name')}
  function lier(champ: 'prenom' | 'nom' | 'email' | 'naissance' | 'presentation' | 'pays') {
    return {
      id: champ,
      value: v[champ],
      disabled: desactive(champ),
      onChange: (e: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | HTMLSelectElement>) =>
        dispatch({ type: 'modifier', champ, valeur: e.target.value }),
      onBlur: () => dispatch({ type: 'quitter', champ }),
    };
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 06 - un formulaire, un objet, un réducteur</h1>
      <div className="row g-4">
        <form className="col-md-7" onSubmit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}>
          <div className="mb-3">
            <span className="form-label d-block">Titre</span>
            {TITRES.map((t) => (
              <div key={t} className="form-check form-check-inline">
                <input type="radio" className="form-check-input" id={`titre-${t}`} name="titre" value={t}
                       checked={v.titre === t} onChange={() => dispatch({ type: 'modifier', champ: 'titre', valeur: t })} />
                <label className="form-check-label" htmlFor={`titre-${t}`}>{t}</label>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
          <div className="row g-3 mb-3">
            <div className="col-5">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="prenom">Prénom</label>
              {/* {...object}: each property of the object becomes an attribute */}
              <input className="form-control" {...lier('prenom')} />
            </div>
            <div className="col-5">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="nom">Nom</label>
              <input className="form-control" {...lier('nom')} />
            </div>
            <div className="col-2">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="age">Âge</label>
              <input id="age" type="number" className="form-control" value={v.age}
                     onChange={(e) => dispatch({ type: 'modifier', champ: 'age', valeur: e.target.valueAsNumber || 0 })}
                     onBlur={() => dispatch({ type: 'quitter', champ: 'age' })} />
            </div>
          </div>
          <div className="row g-3 mb-3 align-items-end">
            <div className="col-5">
              <div className="form-check">
                <input id="newsletter" type="checkbox" className="form-check-input" checked={v.newsletter}
                       onChange={(e) => dispatch({ type: 'modifier', champ: 'newsletter', valeur: e.target.checked })} />
                <label htmlFor="newsletter" className="form-check-label">Recevoir la lettre d'information</label>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div className="col-7">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="email">E-mail (si lettre d'information)</label>
              <input type="email" className="form-control" {...lier('email')} />
            </div>
          </div>
          <div className="row g-3 mb-3">
            <div className="col-6">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="pays">Pays</label>
              <select className="form-select" {...lier('pays')}>
                <option value="fr">France</option>
                <option value="be">Belgique</option>
                <option value="ch">Suisse</option>
              </select>
            </div>
            <div className="col-6">
              <label className="form-label" htmlFor="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
              <input type="date" className="form-control" {...lier('naissance')} />
            </div>
          </div>
          <div className="mb-3">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="presentation">Présentation</label>
            <textarea rows={2} className="form-control" {...lier('presentation')} />
          </div>
          <div className="d-flex gap-2">
            <button type="button" className="btn btn-outline-primary" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'majuscules' })}>
              Nom en majuscules
            </button>
            <button type="button" className="btn btn-outline-secondary" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'reinitialiser' })}>
              Réinitialiser
            </button>
          </div>
        </form>

        <div className="col-md-5">
          <h2 className="h6">Le modèle, en direct</h2>
          <pre className="bg-light p-2 rounded small">{JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)}</pre>
          <h2 className="h6">L'état des champs</h2>
          <table className="table table-sm small">
            <thead><tr><th>champ</th><th>touché</th><th>modifié</th><th>désactivé</th></tr></thead>
            <tbody>
              {CHAMPS_SUIVIS.map((c) => (
                <tr key={c}>
                  <td>{c}</td>
                  <td>{String(etat.touches[c] ?? false)}</td>
                  <td>{String(modifie(c))}</td>
                  <td>{String(desactive(c))}</td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>
          <p className="small mb-0">formulaire modifié : <strong>{String(formulaireModifie)}</strong></p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 25–35: the data structure of the form; [DEPART] (lines 37–47), their initial values;
  • Line 49: [keyof Profil] is the type of the property names for [Profil]: ['titre' | 'prenom' | ...];
  • Lines 51–54: The complete state: the values and the fields that have already been “visited” (exited at least once). [Partial<Record<Champ, boolean>>]: an object whose keys are field names, all of which are optional;
  • lines 57–61: the possible actions, in the form of a “discriminated union”: each action has a [type] property, which specifies what action it is, and its own data;
  • lines 64–77: the reducer: a function that takes the current state and an action, and returns the NOUVEL state. It never modifies the received state (it creates a modified copy, [{ ...etat, ... }]) and does nothing else: it is a pure function, easy to understand and test. [[action.champ]: action.valeur]: a property whose name is computed;
  • line 83: [useReducer(reducteur, étatInitial)] returns the state and a function [dispatch(action)]: the component no longer modifies the state; it describes what has happened ([dispatch({ type: 'quitter', champ: 'nom' })]), and [React] calls the reducer to deduce the new state;
  • lines 87–89: values derived from the state: a field is “modified” if its value differs from the initial value; email is disabled as long as the “newsletter” checkbox is not checked;
  • lines 93–102: a function that generates the attributes common to a field: [id], [value], [disabled], [onChange], [onBlur]. These are “applied” to the element using the syntax [{...objet}] (line 123): each property of the object becomes an attribute. A single line is then sufficient to link a field to the form.

In JSX, specific fields (radio buttons, age, checkbox) call [dispatch] directly; the “Capitalize Name” and “Reset” buttons trigger the corresponding actions. On the right, the live template and the field status.

Enter a first name, enter a last name, check the newsletter box, enter an email address, then click “Capitalize Last Name”:

[useState] is suitable for independent data; [useReducer] is for a composite state, where changes follow rules: all the logic is in one place, outside the component. This is the same concept as the “stores” in [Redux] or [Vuex], but at the component level.

docs.title: 2.7. Example 07: Form Validation
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 07-validation/src/App.tsx - validate a form in the browser
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// React has no built-in validation system: it's just regular code. A
// function PURE, validate(account), returns field errors; it
// call it every time the form is displayed, so the errors are always up to date.
// They aren’t displayed right away (an empty form covered in red is
// unpleasant): they are shown only for a field that has already been exited (“touched”). The submission
// marks all fields as touched, then takes action only if the form
// is valid.
//
// Same rules as the RdvMedecins server ("Create an Account" form).
// ATTENTION: This validation is simply a CONFORT for the user (an
// an immediate response, without any back-and-forth with the server). It does not protect
// anything: anyone can send the server a request fabricated by
// (curl...). The server therefore revalidates TOUJOURS everything (see example 25).
// =========================================================================

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';

interface Compte {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  login: string;
  password: string;
  confirmation: string;
}

type Champ = keyof Compte;
// at most one error message per field
type Erreurs = Partial<Record<Champ, string>>;

const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const FORMAT_LOGIN = /^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/;
const MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6;

// the rules: a pure function that depends only on its arguments
function valider(c: Compte): Erreurs {
  const erreurs: Erreurs = {};
  if (!TITRES.includes(c.titre)) erreurs.titre = 'Choisissez un titre dans la liste.';
  if (c.prenom.trim() === '') erreurs.prenom = 'Le prénom est obligatoire.';
  else if (c.prenom.length > 20) erreurs.prenom = 'Le prénom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.';
  if (c.nom.trim() === '') erreurs.nom = 'Le nom est obligatoire.';
  else if (c.nom.length > 20) erreurs.nom = 'Le nom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.';
  if (c.login === '') erreurs.login = 'Le login est obligatoire.';
  else if (!FORMAT_LOGIN.test(c.login)) erreurs.login = 'Lettres minuscules non accentuées, chiffres, point, tiret, souligné.';
  if (c.password === '') erreurs.password = 'Le mot de passe est obligatoire.';
  else if (c.password.length < MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN) erreurs.password = `Au moins ${MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN} caractères.`;
   // a rule that compares DEUX fields
  if (c.confirmation !== c.password) erreurs.confirmation = 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.';
  return erreurs;
}

const VIDE: Compte = { titre: 'Mr', prenom: '', nom: '', login: '', password: '', confirmation: '' };
const TOUS: Record<Champ, boolean> = { titre: true, prenom: true, nom: true, login: true, password: true, confirmation: true };

export default function App() {
  const [compte, setCompte] = useState<Compte>(VIDE);
  const [touches, setTouches] = useState<Partial<Record<Champ, boolean>>>({});
  const [envoiTente, setEnvoiTente] = useState(false);
  const [succes, setSucces] = useState(false);

   // Errors: recalculated with each display, never saved in the report
  const erreurs = valider(compte);
  const nbErreurs = Object.keys(erreurs).length;

   // A field’s Bootstrap class: red (is-invalid) or green (is-valid),
   // only once it has been selected
  function classe(champ: Champ, base = 'form-control'): string {
    if (!touches[champ]) return base;
    return `${base} ${erreurs[champ] ? 'is-invalid' : 'is-valid'}`;
  }

   // attributes common to all fields
  function lier(champ: Champ) {
    return {
      id: champ,
      value: compte[champ],
      onChange: (e: { target: { value: string } }) => {
        setCompte((c) => ({ ...c, [champ]: e.target.value }));
        setSucces(false);
      },
      onBlur: () => setTouches((t) => ({ ...t, [champ]: true })),
    };
  }

  function envoyer(evenement: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    evenement.preventDefault();
    setEnvoiTente(true);
    setTouches(TOUS); // all errors appear
     // here, the form would be submitted to the server (see Example 25)
    setSucces(nbErreurs === 0);
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 07 - la validation d'un formulaire</h1>
      {/* noValidate: browser-specific validation is disabled, so that
          afficher NOS messages, dans NOTRE style */}
      <form className="card p-4" noValidate onSubmit={envoyer}>
        <div className="mb-3">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="titre">Titre</label>
          <select className={classe('titre', 'form-select')} {...lier('titre')}>
            {TITRES.map((t) => <option key={t}>{t}</option>)}
          </select>
          <div className="invalid-feedback">{erreurs.titre}</div>
        </div>
        <div className="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="prenom">Prénom</label>
            {/* `is-invalid` highlights the field in red; `ET` displays the
                .invalid-feedback qui le suit : on y écrit l'erreur du champ */}
            <input className={classe('prenom')} {...lier('prenom')} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{erreurs.prenom}</div>
          </div>
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="nom">Nom</label>
            <input className={classe('nom')} {...lier('nom')} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{erreurs.nom}</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div className="mb-3">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="login">Login</label>
          <input className={classe('login')} autoComplete="username" {...lier('login')} />
          <div className="invalid-feedback">{erreurs.login}</div>
        </div>
        <div className="row g-3 mb-4">
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="password">Mot de passe</label>
            <input type="password" className={classe('password')} autoComplete="new-password" {...lier('password')} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{erreurs.password}</div>
          </div>
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="confirmation">Confirmation</label>
            <input type="password" className={classe('confirmation')} autoComplete="new-password" {...lier('confirmation')} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{erreurs.confirmation}</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <button type="submit" className="btn btn-primary">Créer le compte</button>
        {envoiTente && nbErreurs > 0 && (
          <div className="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">Le formulaire contient {nbErreurs} erreur(s).</div>
        )}
        {succes && <div className="alert alert-success mt-3 mb-0">Formulaire valide : il pourrait être envoyé au serveur.</div>}
      </form>
    </div>
  );
}

[React] has no validation system: it’s just regular code.

  • Lines 30–32: at most one error message per field;
  • lines 39–53: the rules: a pure function that returns field errors; these are the same rules as those in the [RdvMedecins] server for creating an account. The last rule compares two fields;
  • Line 65: Errors are recalculated each time the page is displayed and are never cached; they are therefore always up to date;
  • lines 70–73: the [Bootstrap] class for a field—[is-invalid] (red box) or [is-valid] (green box)—only after the field has been selected: an empty form covered in red would be unappealing;
  • lines 76–86: as in Example 06, the common attributes of the fields; leaving a field marks it as selected;
  • lines 88–94: submitting the form marks the fields as filled in (their errors appear), and the submission succeeds only if the form is valid.

JSX:

  • line 101: browser-specific validation is disabled to display NOS messages in the NOTRE style;
  • lines 114–115: the [is-invalid] class frames the field in red; ET displays the following [.invalid-feedback], where the field error is written.

Enter a first name, enter a last name, enter an invalid login:

Click “Create Account”:

Once everything has been corrected:

ATTENTION: This validation is merely for the user's convenience (an immediate response, without a round trip to the server). It provides no protection: anyone can send a manually crafted request to the server ([curl]...). The server therefore revalidates TOUJOURS in its entirety (see Example 25).

docs.title: 2.8. Example 08: React Hook Form
docs.text:
The form from Example 07, written using [React Hook Form], the most widely used form library with [React]:

// =========================================================================
// 08-react-hook-form/src/App.tsx - a form library
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The form in Example 07, written with React Hook Form, the
// the most widely used form library with React. It is found in
// most existing applications.
//    - useForm<T>() returns tools for a form of type T;
//    - register('name', rules) binds a HTML field to the "name" field of the
//      form: it returns the attributes to be applied to the element (name,
//      ref, onChange, onBlur). The NE fields are PAS validated: this is the
//      library that reads their values from the page, without reloading the
//      component with every keystroke;
//    - the rules: required, maxLength, minLength, pattern, validate (a
//      "custom" rule), each with its own message;
//    - formState.errors: errors for each field;
//    - handleSubmit (action): validates everything; only calls the action if the
//      form is valid.
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';

interface Compte {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  login: string;
  password: string;
  confirmation: string;
}

const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

export default function App() {
  const {
    register,
    handleSubmit,
    getValues,
    formState: { errors, isSubmitted },
  } = useForm<Compte>({
     // the default values
    defaultValues: { titre: 'Mr', prenom: '', nom: '', login: '', password: '', confirmation: '' },
     // when to validate: upon leaving a field, then with each keystroke
    mode: 'onTouched',
  });
  const [envoi, setEnvoi] = useState('');

   // a field is flagged as having an error if it has one (errors.nom exists)
  const classe = (champ: keyof Compte) => `form-control${errors[champ] ? ' is-invalid' : ''}`;

   // called by handleSubmit or SEULEMENT if the form is valid;
   // it receives the values, typed as
  function creer(compte: Compte) {
    setEnvoi(JSON.stringify(compte));
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 08 - React Hook Form</h1>
      <form className="card p-4" noValidate onSubmit={handleSubmit(creer, () => setEnvoi(''))}>
        <div className="mb-3">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="titre">Titre</label>
          <select id="titre" className="form-select" {...register('titre', { required: true })}>
            {TITRES.map((t) => <option key={t}>{t}</option>)}
          </select>
        </div>
        <div className="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="prenom">Prénom</label>
            <input id="prenom" className={classe('prenom')}
                   {...register('prenom', {
                     required: 'Le prénom est obligatoire.',
                     maxLength: { value: 20, message: '20 caractères au plus.' },
                   })} />
            {/* errors.prenom?.message: the message for the failed rule */}
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{errors.prenom?.message}</div>
          </div>
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="nom">Nom</label>
            <input id="nom" className={classe('nom')}
                   {...register('nom', {
                     required: 'Le nom est obligatoire.',
                     maxLength: { value: 20, message: '20 caractères au plus.' },
                   })} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{errors.nom?.message}</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div className="mb-3">
          <label className="form-label" htmlFor="login">Login</label>
          <input id="login" className={classe('login')}
                 {...register('login', {
                   required: 'Le login est obligatoire.',
                   pattern: { value: /^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/, message: 'Lettres minuscules non accentuées, chiffres, point, tiret, souligné.' },
                 })} />
          <div className="invalid-feedback">{errors.login?.message}</div>
        </div>
        <div className="row g-3 mb-4">
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="password">Mot de passe</label>
            <input id="password" type="password" className={classe('password')}
                   {...register('password', {
                     required: 'Le mot de passe est obligatoire.',
                     minLength: { value: 6, message: 'Au moins 6 caractères.' },
                      // deps: when the password changes, revalidate AUSSI the confirmation
                     deps: ['confirmation'],
                   })} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{errors.password?.message}</div>
          </div>
          <div className="col-sm-6">
            <label className="form-label" htmlFor="confirmation">Confirmation</label>
            {/* validate: a "custom" rule; getValues reads a AUTRE field */}
            <input id="confirmation" type="password" className={classe('confirmation')}
                   {...register('confirmation', {
                     validate: (valeur) => valeur === getValues('password') || 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.',
                   })} />
            <div className="invalid-feedback">{errors.confirmation?.message}</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <button type="submit" className="btn btn-primary">Créer le compte</button>
        {isSubmitted && (
          <div className={`alert mt-3 mb-0 ${envoi ? 'alert-success' : 'alert-danger'}`}>
            {envoi ? <>Formulaire valide : <code>{envoi}</code></> : 'Formulaire invalide.'}
          </div>
        )}
      </form>
    </div>
  );
}
  • line 21: the library’s main hook;
  • lines 35–40: [useForm<Compte>(options)] returns the components of a [Compte]-type form, which are unwrapped: [register], [handleSubmit], [getValues], and [formState], the form status (including [errors], field errors, and [isSubmitted], which is true after the first submission);
  • line 42: the initial values;
  • line 44: when to validate: upon exiting a field, then after each keystroke;
  • line 49: a field is flagged as having an error if it contains one;
  • lines 53–55: the submission action, called by [handleSubmit] only if the form is valid; it receives the typed values;
  • line 60: [handleSubmit(siValide, siInvalide)] creates the submission handler: it validates all fields, then calls one function or the other;
  • lines 71–74: [register('prenom', règles)] links the HTML field to the [prenom] field in the form, using its rules: [required], [maxLength], [minLength], [pattern], and [validate] (a “custom” rule), each with its own message. [register] returns the attributes to be applied to the element ([name], [ref], [onChange], [onBlur]). The fields are not checked (PAS): the library reads their values from the page via the reference; therefore, the component is not re-invoked with each keystroke, which is important for large forms;
  • line 76: the message for a failed validation rule ([?.]: [undefined] if the field has no errors);
  • line 105: when the password changes, revalidate the confirmation as well;
  • line 114: a custom rule that compares two fields: [getValues('password')] reads the value of another field. It returns [true] (valid) or the error message.

For [React], each requirement has several competing libraries. For forms, we also encounter [Formik], [TanStack Form], and, to describe the rules, [Zod] or [Yup] (validation “schemas” that can be shared with a [Node.js] server). For the case study, where all validation is performed by the server, we will not use a library: validated fields and a custom hook will suffice.

docs.title: 2.9. Example 09: Formatting Values
docs.text: [Angular] has its own “pipes” for formatting a value in a template. [React] does not have its own mechanism: in JSX, we call functions stored in a module. For dates, numbers, and amounts, the browser provides the API [Intl], which understands the conventions of each language.

docs.title: 2.9.1. Formatting functions
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 09-formatting/src/formatage.ts - "custom" formatting functions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// React does not have its own formatting mechanism (Angular has its
// "pipes," Vue.js its functions): in JSX, we call FONCTIONS
// ordinary functions, organized into a module and testable separately:
//      {schedule(time          slot)} -> "8:00 - 8:20"
//      {time(time slot, 'start')} -> "8:00"
// For dates, numbers, and amounts, the browser provides the API
// Intl, which understands the conventions of each language.
// =========================================================================

export interface Creneau {
  hdebut: number;
  mdebut: number;
  hfin: number;
  mfin: number;
}

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
function heure(h: number, m: number): string {
  return `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

export function horaire(c: Creneau, partie: 'tout' | 'debut' | 'fin' = 'tout'): string {
  switch (partie) {
    case 'debut':
      return heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut);
    case 'fin':
      return heure(c.hfin, c.mfin);
    default:
      return `${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}`;
  }
}

// "marie pelissier" -> "Marie Pelissier"
export function majusculeInitiale(texte: string): string {
  return texte.replace(/\p{L}+/gu, (mot) => mot[0].toUpperCase() + mot.slice(1).toLowerCase());
}

// "Marie PELISSIER" -> "MP"
export function initiales(nomComplet: string): string {
  return nomComplet
    .split(/\s+/)
    .filter((mot) => mot !== '')
    .map((mot) => mot[0].toUpperCase())
    .join('');
}

// "2026-10-05" (the format of API RdvMedecins) -> a date, at midnight UTC
export function versDate(jour: string): Date {
  return new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`);
}
  • lines 13–18: a time slot, as sent by the [RdvMedecins] server (start and end hours and minutes);
  • lines 21–23: [padStart(2, '0')] pads the string on the left: “5” becomes “05”;
  • lines 25–34: “8:00 – 8:20,” or just the start or the end, depending on the [partie] parameter, which is optional (default value ['tout']);
  • lines 37–39: [\p{L}+] refers to a sequence of letters, including accented characters (option [u]): the first letter is capitalized;
  • lines 51–53: a date of the form API (["2026-10-05"]) becomes a [Date] object at midnight UTC.

docs.title: 2.9.2. The page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 09-formatting/src/App.tsx - formatting values in JSX
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each row of the table shows a piece of code and what it displays.
// Intl formatters are created once and for all, outside the component:
// Creating them costs more than using them.
// =========================================================================

import { useState } from 'react';
import { horaire, initiales, majusculeInitiale, versDate, type Creneau } from './formatage';

// Dates: dateStyle / timeStyle, or the details of the parts to be displayed
const dateCourte = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('fr-FR', { dateStyle: 'medium' });
const dateComplete = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('fr-FR', { dateStyle: 'full' });
const heureSeule = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('fr-FR', { timeStyle: 'medium' });
const jourLong = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('fr-FR', { weekday: 'long', day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const jourAnglais = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { dateStyle: 'long', timeZone: 'UTC' });
// numbers and amounts
const euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });
const entier = new Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', { maximumFractionDigits: 0 });
const pourcent = new Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', { style: 'percent', minimumFractionDigits: 1 });

const jour = '2026-10-05'; // a date in the format of API RdvMedecins
const prix = 1234.5;
const taux = 0.055;
const nom = 'marie pelissier';
const medecin = { titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER' };
const langages = ['TypeScript', 'HTML', 'CSS', 'JavaScript', 'SQL'];
const creneaux: Creneau[] = [
  { hdebut: 8, mdebut: 0, hfin: 8, mfin: 20 },
  { hdebut: 8, mdebut: 20, hfin: 8, mfin: 40 },
  { hdebut: 14, mdebut: 5, hfin: 14, mfin: 25 },
];

export default function App() {
  const [maintenant, setMaintenant] = useState(() => new Date());

   // [code affiché, valeur]: a row from the table
  const lignes: [string, string][] = [
    ['dateCourte.format(maintenant)', dateCourte.format(maintenant)],
    ['dateComplete.format(maintenant)', dateComplete.format(maintenant)],
    ['heureSeule.format(maintenant)', heureSeule.format(maintenant)],
    ['jourLong.format(versDate(jour))', jourLong.format(versDate(jour))],
    ['jourAnglais.format(versDate(jour))', jourAnglais.format(versDate(jour))],
    ['maintenant.toLocaleDateString()', maintenant.toLocaleDateString()],
    ['euros.format(prix)', euros.format(prix)],
    ['entier.format(prix)', entier.format(prix)],
    ['pourcent.format(taux)', pourcent.format(taux)],
    ['nom.toUpperCase()', nom.toUpperCase()],
    ['majusculeInitiale(nom)', majusculeInitiale(nom)],
    ["'RDV'.toLowerCase()", 'RDV'.toLowerCase()],
    ["langages.slice(0, 3).join(', ')", langages.slice(0, 3).join(', ')],
    ['JSON.stringify(medecin)', JSON.stringify(medecin)],
     // two functions in a row: the result of the first is passed to the second
    ['initiales(majusculeInitiale(nom))', initiales(majusculeInitiale(nom))],
  ];

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 820 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 09 - la mise en forme des valeurs</h1>
      <table className="table table-sm align-middle">
        <thead><tr><th>Dans le code</th><th>Affiché</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          {lignes.map(([code, valeur]) => (
            <tr key={code}><td><code>{`{${code}}`}</code></td><td>{valeur}</td></tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h2 className="h6">Object.entries : parcourir les propriétés d'un objet</h2>
      <ul>
        {Object.entries(medecin).map(([cle, valeur]) => (
          <li key={cle}>{cle} = {valeur}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <h2 className="h6">Une fonction maison : horaire</h2>
      <ul>
        {creneaux.map((c) => (
          <li key={horaire(c)}>{horaire(c)} (début : {horaire(c, 'debut')})</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" onClick={() => setMaintenant(new Date())}>Actualiser l'heure</button>
    </div>
  );
}
  • lines 13–17: date formatters, [Intl.DateTimeFormat(langue, options)]: [dateStyle] and [timeStyle] provide predefined formats ([full], [long], [medium], [short]); you can also specify which parts to display ([weekday], [day], [month], [year]). [timeZone: 'UTC']: The date [2026-10-05T00:00:00Z] must remain October 5, regardless of the browser’s time zone;
  • Lines 19–21: number formatters: an amount in euros, a number without decimals, a percentage;
  • lines 39–56: table rows: the code and its value. The last one chains two functions;
  • line 65: the code enclosed in curly braces;
  • lines 72–74: [Object.entries(objet)] returns the [clé, valeur] pairs of an object, which are iterated over using [map];
  • lines 79–81: the custom function [horaire].

The [Intl] generators are created once and for all, outside the component: creating them costs more than using them. The language is hard-coded there ([fr-FR]); Example 21 will show how to follow the language chosen by the user.

docs.title: 9. Interim Conclusion
docs.text:
The twenty-five examples have introduced the concepts we need to write the [RdvMedecins] client:

ConceptUsage in the case studycomponents, props, functions in props, [children]navigation bar, form fields, windows[useState], calculated values, [useEffect]all pages; the calendar based on its URLvalidated fields, server-side validationlogin, doctor and client profiles, account creation, user accountformatting functions, [Intl]formatting of dates, times, and namescustom hooksform submission, CAPTCHAstores [Zustand]logged-in user, messages, confirmation window[React Router] and its guardspages, permissions for each role, session to be restored after F5[i18next]French and English, and the translation of server errors[fetch], httpOnly cookie, proxythe connection, the expired session, all exchanges with the serverthe access layer to API, [TanStack Query]A [rdvmedecins.api.ts] file, one function per route; reading and caching data

The client will be the exact equivalent of the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, page by page. The difference lies elsewhere: the server no longer generates any pages; it responds in JSON, and everything related to display (pages, language, date formatting, messages) has been moved to the browser.

docs.title: 6.1. Example 21: A Bilingual Application
docs.text: [React] does not have a translation system. The most commonly used library is [i18next], which is linked to [React] via [react-i18next].
