    "RETIRER": "Remove one"
  },
  "ERRORS": {
    "LOGIN_TAKEN": "This login is already used by another account.",
    "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS": "Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{minutes}} minute(s)."
  },
  "SERVEUR": {
    "TITRE": "Translating a server response",
    "EXPLICATION": "The RdvMedecins server only sends keys. The client translates them:"
  }
}

Each text has a key consisting of nested names: [ACCUEIL.BONJOUR]. These are the same dictionaries as in previous lessons, with two specific features of [i18next]:

  • parameters are written as [{{nom}}]; a parameter can be formatted according to the language: [{{date, datetime(dateStyle: full)}}] (a date, with the options from [Intl.DateTimeFormat]), [{{prix, currency(EUR)}}] (an amount in euros);
  • plurals: [i18next] automatically selects the form based on the parameter [count] and the language rules: [RENDEZ_VOUS_one] or [RENDEZ_VOUS_other], and [RENDEZ_VOUS_zero] for zero, if it exists. Polish, Arabic, and other languages have different forms ([_few], [_many]), which [i18next] recognizes.

docs.title: 6.1.2. The configuration
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 21-i18n/src/i18n/i18n.ts - i18next configuration
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// i18next is the most widely used translation library in JavaScript;
// react-i18next connects it to React. It is provided with:
//    - a DICTIONNAIRE per language (fr.json, en.json), where each text has a
//      CLÉ ("ACCUEIL.BONJOUR"); parameters are written as {{name}};
//      {{date, datetime(...)}} and {{price, currency(EUR)}} format
//      a date or an amount depending on the language (using API Intl);
//    - the source language (the one stored in localStorage, otherwise the
//      of the browser, otherwise French) and the fallback language.
// In a component, t('ACCUEIL.BONJOUR', { name: 'Marie' }) returns the text
// in the COURANTE language; changing the language reloads the components that
// use t, and the entire page is re-translated.
//
// On the client side, this follows the same principle as the NestJS course (dictionaries
// i18n/*.json + {{t}} helper) — but the translation now takes place within
// the browser, and switching languages no longer requires any server interaction.
// =========================================================================

import i18n from 'i18next';
import { initReactI18next } from 'react-i18next';
import fr from './fr.json';
import en from './en.json';

export type Langue = 'fr' | 'en';
export const LANGUES: Langue[] = ['fr', 'en'];
const CLE_LANGUE = 'exemple21.langue';

function langueDeDepart(): Langue {
  const memorisee = localStorage.getItem(CLE_LANGUE);
  if (memorisee === 'fr' || memorisee === 'en') {
    return memorisee;
  }
  return navigator.language.startsWith('en') ? 'en' : 'fr';
}

// every time the language changes: it is stored, and
// the page’s lang attribute (useful for screen readers and proofreaders)
i18n.on('languageChanged', (langue) => {
  localStorage.setItem(CLE_LANGUE, langue);
  document.documentElement.lang = langue;
});

// use(initReactI18next): i18next notifies React of language changes
i18n.use(initReactI18next).init({
   // Dictionaries are part of the application code: no requests
  resources: { fr: { translation: fr }, en: { translation: en } },
  lng: langueDeDepart(),
  fallbackLng: 'fr', // A key is missing in English: we use the French version
   // React already escapes everything it displays: i18next doesn’t need to do it
  interpolation: { escapeValue: false },
});

export default i18n;
  • lines 23–24: the dictionaries are part of the application code: they are JSON modules, imported as objects ([resolveJsonModule], see [tsconfig.json]);
  • lines 30–36: the source language: the one stored in [localStorage], otherwise the browser’s language, otherwise French;
  • lines 40–43: each time the language changes, it is stored and the page’s [lang] attribute is updated (useful for screen readers and spell-checkers);
  • lines 46–53: configuration: the dictionaries ([translation] is the name of the default key space), the source language, the fallback language (if a key is missing in English, French is used), and [escapeValue: false]: [React] already escapes everything it displays.
// =========================================================================
// 21-i18n/src/main.tsx - importing i18n/i18n.ts is sufficient to configure i18next,
// before the first display
// =========================================================================

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import './i18n/i18n';
import App from './App';

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App />
  </StrictMode>,
);

Importing [i18n/i18n.ts] is sufficient to configure [i18next] before the first display.

docs.title: 6.1.3. The translated page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 21-i18n/src/App.tsx - a translated page
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - const { t, i18n } = useTranslation() : the translation function, and
//      the i18next object (i18n.language: the current language);
//    - t('CLE'                       ) a text string;
//    - t('CLE', { name: ...          }) text with parameters;
//    - t('CLE', { count: n }         ) plural text: i18next selects
//                                      the key CLE_zero, CLE_one, or CLE_other;
//    - i18n.changeLanguage('en'      ) changes the language: the entire page is
//                                      is re-translated.
// =========================================================================

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { LANGUES } from './i18n/i18n';

// what the server would return: RdvMedecins (see the chapter on the black box)
const REPONSES_SERVEUR = [
  { statusCode: 409, cle: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN', params: {} },
  { statusCode: 429, cle: 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', params: { minutes: '15' } },
];

export default function App() {
  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation();
  const [nombre, setNombre] = useState(2);
  const [aujourdhui] = useState(() => new Date());

   // the tab title follows the language
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = t('APP.TITRE');
  }, [t]);

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 720 }}>
      <div className="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
        <h1 className="h3 mb-0">{t('APP.TITRE')}</h1>
        <div className="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label={t('APP.LANGUE')}>
          {LANGUES.map((l) => (
            <button key={l} className={`btn ${i18n.language === l ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-outline-primary'}`}
                    onClick={() => i18n.changeLanguage(l)}>
              {l.toUpperCase()}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="card p-3 mb-3">
        <p>{t('ACCUEIL.BONJOUR', { nom: 'Marie' })}</p>
        {/* the date and amount are formatted by the dictionary in the current language */}
        <p>{t('ACCUEIL.AUJOURDHUI', { date: aujourdhui })}</p>
        <p>{t('ACCUEIL.PRIX', { prix: 1234.5 })}</p>
        {/* count: selects the plural form and replaces {{count}} */}
        <p className="fw-bold">{t('ACCUEIL.RENDEZ_VOUS', { count: nombre })}</p>
        <div className="d-flex gap-2">
          <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" onClick={() => setNombre(nombre + 1)}>{t('ACCUEIL.AJOUTER')}</button>
          <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" disabled={nombre === 0} onClick={() => setNombre(nombre - 1)}>
            {t('ACCUEIL.RETIRER')}
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="card p-3">
        <h2 className="h6">{t('SERVEUR.TITRE')}</h2>
        <p>{t('SERVEUR.EXPLICATION')}</p>
        <ul className="mb-0">
          {REPONSES_SERVEUR.map((r) => (
             // the server key EST a dictionary key; params provides its parameters
            <li key={r.cle}>
              <code>{r.statusCode} {r.cle}</code>
              <br />→ {t(r.cle, r.params)}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • Line 25: the hook for [react-i18next]: [t], the translation function, and [i18n], the [i18next] object ([i18n.language] is the current language). The component is called when the language changes;
  • lines 30–32: the tab title follows the language: the function [t] changes with the language;
  • line 41: change language: the entire page is re-translated without making any requests to the server;
  • line 49: text with parameters;
  • lines 51–52: a date and an amount, formatted by the dictionary in the current language;
  • line 54: a plural form;
  • line 71: the key sent by the server [RdvMedecins] EST a key from the dictionary (see next chapter); [params] provides its parameters.

In English, after removing two appointments:

On the client side, this works on the same principle as the [NestJS] course ([i18n/*.json] dictionaries + [{{t}}] helper); however, translation now takes place in the browser, and changing languages no longer requires any interaction with the server.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The document’s PDF is HERE.

The document’s codes are HERE.

This document is a product of Anthropic’s IA Claude. It follows the course “Step-by-Step Introduction to the NestJS Web Framework,” from which it shifts the perspective:

  • In the course [NestJS], the server generates the pages HTML (view engine [Handlebars]); the browser simply displays them;
  • in this course, the pages are generated in the browser by an application [React]; the server, now reduced to a simple server JSON, provides only data.

The application’s pages, however, remain unchanged: they are those of the [RdvMedecins] application already presented with the other frameworks (login with CAPTCHA, doctor’s schedule, appointment window, patient portal, doctor and client management, account creation, French and English).

This document follows the same structure as its predecessors: first, numerous short examples, each focusing on a specific concept of [React], followed by a complete case study—the [React] client of the [RdvMedecins] application—with all files annotated. It follows the same structure as the courses *Step-by-Step Introduction to the Vue.js Framework* and *Step-by-Step Introduction to the Angular Framework*: Readers familiar with [Vue.js] or [Angular] will find the same examples, written in the style of [React]: 25 examples, numbered like those in the [Angular] course.

A course already exists on this topic: A React Client/Server Example / NestJS (2026), which covers both the server and the client. This document differs from that one in its approach: the server is treated as a black box, and we are only interested in the API and JSON; we learn [React] step by step before tackling the complete client.

docs.title: 1.1. React’s Role in a Web Application
docs.text:
The application has two parts, which communicate with each other only through requests:

  • 1: The [React] application, running in the browser, sends a HTTP request to the server, for example, [GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-10-05];
  • 2: The server responds with data JSON: this doctor’s schedule for that day. It does not generate any pages;
  • 3: Using this data, [React] updates the page displayed in the browser without reloading it.

The following diagram compares the two architectures:

The browser loads only a single, nearly empty page—HTML—upon startup. Everything else is generated by the code [JavaScript]: this is known as a single-page application (SPA, for [Single Page Application]). When the user clicks on an internal link, no page is requested from the server: the router changes the displayed URL and replaces the page’s content.

[React] is a library created by [Facebook] (now [Meta]) and released in 2013. It is currently the most widely used library for building web interfaces. It is based on three concepts:

  • components: the interface is broken down into reusable parts (a navigation bar, a form field, a confirmation window, etc.). A [React] component is a simple [JavaScript] (or [TypeScript]) function that returns what needs to be displayed, written in JSX, a syntax that combines HTML and [JavaScript];
  • State and declarative rendering: a component’s data is stored in its state ([useState]). When the state changes, [React] calls the component’s function, compares the result to the previous one, and automatically updates whatever has changed on the page. We never write code that directly modifies the page: we describe the page based on its state;
  • hooks: functions ([useState], [useEffect], [useContext]...) through which a component accesses the mechanisms of [React]: state, side effects, and shared data. You can write your own hooks to reuse a behavior.

Unlike [Angular], [React] is not an "all-in-one" framework: it is a rendering library. The router, forms, the HTTP client, translation, and shared state are provided by other libraries, chosen by the developer. This course uses the most common ones: [React Router] (the router), [React Hook Form] (an example form library), [TanStack Query] (reading data from the server), [Zustand] (shared state), and [i18next] (languages). The build tool is [Vite].

We will use [React] 19, with its most recent implementation: function components and hooks (the old components written as classes are no longer used), form actions ([useActionState]), [use()] and [<Suspense>], [<title>] placed by a component, [useEffectEvent] and [<Activity>] (React 19.2).

docs.title: 1.2. Tools Used
docs.text:
The examples were written and tested using the following tools (installation instructions are provided in the appendix):

  • [Node.js] 24 (or at least 22.22: this is a requirement of [React Router] 8) and its package manager [npm];
  • the editor [Visual Studio Code], which includes [TypeScript] and JSX without any additional extensions;
  • a recent browser ([Chrome], [Firefox], [Edge]), if possible with the [React Developer Tools] extension;
  • the command-line tool [curl], which displays the raw HTTP responses;
  • the SGBD [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]), for example, the one for [Laragon] under [Windows]: it is required for the JSON server, as described in the chapter introducing it.

The libraries are those of the [package.json] files: [React] 19.3, [React Router] 8.4, [Vite] 8.3, [TypeScript] 6.0, [React Hook Form] 7.89, [TanStack Query] 5.104, [Zustand] 5.0, [i18next] 26 and [react-i18next] 17, [Bootstrap] 5.3.

docs.title: 1.3. Examples
docs.text:
The codes in the document are organized into three folders:

livrable/
├── exemples-react/            les 25 petits exemples de React
├── rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/   le serveur JSON RdvMedecins (la « boîte noire »)
└── rdvmedecins-react/         le client React de l'étude de cas

The examples folder contains twenty-five small applications—one per example—that share the same libraries:

exemples-react/
├── 01-premiere-application/
│   ├── index.html
│   └── src/
├── 02-etat/
├── ...

Install the libraries once, in a console opened to the [exemples-react] folder (in [VS Code]: Terminal menu / New Terminal):

npm install

Then run a sample by entering its name:

npm start 01-premiere-application

The [Vite] development server serves the example on port 5173: open it at http://localhost:5173/. This server does not need to be restarted when you modify a file: each saved file is immediately recompiled, and the browser page updates automatically, usually without even losing its state. Stop it by entering [Ctrl-C] in the console before running the next example (only one example at a time can occupy port 5173).

Examples 22 through 25 query the JSON and [RdvMedecins] servers: you will need to have installed and started them, as explained in the chapter dedicated to them.

docs.title: 4.1. Example 17: The router
docs.text:
An application [React] is a single-page application: the browser loads only the UNE page HTML. When you click on an internal link, no request is sent to the server: the router changes the address displayed by the browser and replaces the displayed component. [React] does not have a router: the [React Router] library ([react-router] package), which is the most widely used, is used instead.

[React Router] can be used in three ways (its “modes”): declarative (using the [<Routes>] and [<Route>] components, the simplest), “data” (routes described by objects, with functions executed before rendering: [loader], [middleware]...), and “framework” (a complete application with server-side rendering, similar to [Next.js]). We use the data mode, which provides the navigation controls we’ll need.

docs.title: 4.1.1. The data
docs.text:

docs.title: 4.1.2. Routes
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 17-router/src/routes.tsx - the ROUTES of the application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A React application is a single-page application (SPA: Single
// Page Application): the browser loads only UNE one page HTML. When you
// click an internal link, no request is sent to the server: the
// router changes the address displayed by the browser and replaces the
// component displayed in <Outlet />.
//
// React does not have a built-in router: the React Router library is used. A
// route associates a CHEMIN with a COMPOSANT (a "page"):
//    'doctors/:id'  :id is a parameter (/doctors/2 -> id = "2");
//    '*            ' any path: the "page not found" page (the
//                    router always chooses the most specific route).
// The routes are IMBRIQUÉES: the root route displays the shell of
// application shell (Shell), and its children are displayed inside it, at
// the location of its <Outlet />.
// =========================================================================

import { redirect, type RouteObject } from 'react-router';
import Coquille from './Coquille';
import Accueil from './pages/Accueil';
import ListeMedecins from './pages/ListeMedecins';
import DetailMedecin from './pages/DetailMedecin';
import Recherche from './pages/Recherche';
import PageIntrouvable from './pages/PageIntrouvable';

export const routes: RouteObject[] = [
  {
    path: '/',
    Component: Coquille,
    children: [
       // index: the route of the parent’s address itself (“/”)
      { index: true, Component: Accueil },
      { path: 'medecins', Component: ListeMedecins },
      { path: 'medecins/:id', Component: DetailMedecin },
      { path: 'recherche', Component: Recherche },
       // loading DIFFÉRÉ: the code for this page is only downloaded on the
       // first visit (Vite actually creates a separate file)
      { path: 'a-propos', lazy: async () => ({ Component: (await import('./pages/APropos')).default }) },
       // A redirect: the old URL leads to the new one. A LOADER
       // is a function that the router calls AVANT to display the route;
       // if it triggers a redirect, the navigation changes its target
      {
        path: 'docteurs',
        loader: () => {
          throw redirect('/medecins');
        },
      },
      { path: '*', Component: PageIntrouvable },
    ],
  },
];
  • Line 20: [RouteObject] is the type of a route; [redirect] creates a redirect;
  • lines 28–53: Routes are objects: a path ([path]) and a component ([Component], capitalized—we specify the component, not [<Accueil />]);
  • lines 30–32: Routes are nested: the root route displays the application’s “shell” ([Coquille]), and its children ([children]) are displayed at the INTÉRIEUR of the shell, at the location of its [<Outlet />]. The paths of the children are relative to that of the parent;
  • line 34: a route index: that of the parent’s address itself (“/”);
  • line 36: [:id] is a parameter: [/medecins/2] displays [DetailMedecin], where [id] = “2”;
  • line 40: deferred loading: the function [lazy] is called only on the first visit to the page. [import('./pages/APropos')] (a “dynamic” import, in the form of a function) then downloads the module, which [Vite] has stored in a separate file. [lazy] returns the missing properties of the route: in this case, its component, which is exported by default by the module;
  • lines 45–49: a redirect: the old address leads to the new one. A loader is a function that the router calls—AVANT—to display the route (to load its data); if it triggers ([throw]) a redirect, the navigation changes its target;
  • line 50: [*] corresponds to any path: the “page not found” page. The router always chooses the most specific route: the order of the routes does not matter.

docs.title: 4.1.3. Startup
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 17-router/src/main.tsx
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// createBrowserRouter (routes) creates the router, which follows the address of the
// browser; <RouterProvider> displays the route that corresponds to the
//. The root component is no longer “App”; it is now the routes.
// =========================================================================

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { createBrowserRouter } from 'react-router';
import { RouterProvider } from 'react-router/dom';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import { routes } from './routes';

const routeur = createBrowserRouter(routes);

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <RouterProvider router={routeur} />
  </StrictMode>,
);
  • line 16: the router, constructed from the routes. [Browser]: it follows the browser’s address via API and [history];
  • line 20: the component that displays the route corresponding to the current address. The root component is no longer [App]: these are the routes. [RouterProvider] is imported from [react-router/dom], the browser-specific part of the library.

docs.title: 4.1.4. The application shell
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 17-router/src/Coquille.tsx - the application’s “shell”
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - <Link to="...">, <NavLink to="...">: an internal link. It produces a
//      valid <a href>, but clicking it does not reload the page: this is the router
//      that handles it. NavLink also knows if it refers to the currently displayed page: it
//      then sets the "active" class (the Bootstrap class);
//    - <Outlet />: the location where the current route ENFANT is displayed;
//    - useLocation(): the current address (pathname, search...).
// =========================================================================

import { NavLink, Outlet, useLocation } from 'react-router';

export default function Coquille() {
  const location = useLocation();
   // decodeURIComponent: %C3%A9 becomes active again
  const adresse = decodeURIComponent(location.pathname + location.search);

  return (
    <div className="container py-4">
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 17 - le routeur</h1>
      <nav className="nav nav-pills mb-3">
        {/* end: "/" is only active on "/" exactly, not on /doctors */}
        <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/" end>Accueil</NavLink>
        <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/medecins">Médecins</NavLink>
        {/* Parameters after the "?": NavLink compares only the path */}
        <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/recherche?q=généraliste">Recherche</NavLink>
        <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/a-propos">À propos</NavLink>
        <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/docteurs">/docteurs (redirection)</NavLink>
        <NavLink className="nav-link" to="/page-inconnue">Lien cassé</NavLink>
      </nav>
      <p className="small text-muted">adresse courante : <code>{adresse}</code></p>
      <div className="card p-3">
        <Outlet />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • line 15: [useLocation()] returns the current address: [pathname] (the path), [search] (the part after the “?”)... The component is called each time the user navigates;
  • Line 24: [<NavLink to="...">] is an internal link. It generates a valid [<a href>] (which can be opened in a new tab), but clicking it does not reload the page: the router handles this. [NavLink] also knows if it refers to the currently displayed page: in that case, it adds the class [active] (the same as [Bootstrap]). [end]: The home page “/” is active only on “/” exactly, and not on [/medecins]; [<Link>] is the simple version, without an active class;
  • line 27: an address with parameters. [NavLink] compares only the path: the link remains active regardless of the search;
  • line 34: the location where the current route ENFANT is displayed.

docs.title: 4.1.5. The pages
docs.text:
The home page:

// React 19: A <title> element written in a component is placed by React
// in the page’s <head>; it changes the tab title as long as the
// component is displayed
export default function Accueil() {
  return (
    <>
      <title>Accueil</title>
      <p className="mb-0">
        Bienvenue. Cliquez sur les liens : l'adresse du navigateur change, la page n'est jamais rechargée (ouvrez
        l'onglet Réseau des outils de développement pour le vérifier). Les boutons Précédent et Suivant du navigateur
        fonctionnent, ainsi que le rechargement (F5) de n'importe quelle page.
      </p>
    </>
  );
}
  • line 7: [React] places any element written in a component into the page’s [<head>], as long as the component is displayed: Each page thus sets the tab title (you can do the same with [<meta>] and [<link>]).

The list of doctors, with parameterized links:

// 17-router/src/pages/ListeMedecins.tsx - links with parameters
import { Link } from 'react-router';
import { MEDECINS } from '../donnees';

export default function ListeMedecins() {
  return (
    <>
      <title>Médecins</title>
      <ul className="mb-0">
        {MEDECINS.map((m) => (
           // a string template generates the URL /doctors/2
          <li key={m.id}>
            <Link to={`/medecins/${m.id}`}>{m.titre} {m.prenom} {m.nom}</Link>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </>
  );
}

A string template generates the address [/medecins/2].

A doctor’s profile:

// =========================================================================
// 17-router/src/pages/DetailMedecin.tsx - a page with a parameter
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// useParams(): path parameters, here { id: "2" } - always
// CHAÎNES. useNavigate(): a function for navigating PAR LE CODE;
// navigate(-1) returns to the previous page, just like the Back button.
// If you navigate from /doctors/1 to /doctors/2, React RÉUTILISE uses the same
// component: it is simply re-rendered with a different ID.
// =========================================================================

import { useNavigate, useParams } from 'react-router';
import { MEDECINS } from '../donnees';

export default function DetailMedecin() {
  const { id } = useParams();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const medecin = MEDECINS.find((m) => m.id === Number(id));

  if (!medecin) {
    return <p className="text-danger mb-0">Le médecin n° {id} n'existe pas.</p>;
  }

  const suivant = (medecin.id % MEDECINS.length) + 1;
  return (
    <>
      <title>{`${medecin.prenom} ${medecin.nom}`}</title>
      <h2 className="h5">{medecin.titre} {medecin.prenom} {medecin.nom}</h2>
      <p>Spécialité : {medecin.specialite}</p>
      <div className="d-flex gap-2">
        <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" onClick={() => navigate(-1)}>Retour</button>
        <button className="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" onClick={() => navigate(`/medecins/${suivant}`)}>Médecin suivant</button>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
  • Line 15: [useParams()] provides the path parameters—in this case, [{ id: "2" }]—always in string format;
  • line 16: a function for navigating by code;
  • lines 19–21: an unknown doctor ([/medecins/9]): a message;
  • line 26: a calculated title: [<title>] only accepts the string UNE, hence the template;
  • line 30: [navigate(-1)] returns to the previous page, like the browser’s Back button;
  • line 31: navigate to an address. Going from [/medecins/1] to [/medecins/2] does not recreate the component: [React] simply reloads it, with a different [id].

The search:

// =========================================================================
// 17-router/src/pages/Recherche.tsx - a page driven by the URL
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// /search?q=pediatrician: as with the GET form from the NestJS course, the
// page is fully described by its address: you can bookmark it
// bookmark, reload it, or go back. useSearchParams() provides the
// parameters after the ?.
// <Form> (from React Router) is a GET... form without reloading: the
// router navigates to /search?q=<input>. The page displays what
// the URL says, and nothing else.
// =========================================================================

import { Form, useSearchParams } from 'react-router';
import { MEDECINS } from '../donnees';

export default function Recherche() {
  const [parametres] = useSearchParams();
  const q = parametres.get('q') ?? ''; // is null if absent
  const resultats = MEDECINS.filter((m) => `${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${m.specialite}`.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase()));

  return (
    <>
      <title>Recherche</title>
      <Form className="d-flex gap-2 mb-3" action="/recherche">
        {/* a validated NON field, which starts with the value of URL;
            key={q} : si l'URL change (bouton Précédent), React recrée le
            champ, qui reprend alors la nouvelle valeur de l'URL */}
        <input key={q} name="q" className="form-control" placeholder="nom ou spécialité" defaultValue={q} />
        <button className="btn btn-primary">Rechercher</button>
      </Form>
      <ul className="mb-0">
        {resultats.map((m) => (
          <li key={m.id}>{m.prenom} {m.nom} ({m.specialite})</li>
        ))}
        {resultats.length === 0 && <li className="text-muted">Aucun résultat.</li>}
      </ul>
    </>
  );
}
  • Line 17: the parameters after the “?”, in the form of an object [URLSearchParams]: [parametres.get('q')] is equal to [null] if [q] is absent. [useSearchParams] also returns (as the second element) a function to change them;
  • line 24: [<Form>] (from [React Router]) is a GET form... without reloading: upon submission, the router navigates to [/recherche?q=<saisie>] ([q] being the [name] for the field). As with the GET form from the [NestJS] course, the page is fully described by its address: you can bookmark it, reload it, or go back;
  • Line 28: The field is not validated; it starts with the value of the URL ([defaultValue]). If the URL changes without the page being reloaded (using the Back button), the field would retain its previous text; [key={q}] resolves this issue. When an element’s key changes, [React] treats it as a AUTRE element: it destroys the old one and creates a new one, which starts with the new default value. This is a common trick for “resetting” a component.

The on-demand page and the "page not found" page:

// 17-router/src/pages/APropos.tsx - a page loaded on demand
// "export default": the route finds it via (await import(...)).default
export default function APropos() {
  return (
    <>
      <title>À propos</title>
      <p className="mb-0">
        Cette page a été téléchargée à la première visite (onglet Réseau : un fichier APropos-XXXX.js en production).
        Son titre d'onglet vient de l'élément title qu'elle contient.
      </p>
    </>
  );
}

import { useLocation } from 'react-router';

export default function PageIntrouvable() {
  const { pathname } = useLocation();
  return (
    <>
      <title>Page introuvable</title>
      <p className="text-danger mb-0">Aucune page à l'adresse <code>{pathname}</code>.</p>
    </>
  );
}

docs.title: 4.2. Example 18: Navigation Controls
docs.text: Some pages require the user to be logged in or to have a specific role. The router can verify this before displaying them, using middleware.

docs.title: 4.2.1. The session
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 18-guards/src/session.ts - a session SIMULÉE (without a server)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user must be recognized by COMPOSANTS (the top bar,
// the calendar page) and by GARDES (the router’s functions, which are
// components and therefore cannot read a context). We store it
// in a simple, hand-coded module, a “store”:
//    - a private variable, the state;
//    - functions to read and modify it;
//    - `subscribe`: the list of functions to be notified when it changes.
// A component subscribes to it using useSyncExternalStore (see useSession): it
// is called when the state changes. Example 20 will delegate this task to a
// library, Zustand. (Example 23 will do the same thing with a real
// server.)
// =========================================================================

import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  role: Role;
}

// three "hard-coded" accounts (password = login)
const COMPTES: Record<string, Role> = { admin: 'ADMIN', pelissier: 'DOCTOR', martin: 'USER' };

let utilisateur: Utilisateur | null = null; // the status
const abonnes = new Set<() => void>();

function changer(u: Utilisateur | null) {
  utilisateur = u;
  abonnes.forEach((prevenir) => prevenir());
}

export const session = {
  utilisateur: () => utilisateur,
  connecter(login: string, password: string): boolean {
    const role = Object.hasOwn(COMPTES, login) ? COMPTES[login] : undefined;
    if (role === undefined || password !== login) {
      return false;
    }
    changer({ login, role });
    return true;
  },
  deconnecter: () => changer(null),
  subscribe(prevenir: () => void) {
    abonnes.add(prevenir);
    return () => abonnes.delete(prevenir); // to unsubscribe
  },
};

// the component hook: the logged-in user, always up to date
export function useSession(): Utilisateur | null {
  return useSyncExternalStore(session.subscribe, session.utilisateur);
}

The logged-in user must be known to the components (the top bar, the calendar page) and to the guards—router functions that are not components and therefore cannot read a context. It is stored in a simple, hand-written module, a store ([store]):

  • lines 29–30: the state, a private variable of the module, and the list of functions to notify when it changes;
  • lines 32–35: change the state and notify subscribers;
  • lines 37–52: the public functions: read the user, log in (three hard-coded accounts, password = login), log out, and subscribe ([subscribe] refers to the function that unsubscribes);
  • lines 55–57: the component hook. [useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, lire)] is the hook for [React] designed for this purpose: it subscribes the component to the store and calls it back when the read value changes.

Example 20 will delegate this task to a library.

docs.title: 4.2.2. The guards
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 18-guards/src/gardes.ts - navigation GARDES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A React Router MIDDLEWARE is a function called by the router
// AVANT to display a route that declares it (middleware: [...]), to CHAQUE
// navigation to it. It can:
//    - do nothing: navigation continues;
//    - throw a redirect, redirect('/address'): the
//      navigation is replaced by navigation to that address.
// It receives the navigation request (request.url: the requested address).
//
// This is the client-side equivalent of the NestJS (JwtAuthGuard,
// RolesGuard) — with one difference: FONDAMENTALE: a client key is
// merely a convenience. The client code is in the hands of the user, who
// can change it at will. True data protection remains that
// that provided by SERVEUR (see the chapter on the black box).
// =========================================================================

import { redirect, type MiddlewareFunction } from 'react-router';
import { session, type Role } from './session';

// the requested address, without the machine: "/agenda?x=1"
function adresse(request: Request): string {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  return url.pathname + url.search;
}

// the page requires you to be logged in
export const connexionRequise: MiddlewareFunction = ({ request }) => {
  if (session.utilisateur() === null) {
     // not logged in: redirects to the login page, while remembering where you wanted to go
    throw redirect(`/connexion?redirect=${encodeURIComponent(adresse(request))}`);
  }
};

// the page requires one of the specified roles: a function that FABRIQUE retains it
export function roleRequis(...roles: Role[]): MiddlewareFunction {
  return ({ request }) => {
    const u = session.utilisateur();
    if (u === null || !roles.includes(u.role)) {
       // logged in, but not with the correct role: redirect to the home page, with an explanation
      throw redirect(`/?refus=${encodeURIComponent(adresse(request))}`);
    }
  };
}

A middleware component [React Router] is a function that the router calls—AVANT—to display a route that declares it, and CHAQUE to navigate to it. It can do nothing (navigation continues), or trigger a redirection, which replaces the navigation.

  • Lines 23–26: It receives the navigation request: [request.url] is the full requested address ([http://localhost:5173/agenda?x=1]); only the path and parameters are retained;
  • lines 29–34: not logged in: redirects to the login page, while retaining the intended destination ([?redirect=...]);
  • lines 37–45: a function that returns FABRIQUE, a token, for the given roles; [...roles]: any number of arguments, grouped into an array. Logged in, but not with the correct role: redirect to the home page, with a reason.

This is the client-side equivalent of the [NestJS] guards ([JwtAuthGuard], [RolesGuard]), with one difference: a client-side guard is merely a convenience. The client code is in the user’s hands, and the user can modify it at will. True data protection remains that provided by SERVEUR (see the chapter on the black box).

docs.title: 4.2.3. Protected Routes
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 18-guards/src/routes.tsx - routes PROTÉGÉES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// middleware: the guards to pass through, in order. A page loaded at the
// (lazy) request is downloaded only after the checkpoints have been passed.
// =========================================================================

import { redirect, type RouteObject } from 'react-router';
import Coquille from './Coquille';
import Accueil from './pages/Accueil';
import Connexion from './pages/Connexion';
import Agenda from './pages/Agenda';
import { connexionRequise, roleRequis } from './gardes';

export const routes: RouteObject[] = [
  {
    path: '/',
    Component: Coquille,
    children: [
      { index: true, Component: Accueil },
      { path: 'connexion', Component: Connexion },
      { path: 'agenda', Component: Agenda, middleware: [connexionRequise] },
      {
        path: 'administration',
        middleware: [connexionRequise, roleRequis('ADMIN')],
        lazy: async () => ({ Component: (await import('./pages/Administration')).default }),
      },
       // any other address: return to the home page
      { path: '*', loader: () => redirect('/') },
    ],
  },
];
  • line 22: the route’s safeguards, executed in order;
  • lines 24–26: a page loaded on demand is downloaded only after the guards have been passed;
  • line 29: any other address: return to the home page. A loader can also RENVOYER handle the redirection.

The startup code is the same as in Example 17:

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { createBrowserRouter } from 'react-router';
import { RouterProvider } from 'react-router/dom';
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import { routes } from './routes';

const routeur = createBrowserRouter(routes);

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <RouterProvider router={routeur} />
  </StrictMode>,
);

docs.text:
// 18-gardes/src/Coquille.tsx - links, and the logged-in user
import { NavLink, Outlet, useNavigate } from 'react-router';
import { session, useSession } from './session';

// NavLink accepts a FONCTION for className: she receives { isActive }
const classe = ({ isActive }: { isActive: boolean }) => (isActive ? 'fw-bold' : '');

export default function Coquille() {
  const utilisateur = useSession();
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  function seDeconnecter() {
    session.deconnecter();
    navigate('/');
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-4" style={{ maxWidth: 720 }}>
      <h1 className="h3 mb-3">Exemple 18 - les gardes de navigation</h1>
      <nav className="d-flex gap-3 align-items-center mb-3">
        <NavLink to="/" end className={classe}>Accueil</NavLink>
        <NavLink to="/agenda" className={classe}>Agenda (connecté)</NavLink>
        <NavLink to="/administration" className={classe}>Administration (ADMIN)</NavLink>
        <span className="ms-auto">
          {utilisateur ? (
            <>
              {utilisateur.login} <span className="badge text-bg-primary">{utilisateur.role}</span>
              <button className="btn btn-sm btn-link" onClick={seDeconnecter}>déconnexion</button>
            </>
          ) : (
            <NavLink to="/connexion">connexion</NavLink>
          )}
        </span>
      </nav>
      <div className="card p-3"><Outlet /></div>
    </div>
  );
}
  • Line 6: [className] from a [NavLink] can be a function that takes [{ isActive }] as input and returns the classes;
  • Line 9: the logged-in user; the bar tracks their changes;
  • Lines 12–15: Logout and return to the home page.
import { useSearchParams } from 'react-router';

export default function Accueil() {
   // ?refus=... : submitted by the guard roleRequis when the role is not appropriate
  const refus = useSearchParams()[0].get('refus');
  return (
    <>
      {refus && <p className="alert alert-danger">Votre rôle ne permet pas d'ouvrir {refus}.</p>}
      <p className="mb-0">
        Page publique. Essayez les deux autres liens, connecté ou non (admin, pelissier, martin - mot de passe = login).
      </p>
    </>
  );
}

import { useSession } from '../session';

export default function Agenda() {
  const utilisateur = useSession();
  return (
    <p className="mb-0">
      L'agenda de <strong>{utilisateur?.login}</strong> : cette page exige d'être connecté.
    </p>
  );
}

export default function Administration() {
  return (
    <p className="mb-0">
      Administration : page réservée au rôle ADMIN, chargée à la demande (onglet Réseau : son fichier n'est téléchargé
      qu'à la première visite, et seulement si les gardes l'ont permis).
    </p>
  );
}

// =========================================================================
// 18-guards/src/pages/Connexion.tsx
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// After logging in, the user is redirected to the page they wanted
// to open (with the ?redirect=... parameter set by the guard), or to the home page.
// =========================================================================

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import { useNavigate, useSearchParams } from 'react-router';
import { session } from '../session';

export default function Connexion() {
  const redirection = useSearchParams()[0].get('redirect');
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const [login, setLogin] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const [erreur, setErreur] = useState(false);

  function valider(e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (!session.connecter(login.trim(), password)) {
      setErreur(true);
      return;
    }
     // Only one path is accepted: INTERNE—it starts with /, but not with //
     // (//site.com/... refers to a AUTRE site) - no redirection to another site
    const interne = redirection !== null && redirection.startsWith('/') && !redirection.startsWith('//');
    navigate(interne ? redirection : '/');
  }

  return (
    <>
      {redirection && <p className="alert alert-warning">Connectez-vous pour ouvrir {redirection}.</p>}
      <form className="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2" onSubmit={valider}>
        <input className="form-control w-auto" placeholder="login" autoComplete="username" value={login}
               onChange={(e) => setLogin(e.target.value)} />
        <input type="password" className="form-control w-auto" placeholder="mot de passe" autoComplete="current-password"
               value={password} onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)} />
        <button className="btn btn-primary">Se connecter</button>
      </form>
      {erreur && <p className="text-danger mt-2 mb-0">Login ou mot de passe incorrect.</p>}
    </>
  );
}
  • Line 13: the address we wanted to open, handed over by the guard;
  • lines 27–28: after logging in, we go there... provided it is a INTERNE path (it starts with “/”, but not with “//”, which refers to another site): a booby-trapped login URL ([/connexion?redirect=https://site-malveillant.fr]) must not lead outside the application.

docs.title: 7. The RdvMedecins server, a black box
docs.text:
Examples 22 through 25, followed by the case study, interact with a server: the JSON server of the [RdvMedecins] application. This is the [NestJS] server from the previous lesson, whose controllers no longer generate HTML pages but instead produce JSON responses. Its business and data access layers remain unchanged.

In this course, this server is a black box: we don’t need to know how it’s written. All that matters is its API—that is, the list of HTTP requests it accepts and the responses it returns. This is the typical situation for a client developer: the API is a contract, and the server team can change whatever they want behind that contract. Its source code is provided ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder) and extensively commented, for the curious reader.

This chapter explains how to install the server, describes its API, and queries it using [curl].

docs.title: 7.1. The RdvMedecins Application
docs.text:
The application manages appointments for a medical practice. It has three roles:

RoleWhoWhat they can do[ADMIN]The administrator ([admin])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; manage doctors and clients[DOCTOR]Doctors ([pelissier], [tatou], [dupont])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; view all names in the calendars[USER]Patients ([martin], [durand], [bistrou], [german])book appointments for themselves; cancel their appointments; manage their accounts. In a calendar, they cannot see the names of other patients

Demo accounts use their login as the password. The management rules are verified by the server, regardless of the client:

  • no appointments in the past;
  • only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • a time slot can only be booked once per day;
  • two doctors (or two clients) cannot have the same first and last names; a login belongs to only one account;
  • a doctor with appointments cannot be deleted;
  • A record that has been modified in the meantime by someone else cannot be overwritten (optimistic lock);
  • a patient is never assigned the name of another patient.

docs.title: 7.2. Installation
docs.text:
You will need [Node.js] and a [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]) server: their installation is described in the appendix.

1. The database. The script [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] creates the database [dbrdvmedecins2], its tables, and its sample data. Using [Laragon], run it from within [HeidiSQL] (File menu / Run SQL); at the command line:

mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql

The script always starts with an empty database: you can rerun it to restore the initial data.

2. Libraries. In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder:

npm install

3. Configuration. Copy the file [.env.example] to [.env] (under [Windows]: [copy .env.example .env]), then modify it:

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample configuration file.
# Copy this file to [.env], then adjust the values for your machine.
# The [.env] file must never be shared or committed (passwords).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# listening port for the JSON server (the React client connects to it via the Vite proxy)
PORT=8080

# Database connection settings for MySQL [dbrdvmedecins2]
# (script: database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql)
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3306
DB_USERNAME=root
DB_PASSWORD=
DB_DATABASE=dbrdvmedecins2
# true: displays in the console the SQL queries sent to MySQL
DB_LOGGING=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# authentication
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# secret key used to sign/verify JWT tokens—must be changed
# mandatory in production (a long random string, never committed).
JWT_SECRET=change-moi-en-une-longue-chaine-aleatoire
# Validity period of a JWT token, in seconds (7200 s = 2 h). The cookie
# that carries the token has the same lifetime.
JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS=7200
# Set to true in production (site served as HTTPS): the
# will then never be sent over an unencrypted connection.
COOKIE_SECURE=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# protection against bots
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# login: number of failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or password) allowed for
# the same login from the same address IP, before this combination is blocked...
LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS=5
# ... during this period (an address IP is also blocked if it accumulates
# 5 times as many failed attempts, across all logins)
LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES=15
# customer account creation: maximum number of accounts created per hour
# from the same IP address. In a classroom, all workstations log out
# from the same IP address: increase if necessary.
INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE=10

# MODE TEST Captcha: if this variable has a value, that value is
# accepted as the answer to the N'IMPORTE QUEL CAPTCHA. Useful for querying
# the API using curl (you can't "read" the image in a console).
# Leave VIDE in production.
CAPTCHA_TEST=

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# production
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compiled React client directory, served by this server (default: client/)
# DOSSIER_CLIENT=client
# set to true if the server is behind a proxy (nginx...)
TRUST_PROXY=false
  • line 8: the server listens on port 8080;
  • lines 12–16: the connection to [MySQL]. With [Laragon], the user [root] has no password: the default values are fine;
  • line 25: the secret key that signs the authentication tokens;
  • lines 38–45: anti-bot protections (lockout after multiple failed login attempts, number of accounts created per hour);
  • Line 51: Captcha test mode. The login page asks you to type the characters from an image, which is impossible from a console. If this variable has a value, that value is accepted as the answer to any CAPTCHA, just like the “test keys” that [Google] provides for its [reCAPTCHA]. For the tests with [curl] in this chapter, enter [CAPTCHA_TEST=test]. Leave it as VIDE in production;
  • lines 57–59: two settings for production (see the “Deployment” chapter).

4. Launch.

npm run start:dev

The console displays (excerpt):

[Nest] LOG [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] AgendaController {/api/agenda}:
[Nest] LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/api/agenda, GET} route
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] RendezVousController {/api/rendez-vous}:
...
[Nest] WARN [RdvMedecins] MODE TEST du captcha actif (CAPTCHA_TEST dans .env) : à ne jamais utiliser en production
[Nest] LOG [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] serveur JSON démarré : http://localhost:8080/api

If the database is inaccessible ([MySQL] server stopped, incorrect password), the server stops immediately with a connection error message.

docs.title: 7.3. Response Format
docs.text:
All URLs begin with [/api]. A successful request receives a 2xx status code and, in its body, the requested data in the format JSON. A rejected request receives a 4xx or 5xx code and, in the body, TOUJOURS, which has the same format:

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": { "min": "6" },
  "champs": { "nom": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", "password": "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT" }
}
  • [statusCode]: the code HTTP, repeated in the body;
  • [cle]: the message translation key. The server never returns text to be displayed: it no longer knows the user’s language. It is the client that translates the key using its dictionaries (see Example 21);
  • [params] (optional): the message parameters ([Au moins {min} caractères], [Réessayez dans {minutes} minute(s)]);
  • [champs] (optional): for a rejected form, the error for each field.

Codes used:

CodeMeaningExamples of keys400Invalid request[ERRORS.INVALID_FORM] (+ fields), [ERRORS.INVALID_DATE], [ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA], [ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT], [ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD], [ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST]...401not authenticated[ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED] (no token), [ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED] (invalid or expired token), [LOGIN.ERROR]403Access Denied[ERRORS.FORBIDDEN] (insufficient role), [ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT] (no pass)404Not found[ERRORS.NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND]...409Business rule violation[ERRORS.PAST_DATE], [ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED], [ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN], [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE]...415POST, which is not in JSON[ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED]429Too many attempts[ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS], [ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS] (+ params.minutes)500server error[ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR]

docs.title: 7.4. Authentication
docs.text:
The client authenticates using [POST /api/auth/login], with a username, password, and CAPTCHA response. In return, the server places a cookie in the browser that contains a signed token JWT:

Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

Its attributes are important for security:

  • [HttpOnly]: The page's code [JavaScript] cannot read this cookie. A malicious script that might have been injected into the page would therefore be unable to steal the token. Consequence for the client: it cannot determine on its own whether it is logged in. It asks the server ([GET /api/auth/moi]);
  • [Path=/api]: the browser only includes it in requests to the API;
  • [SameSite=Strict]: The browser only includes this token in requests sent to DEPUIS for a page on this site. A malicious page on another site cannot cause the browser to act on the user’s behalf (a so-called CSRF attack);
  • [Max-Age=7200]: It expires after two hours, at the same time the token expires.

The browser then automatically sends this cookie with every request to [/api]. The client [React] therefore does not need to do anything to authenticate itself, provided that its pages and the API share the same origin (same protocol, same machine, same port). This is the role of the development server’s proxy, [Vite] (see Example 22), and of the server itself in production (see the “Deployment” chapter).

A second safeguard against CSRF attacks: the server rejects (415) any POST request whose body is not in JSON. A compromised HTML form on another site cannot send JSON.

docs.title: 7.5. The API
docs.text:
MethodAddressRolesSent/response bodyGET[/api/captcha]publicResponse: [{ id, svg }]POST[/api/auth/login]public[{ login, password, captchaId, captcha }]; response: [{ login, nom, role }] + cookiePOST[/api/auth/logout]public[{}] ; deletes the cookieGET[/api/auth/moi]logged inresponse: [{ login, nom, role }]GET[/api/agenda?idMedecin=&jour=]allAnswer: the calendar (excluding idMedecin: for a DOCTOR, his own)POST[/api/rendez-vous]all[{ jour, idCreneau, idClient }] (idClient ignored for a USER); 201DELETE[/api/rendez-vous/:id]allA USER cancels only its ownGET[/api/medecins]allthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/clients]ADMIN, DOCTORthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINa recordPOST[/api/medecins], [/api/clients]ADMIN[{ titre, prenom, nom, login?, password? }]; 201PUT[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMIN[{ titre, prenom, nom, login?, password?, version }]DELETE[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINAnswer: [{}]POST[/api/inscription/acces]public[{ captchaId, captcha }]; issues a token (cookie)GET[/api/inscription/acces]publicresponse: [{ valide }]POST[/api/inscription]public + pass[{ titre, prenom, nom, login, password, confirmation }]; 201GET[/api/mon-espace]USERresponse: [{ patient, rendezVous }]GET[/api/mon-compte]USERResponse: [{ titre, prenom, nom, login, version }]PUT[/api/mon-compte]USER[{ titre, prenom, nom, login, password?, confirmation?, motDePasseActuel, version }]DELETE[/api/mon-compte]USER[{ motDePasseActuel }]; deletes the account and its appointments

A calendar entry ([GET /api/agenda]) describes a time slot (ET) and what the logged-in user is authorized to do with it:

{ "id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0,
  "libre": false,
  "patient": { "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND" },
  "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2 }
  • [libre]: Is the time slot available on that day?
  • [patient]: the patient for the appointment. For a logged-in patient, this is equal to [null], except for SON (appointment): the names of other patients are never sent;
  • [moi]: This is the logged-in patient’s appointment;
  • [reservable]: Can the user book this time slot (available, not in the past, and, for a patient, no upcoming appointments)?
  • [idRv]: filled in if the user can cancel this appointment.

The server handles DÉCIDE; the client displays it. And even if a client were to cheat (by displaying a “Book” button when it shouldn’t), the server would double-check everything at the time of booking.

docs.title: 7.6. Querying the API with curl
docs.text:
The [curl] folder on the server contains the JSON bodies of the requests in this chapter, one file per request. For example, [curl/login-admin.json]:

{ "login": "admin", "password": "admin", "captchaId": "-", "captcha": "test" }

Commands are entered in a console opened in the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] directory. Some options for [curl]:

  • [-i]: also display the response headers; [-s]: without a progress bar;
  • [--json @fichier]: send the contents of the file in POST, with the header [Content-Type: application/json] (curl 7.82 and later; with an older version, use [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier]);
  • [-X PUT], [-X DELETE]: the HTTP method;
  • [-c cookies.txt]: save the received cookies to this file; [-b cookies.txt]: send them back. This is how [curl] “stays logged in” from one command to the next, just as a browser would.

Under [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe] and not [curl] (which refers to a different command there). The somewhat lengthy responses for JSON have been formatted for this document, and the headers for [Date], [ETag], [Connection], and [Keep-Alive] have been removed.

docs.title: 7.6.1. Login
docs.text:
First, the CAPTCHA (the image is cropped):

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/captcha
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: no-store
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 11397

{"id": "9931064f-dcc3-45f7-a35c-3057d208a1d4", "svg": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"150..."}

Without a token, a protected URL returns a 401 response:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

An incorrect CAPTCHA, followed by an incorrect password:

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-mauvais-captcha.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 91

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA", "champs": {"captcha": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA"}}

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-mauvais-mdp.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 38

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "LOGIN.ERROR"}

A successful login sets the cookie, which [curl] stores in [cookies.txt]:

$ curl -i -c cookies.txt --json @curl/login-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "nom": "Administrateur", "role": "ADMIN"}

With this cookie, the server knows who we are:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "nom": "Administrateur", "role": "ADMIN"}

A forged (or expired) token results in an expired session, and the server instructs the browser to delete the cookie:

$ curl -i -b "rdvmedecins_jwt=abc.def.ghi" http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 49

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/doctors

docs.title: 7.6.6. Managing doctors and clients (ADMIN)
docs.text:
An addition. If the username is missing, the default is the name in lowercase; the password is the username:

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-ajout.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 82

{"id": 4, "version": 1, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY", "login": "leroy"}

Invalid body: the response lists the error for each field:

{ "titre": "Dr", "prenom": "", "nom": "UN-NOM-BIEN-TROP-LONG-POUR-LA-BASE", "login": "Claire L" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-invalide.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 210

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": {"min": "6"},
  "champs": {"login": "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN", "titre": "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE", "prenom": "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED", "nom": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG"}
}

A homonym: both affected fields are flagged:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-doublon.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 143

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "champs": {"prenom": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "nom": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS"}}

A modification. The [version] is the one read from the record (here, 1):

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY-MARTIN", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/medecin-modif.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 89

{"id": 4, "version": 2, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY-MARTIN", "login": "leroy"}

The record is now at version 2. Resubmitting the same change (with version 1) would overwrite a record that has since been modified by someone else: the optimistic lock prevents this:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/medecin-modif.json http://localhost:8080/api/medecins/4
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 51

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE"}

A doctor with appointments cannot be deleted; the others can:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/1
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 57

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 7.6.7. Creating an account
docs.text:
Without a pass, it’s impossible:

$ curl -i --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

First, you solve a CAPTCHA; the server issues a token, valid for 15 minutes, in a cookie:

$ curl -i -c cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/captcha-test.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration/access
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_inscription=1c3352aa-26ba-4f85-9f61-ed2c6a731d84; Max-Age=900; Path=/api/inscription; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:04:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -b cookies-inscription.txt http://localhost:8080/api/registration/access
{"valide": true}

The password confirmation must be identical:

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription-confirmation.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 98

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM", "champs": {"confirmation": "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"}}

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "password": "secret1", "confirmation": "secret1" }

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt -c cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_inscription=; Path=/api/inscription; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 20

{"login": "jbernard"}

The passcode has been used: it cannot be used to create a second account:

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

docs.title: 7.6.8. Manage Your Account
docs.text:
The new patient logs in and reads her medical record:

$ curl -s -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
{"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "version": 1}

Any changes require the current password. The server issues a new token, which contains the new name:

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD-DUVAL", "login": "jbernard", "motDePasseActuel": "secret1", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X PUT --json @curl/mon-compte.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:13 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 62

{"login": "jbernard", "nom": "Julie BERNARD-DUVAL", "role": "USER"}

Deleting the account also deletes the cookie:

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X DELETE --json @curl/mon-compte-suppression.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 7.6.9. Some errors
docs.text:
An unknown route, a body that is not a valid JSON:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/does-not-exist
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 404, "cle": "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{pas du json" http://localhost:8080/api/appointment
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 45

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST"}

We now know everything we need to know about the server to write our client.
